headline: Jailed Brazil Beach Soccer Star Drawn Into Russia-US Spy Dispute
content: A Brazilian beach soccer star has become an unlikely bargaining chip in a dispute over an alleged Russian spy who has been sought by both Moscow and Washington.The Russian government is seeking a prisoner swap involving Letícia “Lelê” Villar, a Brazilian player jailed since July 2025 for bringing hashish into Russia, for Sergey Cherkasov, an alleged spy serving a five-year sentence in Brazil for using false documents, according to an official who asked not to be identified discussing private matters.Cherkasov was arrested in Brazil in 2022 after after Dutch authorities denied him entry as he sought to take up an internship at the International Criminal Court using a false Brazilian identity. In 2023, the US government charged Cherkasov, who had previously used his Brazilian passport to move to the US to pursue graduate studies at Johns Hopkins University, with acting as an agent of a Russian intelligence service and later requested his extradition.Brazilian police found no evidence that Cherkasov, who used the alias Victor Muller Ferreira, spied on the Brazilian government, companies or institutions. Brazil rejected a US request to extradite Cherkasov after its Supreme Court had approved his eventual transfer to Russia, subject to the completion of proceedings against him in Brazil. In July, the government separately ordered him expelled once he completes his Brazilian sentence or is released by the judiciary. Villar, meanwhile, has appealed directly to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for help securing her release. In a letter to Lula this month, she said “there are no words that can express or convey all the suffering, burden and pain I feel being in this place.”Brazil’s foreign affairs ministry said it has been following the situation and has been providing consular assistance to her and her family. The Justice Ministry said it doesn’t comment on ongoing cases. The Russian Embassy in Brazil and Villar’s lawyer didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.Villar, who has played for Brazil’s national team and won multiple international titles at the club level, isn’t the first prominent athlete whose detention in Russia has become entangled in a prisoner exchange. American basketball star Brittney Griner was released in a one-for-one swap in 2022 for Russian arms dealer Viktor Bout. Griner had been sentenced to nine years in prison after customs officials found vape cartridges containing cannabis oil in her luggage at a Moscow airport.Lula has cultivated a pragmatic and at times warm relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin, potentially giving Brazil room to navigate the dispute. headline: Telangana targets overseas jobs for 7,000 unemployed youth, to offer 50% subsidy on eligible expenses
content: Hyderabad: Telangana govt is targeting overseas jobs for 7,000 unemployed youth in 2026-27, offering a 50% subsidy on eligible expenses ranging from skill and foreign language training to visas and air travel. The assistance will be capped at Rs 50,000 for those directly securing jobs abroad and Rs 1.75 lakh for those requiring foreign language proficiency.Though the chief minister’s Overseas Employment Scheme was announced a few months ago, the govt has now issued guidelines for its implementation. Telangana youth from economically weaker families, aged between 18 and 40, will be eligible, subject to prescribed conditions.The scheme will be implemented by Telangana Overseas Manpower Company Limited (TOMCOM), officials said.“In the 2026-27 financial year, the state govt aims to provide financial assistance to 7,000 individuals across the state through this scheme. Financial aid will be given to 5,880 candidates going directly for overseas jobs and 1,120 candidates going for jobs requiring foreign language proficiency. Categories will be determined based on the candidates’ interests, educational qualifications, vocational skills, and overseas job opportunities,” the govt said.The scheme seeks to address barriers that prevent skilled workers and those with vocational qualifications from taking up overseas jobs, including lack of awareness and requisite skills and the high cost of going abroad. TOMCOM will facilitate foreign-language training, upskilling to international standards and job certifications, besides helping candidates secure overseas employment safely and legally.Two categories of subsidyUnder the guidelines, beneficiaries have been divided into two categories. Candidates securing overseas jobs that do not require special foreign language training or examinations fall under the first. Eligible visa and air travel expenditure will be capped at Rs 1 lakh, with the govt bearing 50%, subject to a maximum subsidy of Rs 50,000.The second category covers jobs requiring proficiency in the destination country’s language. Eligible expenditure will be capped at Rs 3.50 lakh, with a 50% subsidy of up to Rs 1.75 lakh.Candidates in both categories must meet the remaining 50% of the expenditure. Those unable to raise the money can seek bank loans, with TOMCOM coordinating with nationalised banks to formulate a special loan policy.“Applicants must be locals of Telangana and must have studied from Class 6 to Class 10 in Telangana. Those applying with ITI qualifications must have completed their ITI from recognised institutions in Telangana,” the GO said.Irrespective of social category, unemployed people falling within the govt-prescribed EWS income limit can apply. Candidates should have at least two years of work experience in the relevant trade, though exemptions will apply depending on the work visa rules of the destination country.One beneficiary per familyThe subsidy will be restricted to one person per family based on the ration card. The MPDO, panchayat secretary or municipal staff must certify that no other family member has availed of assistance under the scheme.At least 33.33% of the beneficiaries will be women and 5% will be persons with disabilities.Officials said the selection process would be entirely online. A district-level committee will identify eligible candidates and recommend them to the state-level committee for final approval. Beneficiary selection will be completed within 30 days of the application deadline or completion of registration.Subsidy credited to bank accountsCandidates in the first category must clear interviews conducted by foreign employers. After they secure a job offer and visa, 50% of the eligible visa fee will be reimbursed.Once candidates travel and reach the destination country, they must submit their travel documents for verification, following which 50% of the eligible travel expenditure will be paid.GFX:Job opportunities in ten sectorsThe state govt said the scheme applies to jobs in the following sectors: construction and infrastructure, manufacturing industries, automobile, mechanical, electrical, electronics, transport and logistics, facility management, paramedical/healthcare support services, hotels and tourism, repairs and maintenance, and domestic and personal services. headline: Support to Bill may not automatically lead DMK to NDA, but will open alignment path
content: NEW DELHI: If Congress and DMK could join hands in 2004 after their bitter split where the Sonia Gandhi-led outfit accused the M Karunanidhi government of complicity in the assassination of former PM Rajiv Gandhi and brought down the United Front government in 1998, then anything can happen in politics. Thus said a multi-term DMK MP over the prospect of his party’s widely-expected support to BJP in securing passage of the delimitation bill in Parliament after it was in the vanguard of opposition to the governing party since 2014.While DMK’s support to the bill is unlikely to automatically lead the party to BJP-led NDA but it does open a path for their alignment and offer the national party a fresh opening in Tamil Nadu, which has remained a tough nut for it to crack despite repeated attempts. It certainly weakens the anti-South charge DMK, Congress and others have levelled against BJP.Besides making explicit provision in the bill that the share of every state in Lok Sabha will remain the same and the maximum strength of LS will be frozen till 2051, both concessions aimed at winning over DMK, BJP has of late made subtle moves to dial down its push for legislative measures which had drawn sharp opposition from the Tamil party.This includes a sudden slowdown in the working of two parliamentary committees overseeing Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, which has proposed an apex regulator in place of several for higher education, and a Constitution Amendment Bill, which proposes automatic removal of PM, CMs and ministers detained on criminal charges for 30 continuous days, when they were on the verge of adopting their reports.DMK, which has long championed state autonomy and decried central government’s alleged encroachment on its turf, has been sharply critical of both bills.Both parties have a history of working together. BJP and DMK were allies in the 1999 Lok Sabha elections and the regional party was a member of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led government before their split in 2003. Their “secular” opposition to BJP, which then moved closer to DMK’s rival AIADMK, helped them explain away their alliance. DMK’s current challenge is the sudden emergence of Vijay-led TVK as Congress dumped it overnight to help the star actor become chief minister.With DMK out of INDIA bloc, its options are limited. With misgivings persisting in a section of party over joining hands with BJP, which too has been a bitter critic of its anti-Hindutva rhetoric, political compulsions may be the glue for them in the same it worked for DMK and Congress in 2004.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Opposition mood despondent as NCP (SP), DMK change stand
content: NEW DELHI: The opposition Friday was staring at possible passage of the delimitation bill, after DMK and NCP (SP), which were critical to its defeat in April, signalled willingness to back the legislation. Congress said BJP wants to “change the Constitution” through delimitation after the ruling party failed to achieve it with the “400 paar” election, alleging the redrawing of LS seats would be done by “compromised” CEC Gyanesh Kumar, who has been “exposed” for manipulating electoral rolls.Vowing to “expose” BJP, AICC general secretary KC Venugopal said, “Modi and Shah want to set a big trap against the people of India. That is the design of this episode.” But the mood in the opposition was despondent as its persisting confidence about unity in the anti-bill ranks dissipated with statements from M K Stalin and NCP (SP) leaders.There was regret within that the Congress’s decision to abruptly dump a staunch ally, the DMK, in favour of TVK to form govt in TN had angered the Dravidian party into drifting towards BJP. The attacks from Congress leaders on DMK on Friday reflected the anger at the former ally, even as TN Congress members were peppered with queries about whether they regretted leaving the DMK alliance.Odisha’s interests to guide party’s delimitation stand: BJDAhead of the special sitting of Parliament, BJD Friday said party president Naveen Patnaik will take the final call on delimitation and the women’s reservation bills, with Odisha’s interests guiding the party’s stand, reports Ashok Pradhan. “Our decision will be guided by Odisha’s interests. Once we get a clear idea about the agenda and details of the bills, we will take an appropriate decision as per our party chief’s direction,” said Manas Mangaraj, head of BJD parliamentary party in Rajya Sabha.BJD has five members in Rajya Sabha but no representation in Lok Sabha.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions for States until 2051
content: New Delhi A new Constitutional Amendment Bill approved by the Union Cabinet on Friday (November 27, 2026) proposes an extension of the existing freeze on the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years, until 2051, addressing the core concern of States that feared a loss of their proportionate strength due to the decline in their share of the national population. Union Cabinet clears delimitation bill storyline 1 Also read | Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/lok-sabha-seat-freeze-is-no-longer-linked-to-population-stabilisation/article71752281.ece The 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill marks a significant turn from the 131st Amendment Bill moved by the Centre in April 2026 that sought to redistribute Lok Sabha seats among States according to the 2011 Census population. How should the Census count caste? storyline 1 The proposed amendment removes the linkage of the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats to the 1971 Census and links it with provisions related to women’s reservation in Article 334A of the Constitution. The guarantee for a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats for each State is being written into this, providing that, for the purposes of giving immediate effect to such reservation for women, “the delimitation so undertaken shall provide for an increase of fifty per cent in the number of seats allocated to each State and Union territory in the House of the People.” The total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State and Union territory will also increase similarly, “over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation”. The new Bill, accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in each State by 50%, while the maximum strength of the lower House will rise from the current 550 to 850. If these Bills are passed by Parliament in its special sittings from November 30 to December 3, the path to immediate delimitation will open, which will also bring into force the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha. Parliament will meet in a special sitting from November 30 to consider the proposal. Cabinet clears delimitation Bill; is a two-thirds majority within reach? | Above the Fold | Nov 27, 2026 video 1 Amendments to Articles 81 and 82, which mandate the size and distribution of Lok Sabha seats among the States, propose to extend a sunset clause for the existing proportion until 2051. The existing provision in Article 82 that says that “until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published, it shall not be necessary to readjust” the distribution of seats is being amended in the Bill and will be changed to read “until the year 2051”. The proposed amendment will extend the sunset clause to “until the year 2051”, but the reference to the 1971 Census has been dropped. The Bill proposes that the distribution among States will be determined “in accordance with Article 334A”, while the boundaries of individual constituencies will be determined by the “latest published census figures available on the date of the commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 2026”. headline: Hyderabad needs unified app for seamless bus-metro travel
content: Hyderabad: A single app integrating Metro and TGSRTC bus services, allowing commuters to plan journeys, check timings and buy tickets, could make public transport more convenient, experts said at a panel discussion on ‘How unified ticketing and open data can transform mobility’ at Cyberabad Moves.“The aim should be to make ticketing seamless, so passengers can pay for their entire journey as easily as making a UPI payment,” said Kavikrut, CEO of T-Hub.Moderated by Rohan Rao of WRI India, the session on ‘How unified ticketing and open data can transform mobility’ stressed the need for transport agencies to work together rather than operate in silos.T Ravikiran, commissioner of Electronic Services Delivery, and Sridhar, executive director of TGSRTC, called for better coordination between agencies to integrate bus and Metro services and boost public transport usage.The panel also highlighted the need for better last-mile connectivity through shared rides and carpooling between Metro stations and workplaces. Coupons and rewards could encourage commuters to use these options.Sharing anonymised data on routes, timings, live arrivals and passenger numbers could help developers build better travel apps and officials identify service gaps, plan feeder buses and improve connectivity, said Rakesh Dubbudu, CEO and faculty member.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. headline: Attacks on shipping, seafarers unacceptable: EAM
content: NEW DELHI: Attacks on maritime shipping and seafarers are simply unacceptable and call for a global response, EAM S Jaishankar said Friday. Addressing the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), an inter-governmental body comprising 23 member-states, he said international law, particularly United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, must be respected.The 25th meeting of the IORA council of ministers here was followed by a joint communique that expressed concern over the undermining of maritime safety and security of vessels and seafarers and called for ensuring their safety and security.PM Narendra Modi met the foreign ministers and heads of delegation of the 23 IORA member-states participating in the meeting. “Indian Ocean has connected our people for a millennia. As chair of IORA, India looks forward to working closely with all partners to advance its vision of Mahasagar (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) and to strengthen peace, security, stability and prosperity in the Indian Ocean Region,” he posted on X.According to the Delhi communique, IORA reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining the Indian Ocean as a region of peace, stability and prosperity, and to upholding applicable international law to ensure “freedom of navigation and overflight, unimpeded commerce, peaceful settlement of disputes and other lawful uses of the sea”. It also reaffirmed its commitment to sovereign equality, territorial integrity, political independence, non-interference in internal affairs, peaceful co-existence and mutual benefit.India announced a grant of $500,000 for the association’s institutional and financial capacity-building. “Whether it is to counter terrorism, narcotics trade or illegal, unreported, unregulated fishing, or indeed response to climate events and disaster situations, we have to become more self-reliant as well as more enthusiastic about cooperating with partners,” said Jaishankar.“We are focused on the volatile aspects of a transforming global order, especially conflicts, frictions and disruptions. It is equally imperative to appreciate the promising aspects: deep interdependence, strong globalisation and the benefits of international cooperation,” he said.The Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security, connectivity and economic prosperity. It is also a region of immense diversity, opportunity and of shared challenges, he stressed. “Our collective responsibility is to ensure that it remains peaceful, stable, secure and conducive to development,” Jaishankar added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Forus Health, Eyebetes Foundation work on AI-based diabetes screening - Mint
content: Mumbai’s Ganpati celebrations are synonymous with faith, community and public gatherings. This year, two of the city’s festival destinations became the setting for an initiative that brought an important conversation into the celebrations: preventive healthcare.Eyebetes Foundation, in collaboration with Forus Health, conducted a pilot retinal screening initiative at Siddhivinayak Temple and GSB Ganpati Mandal, exploring how retinal imaging and artificial intelligence could potentially support diabetes risk screening and generate insights associated with HbA1c levels.The initiative offered free screening activities to devotees and was designed to reach more than 15,000 people, bringing health awareness and preliminary screening closer to communities in an accessible environment.When the eye becomes a window to metabolic healthThe retina offers a distinctive view of the body’s microvascular system. Since diabetes can affect small blood vessels and cause changes in retinal structures, retinal imaging has attracted attention as a potential tool for identifying indicators associated with systemic health.At the Mumbai pilot, Forus Health explored this potential through AI-enabled retinal analysis, including its FH-POISE AI solutions. The technology uses retinal images to explore associations with diabetes risk and estimate HbA1c levels, offering a non-invasive screening pathway that does not initially require a blood sample or laboratory processing.“With FH-POISE AI solutions, we were exploring how a simple retinal image could provide insights that traditionally required a blood test. Our AI models could estimate HbA1c levels and flag diabetes risk from a single retinal image, without the need for a blood draw or laboratory processing. The retina gave us a unique, non-invasive view of the body’s microvascular health, and AI could help translate these insights into meaningful screening support,” said Srinivasan Venkatakrishnan, Chief Technology Officer and Head of Research & Development, Forus Health.The pilot demonstrated how technology can potentially bring preliminary health screening into settings beyond conventional hospitals and diagnostic centres.Taking screening where communities gatherOne of the takeaways from the initiative was the importance of accessibility. Diabetes screening often depends on an individual actively visiting a healthcare facility, undergoing testing and following up with a medical professional. Community-based initiatives can create an additional touchpoint by taking awareness and preliminary screening directly to people.Ganpati celebrations provided a significant setting for this approach. With thousands of devotees visiting the pandals, the initiative integrated health awareness into an existing community experience rather than requiring people to make a separate healthcare visit.Such models could have relevance for community health camps, workplaces, primary healthcare settings and mobile screening programmes, particularly where awareness or access to diagnostic facilities remains a challenge.Moving from screening to timely actionThe potential of AI-powered screening lies not simply in generating a digital insight, but in encouraging people to take the next step towards appropriate healthcare.An AI-generated estimate or risk indicator cannot replace conventional diagnostic testing. For individuals identified as potentially at risk, appropriate follow-up, including conventional HbA1c testing and consultation with a qualified healthcare professional, remains essential.“Diabetes was no longer only a metabolic concern; it was a major public health challenge with consequences that could affect the eyes, kidneys, heart, nerves and overall quality of life. What made AI-powered retinal screening particularly promising was its potential to make diabetes risk assessment quicker, non-invasive and more accessible, especially in communities where regular laboratory testing might not always be easy to access,” said Dr. Nishant Kumar, Consultant Ophthalmologist, Retina Surgeon and Uveitis Specialist, and Founder, Eyebetes Foundation.The collaboration highlighted the importance of developing datasets that represent Indian populations. Building Indian datasets and training AI models on relevant populations could play an important role in evaluating and refining the applicability of such technologies in the country.A broader role for AI in preventive healthcareThe Mumbai pilot reflects an evolution in healthcare, where artificial intelligence is being explored as a supporting tool for screening, risk identification and early intervention.For retinal healthcare, the possibilities extend beyond detecting eye conditions. The ability to examine retinal images for patterns associated with systemic health conditions could position the eye as an accessible entry point for preventive screening.However, responsible implementation remains central to this evolution. Clinical validation, representative datasets, appropriate referral pathways and clear communication about the limitations of AI-generated insights are critical to ensuring that technology complements rather than replaces established medical care.Bringing health awareness into everyday lifeThe collaboration between Forus Health and Eyebetes Foundation demonstrated an approach that combined technology, medical expertise and community engagement.By taking retinal screening to Siddhivinayak Temple and GSB Ganpati Mandal during one of Mumbai’s largest cultural celebrations, the initiative created an opportunity to connect preventive healthcare with everyday community life.Its significance extended beyond the screening activity itself. It opened a conversation around whether emerging technologies such as AI-powered retinal analysis could help make preliminary health screening more accessible, encourage earlier awareness and create links between communities and formal healthcare systems.The screening programme was intended for awareness and preliminary risk assessment. AI-generated health insights should not be considered a substitute for conventional HbA1c testing, clinical diagnosis or consultation with a qualified healthcare professional.Note to the Reader: This article is part of Mint's paid consumer connect initiative and is independently created by the brand. headline: E-certificates for new citizens, hard copy on request
content: NEW DELHI: Individuals who acquire Indian citizenship by registration or naturalisation will henceforth only be issued a digital certificate of registration as a citizen, with a hard copy being provided only upon the applicant’s request.As per amendments notified to Citizenship Rules, 2009, every person who is registered as a citizen of India under clauses a, c, d, e or f of Section 5(1) of Citizenship Act — by virtue of marriage to an Indian national, being born to Indian parents, or persons of Indian origin, etc — will be issued a digital certificate of registration in Form X, digitally signed or signed by an officer not under the rank of under-secretary to government of India or one who is authorised by the central government.Persons acquiring citizenship by naturalisation under Section 6(1) of the Citizenship Act will also be issued a digital certificate of naturalisation in Form XII, signed by an officer authorised by the Centre, and must place a request in case they want a hard copy of the certificate.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Hyderabad needs health database to track pollution impact
content: Hyderabad: Hyderabad needs a city-wide, anonymised health database linking major hospitals and public health authorities to track the impact of air pollution and identify vulnerable groups, experts said at the Cyberabad Moves event on Thursday.During a panel discussion on ‘Impact of Mobility on Air Quality and Public Health’, experts said the database could help identify patterns in respiratory and cardiac illnesses and trigger timely warnings on days of poor air quality.“What you cannot measure, you cannot manage. The data could help identify patterns in respiratory, cardiac and other illnesses, supporting evidence-based policymaking,” said Dr Sudhir V, regional medical director at KIMS. He suggested that hospitals display the Air Quality Index (AQI) and send alerts to patients with respiratory conditions during high-pollution days.Children, the elderly and pregnant women are particularly vulnerable to traffic pollution. Prolonged exposure could hamper lung development in children, while pregnant women could face complications, including low birth weight.“Pollution is contributing to a growing burden of respiratory illnesses, including asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD),” said Dr Vishwanath Gala, pulmonologist at AIG Hospitals, Gachibowli.Dr Shailaja Tetali, professor and dean at Public Health Foundation of India, said nearly 80% of schoolchildren lived within 2–3 km of their schools, making school zones ideal for targeted safety interventions. Travel also affects public health through road safety, physical activity and pollution exposure, she added.Experts urged cities to implement existing research rather than repeatedly conducting similar studies. A highway eye-screening programme had found poor eyesight among nearly 40% of truck drivers, highlighting the need for regular checks.“Unsafe road design, poor visibility at junctions and weak enforcement contribute to crashes. Simple engineering changes could improve safety without substantial expenditure,” said orthopaedic surgeon Dr Gurva Reddy.Panellists called for better last-mile connectivity, carpooling and integrated public transport to reduce private vehicle use. headline: Telangana’s working age mortality rate among the highest in major states
content: Hyderabad: Telangana recorded a death rate of 3.4 per 1,000 population among people aged 15-59 years in 2024, higher than the national average of 2.9, highlighting mortality risks among the working-age population that the govt seeks to address through its new family insurance scheme.According to Sample Registration System (SRS) Statistical Report 2024, Telangana’s mortality rate in this age group was among the highest reported by major states, alongside Karnataka and Odisha. Chhattisgarh topped the list with 4.4 deaths per 1,000.Gender-wise data showed a significant disparity, with the death rate among males at 4.6 per 1,000 against 2.3 among females. The rural mortality rate stood at 4.2, compared with 2.6 in urban areas. Rural male mortality was particularly high at 5.8 per 1,000.The figures assume significance as the govt considered mortality rates over the past decade while drawing up the framework for the Indiramma Kutumba Jeevitha Bima Padhakam. The scheme provides ₹5 lakh insurance cover to one member aged 18-59 years in each eligible household, with govt bearing the premium.Sources said the annual premium is estimated at around ₹3,000 per insured person, taking the annual cost of the scheme to ₹2,500 crore to ₹3,000 crore, depending on the final number of beneficiaries.The govt is preparing a request for proposal (RFP) to select an insurance company to implement the scheme. Mortality data is expected to help assess the potential claims burden and financial requirements.Funds for the scheme are expected to be allocated in next year’s budget, following the initial three months of implementation, sources said.However, the SRS figure covers the 15-59 age group and cannot be treated as an exact mortality rate for the scheme’s eligible 18-59 age group. headline: Indiramma insurance: Telangana weighs Aadhaar-based cover for families without ration cards
content: Hyderabad: Telangana govt is considering extending Indiramma Kutumba Jeevitha Bima Padhakam to families without ration cards, with officials exploring Aadhaar-based enrolment. Final eligibility guidelines, however, are yet to be worked out.Another issue under consideration is enrolment of families whose heads are living abroad. Around three lakh families are estimated to fall under this category. Officials are examining whether another family member can register on behalf of the household head or whether the insured person must personally complete the enrolment process.Launched by chief minister A Revanth Reddy at Siddipet on Nov 19, the scheme provides ₹5 lakh life insurance cover to one member aged 18-59 years in each eligible household, with govt bearing the premium. Sources said three lakh families have been enrolled in the scheme since its launch.According to sources, initial enrolment is based on ration card details, but officials are considering allowing families without ration cards to register in a subsequent phase. One proposal is to exclude income-tax payers among such households.Telangana has around 1.15 crore families, of whom nearly 40 lakh are already covered under various govt insurance schemes and welfare programmes. Existing insurance schemes, including Rythu Bima, are proposed to be brought under the new umbrella to avoid overlap in coverage.Meanwhile, implementation guidelines issued on Nov 21 allow families holding ration cards from other districts to enrol at the nearest registration camp. Their details will be retrieved from the original district for verification, with original ration card numbers serving as a unique reference to prevent duplicate applications. This facility applies only to Telangana ration cards.The guidelines also prescribe July 1 as the deemed date of birth when Aadhaar mentions only the year of birth. Applicants with incorrect birth dates must get Aadhaar corrected before enrolment. Pending ration card e-KYC must be completed at the respective PDS shops. headline: Teachers won't be assigned non-academic duties, assures Karnataka Education minister Madhu
content: Minister for School Education and Literacy on Friday assured teachers that they would not be deputed for miscellaneous non-academic work..Amid reports of the Department of Youth Empowerment and Sports (DYES) mulling appointing teachers as co-ordinators for the Bharat Jodo Youth Clubs, the minister’s statement is certain to have teachers heaving a sigh of relief. .“Both the state and central governments must look for alternatives to teachers for undertaking work on exercises such as SIR, census, et al,” Madhu told DH..Teachers had recently been invited to a meeting organised by DYES to discuss plans for the Bharat Jodo Youth Clubs, where they were told that they would be roped in as co-ordinators for the exercise. .Karnataka State Primary School Teachers’ Association drew the minister’s attention to the proposal, and appealed to him to save them from being enlisted for yet another non-academic exercise..Madhu Bangarappa sets April deadline to recruit government schoolteachers.Acknowledging the receipt of the representation submitted by the association, Madhu added, “I am prepared to participate in any agitation to prevent teachers from being enlisted for other work. Above all else, it is the future of children that matters most.”.The minister said that he would table the issue for discussion in the Cabinet. Urging both state and Central governments to make alternative arrangements, Madhu said that teachers’ concerns about being kept away from classrooms for a prolonged period owing to their participation in SIR had been conveyed to the competent authorities. .“Teachers must complete portions, take special classes. Such being the case, assigning them other work is unacceptable,” he said..Madhu inaugurated a workshop organised for teachers as part of the government’s efforts to improve SSLC results.

headline: Explainer: 80 per cent jobs for Himachalis, how?
content: Even as the Congress government in Himachal Pradesh has proposed to stringently enforce the provision for providing 80 per cent jobs to locals in industrial units in the state through a legislation, critics point to the impracticality of the move, which was first announced in the 2019 Industrial Policy of the then BJP government.The issue again came into focus during the passage of the Himachal Pradesh Investment Promotion and Facilitation Bill, 2026, on the last day of the Winter Session on November 21. Although the Bill is silent on making 80 per cent jobs for Himachalis mandatory, Industries Minister Harshwardhan Chauhan assured that it will form part of the Rules to be framed under the legislation.It was in the 2004 Industrial Policy that a provision was made for making 70 per cent jobs mandatory for Himachalis in industries. The figure was enhanced to 80 per cent in the 2019 policy. The Labour and Employment Department was tasked with inspecting industrial units to ensure its implementation.Responding to the Opposition queries when the Bill came up for discussion last week, the Industries Minister assured that the state government will frame Rules to make it mandatory to provide 80 per cent jobs to Himachalis. This, he said, would make compliance legally binding, failing which strict action would be initiated against the industrial units.Investment promotion legislationThe recently passed Bill provides for a comprehensive legal framework to attract investment, expedite industrial approvals, strengthen infrastructure and promote sustainable industrialisation.The industry in Himachal is primarily confined to areas close to the border with Punjab and Haryana: Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh (BBN) in Solan, Kala Amb as well as Paonta Sahib in Sirmaur, and Una.Past experience shows that there are several practical challenges in enforcing the provision of 80 per cent jobs for locals. The biggest hurdle is the skill mismatch; there is a lack of qualified and trained workforce, besides the reluctance to work in smaller units.Former Director Industries Rajender Singh, while supporting the job quota, stresses the need for making skilled training demand-driven. “We have not been able to meet even 60 per cent jobs for Himachalis in the past. There has to be a coordinated effort from the industry, the state government and the unemployed youth so that the 80 per cent condition does not remain confined to paper,” he says.Why it is difficult to implementIn states like Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Jharkhand and Karnataka, the provision of 70 to 80 per cent jobs for locals was challenged in court and even struck down in some places. As such, the move could have legal implications.President of the Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh Industries Association YS Guleria says the exact details of the legislation are awaited. “We are not averse to providing maximum jobs to Himachalis but before enforcing the 80 per cent clause, certain issues like the mismatch between availability and requirement and synchronisation and updation of the data of the Employment Exchanges will have to be addressed,” he points out. Guleria adds that the industry will take up the matter with the state government to get a clear picture.Himachal Pradesh has limited industries, that too confined to the fringes. Having strict statutory quotas for jobs, the industry leaders point out, could make investors wary of setting up factories or expanding existing units as domicile job quotas can result in legal scrutiny. Many investors feel that making the jobs for locals requirement legally binding would be counter-productive in attracting investors as even now a majority of workers are from Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and other states.Critics point out that mandating jobs for locals could be a double-edged sword, as it could discourage industrial investment in a state which has very limited job avenues. Himachal, they add, has to grapple with severe geographical constraints and locational disadvantages as it has very limited sectors as employment-generating avenues.

headline: CJI had sought probe against Jharkhand high court judge. He is Jhakhand acting chief justice now
content: NEW DELHI: In a rare instance, CJI Surya Kant last week asked Jharkhand High Court’s then Chief Justice M S Sonak to probe a spate of complaints questioning the integrity of Justice Sujit Narayan Prasad of the HC.The CJI neither confirmed nor denied receiving a report from Justice Sonak, who is credited with streamlining procedures at the HC after becoming CJ on Jan 9. Justice Sonak retired on Nov 27, and Justice Prasad was appointed acting CJ from Nov 28.Though the CJI’s office routinely receives complaints against sitting judges of various HCs, largely driven by angst of litigants or counsel, in Justice Prasad’s case, many complainants provided documentary evidence to back up their charges.Sources in the Jharkhand government told TOI that complaints against the judge had also reached CM Hemant Soren, who recently requested CJI Kant to look into the concerns.Justice Prasad was appointed to Jharkhand HC on Sept 26, 2014, and transferred six months later to Orissa HC. He was repatriated to Jharkhand HC on Nov 22, 2018. He will retire as an HC judge on June 19, 2029, unless elevated to the SC.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Young artists bring laurels to Government Smart School
content: Two students of Government Smart School, Moti Nagar, have brought laurels to their institution by securing top honours in different categories at the district-level educational competitions.While Pooja impressed the judges with her painting skills, Muskan secured the top position in the “Waste to Best Material” category by transforming discarded items into a creative piece.Expressing happiness over her achievement, Pooja said, “I enjoy expressing my thoughts through colours and sketches. Winning the competition has motivated me to work even harder and participate in more art events.”Muskan said the competition had taught her the importance of creativity and sustainability. “It feels great to turn waste materials into something useful and beautiful. This achievement has boosted my confidence and encouraged me to think more innovatively,” she said.School Head Sukhdir Singh Sekhon said the institution focused on the holistic development of students through art workshops, craft activities, creative writing, yoga, quizzes, abacus and sports.He said special training in art and creative crafts was being provided by artists Amar Singh and Inderpreet Kaur, who were helping students nurture their talents and prepare for various competitions.The two students were felicitated during a special morning assembly, where teachers and classmates applauded their achievements. They were presented with prizes and encouraged to continue pursuing their creative interests, serving as an inspiration for other students to explore their talents and participate in creative activities.

headline: Supreme Court raps TVK government, orders lamp lit at Tamil Nadu site today
content: NEW DELHI: In a rebuke to the Vijay government, the Supreme Court on Friday initiated contempt proceedings against top officers of Tamil Nadu — its chief secretary, DGP and 11 others — for “wilful” and “deliberate” disobedience of its order on lamp lighting at Deepathoon at the temple of Lord Murugan and acting not on its direction, but seemingly “on the dictates of their political boss”.It directed that lighting would be done on Saturday and, unlike in the previous order where only limited people were allowed to light the lamp, Supreme Court said that now every devotee can light the lamp at the disputed site 50 metres away from the nearby dargah.Holding that the majesty of the court is non-negotiable, Supreme Court also directed CRPF to take over the security of the site from the state police, indicating that the court had lost faith in the state administration to carry out its order. The bench then went on to suspend the board of trustees of Arulmigu Subramania Swamy Temple and appointed former Madras HC judges Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthiban as receivers to manage the affairs of the site. The court said that the conduct of all state authorities, including the board of trustees and state police, shocked its conscience.An order of this court is not an invitation to negotiate, warns Supreme CourtThe Supreme Court made it clear that all state authorities must be treated with an iron hand for creating “constitutional chaos” by refusing to comply with its order.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi held that a contempt case is prima facie made out against them and directed them to appear before it on Dec 15 to explain the defiance of the apex court’s directive.The non-compliance stood out against the backdrop of opposition to the lighting of the lamp atop the Deepathoon from Sikandar Badusha Dargah Committee, state government, its Hindu religious and charitable endowments department, Madurai district administration, and the temple board of trustees.An array of political parties — TVK as well as its predecessor in office, DMK, Congress, Left parties — and Muslim outfits have been opposing the move.Expressing its “pain and anguish” at the way in which its order had been undermined, the court indicated that it was left with no option but to deal with an iron hand, or it would lead to constitutional chaos. At the outset of dictating the order, Justice Kumar said, “Alas is the first word that comes to mind.”It said the concept of the rule of law is supreme in a democratic society and cannot be allowed to be weakened, and it is mandatory under Article 14 for all authorities, civil and judicial, in the territory of India to act in aid of the Supreme Court.“An order of this court is not an invitation to negotiate. It binds the state, its officers and every statutory or religious institution functioning under the state’s law until this court itself modifies it. Any attempt to pollute the stream of justice by any person, howsoever high he may be, would not be tolerated… Therefore, when an order of this court is violated, we cannot sit in silos… This is the message which we intend to convey in this order.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Gavai cites two examples to buttress caste bias claim
content: NEW DELHI: Slamming the Supreme Court collegium’s recent recommendation for transfer of Tripura HC Chief Justice MS Ramachandra Rao as the chief justice of Karnataka HC, former CJI B R Gavai Friday asked whether the judge, who was transferred multiple times on punitive considerations, was being rewarded with a bigger and more prominent high court just because he belonged to an upper caste.Without naming Justice Rao, the ex-CJI in his letter to President Droupadi Murmu said the recommendation “raises several unanswered questions as to how a judge transferred multiple times on punitive considerations is now being recommended to be chief justice of a much bigger and prominent high court”.On Nov 26, TOI had reported that Justice Rao, son of former Supreme Court judge Justice M Jagannadha Rao, was appointed as judge of Andhra Pradesh HC in 2012 and had opted for Telangana HC in 2019 after the state’s bifurcation.He was transferred to the Punjab and Haryana HC and then made the chief justice of the Himachal Pradesh HC. Later, he was shifted to the Jharkhand and Tripura high courts.“A chief justice who was transferred from one high court to another smaller HC and thereafter from that HC to one of the smallest HCs of the country has now been rewarded for being from a particular community, by transfer to a prominent high court,” the ex-CJI said.Sources in the top court said serving Supreme Court judges from Karnataka, one of whom is in the collegium and is slated to become the first woman CJI next year, were prominent backers of the proposal to transfer Justice Rao as CJ of Karnataka.The Centre is yet to act on the recommendations, which include transfer of Karnataka HC CJ Vibhu Bakhru to Jharkhand HC and appointment of Justice Vivek Singh Thakur of Himachal HC as the chief justice of Tripura HC.Again, without naming Justice Bakhru, former CJI Gavai said the transfer of the “meritorious and hardworking CJ of Karnataka” to a smaller high court to make way for Justice Rao not only demoralises meritorious judges like Justice Bakhru but “also has a chilling effect on all hard-working judges, including persons belonging to marginalised sections of society”.Justice Gavai said he was highlighting the issue (relating to Justice Rao) as he was part of the collegium when the judge was transferred from one HC to a smaller HC (Jharkhand) and was heading the collegium when he was transferred to the smallest high court (Tripura).Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: BJP says SC rebuke exposes Congress’s anti-Sanatan character
content: NEW DELHI: BJP president Nitin Nabin Friday hailed the SC order for the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at a stone pillar considered sacred by Hindus at Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai, and said that the rebuke to the TVK government has exposed the anti-Sanatan character of Congress and its allies.“By ordering the ceremonial lamp to be lit at the Thiruparankundram Deepathoon tomorrow (Saturday) and pulling up Tamil Nadu authorities for acting at the dictates of their political bosses, SC has thoroughly exposed the INDI Alliance government’s anti-Sanatan mindset,” he said.“No political conspiracy can stop the sacred traditions of Bharat. May the divine blessings of Lord Murugan protect all devotees and guide them on the path of courage and righteousness,” he added.“Today’s judicial intervention reinforces the principle that the rule of law, constitutional values and the rights of devotees must take precedence over political appeasement and ideological prejudice,” he said, adding that India’s spiritual heritage is rooted in its civilisational traditions.He said no political conspiracy, administrative obstruction or ideological hostility can stand in the way of the faith of millions of people.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Uttar Pradesh Khadi Mahotsav begins in Lucknow
content: Lucknow Uttar Pradesh Minister for Khadi and Village Industries, Silk Industry and MSME Rakesh Sachan in Lucknow on Friday (November 27, 2026) said Khadi is not merely a fabric, but a powerful idea of self-respect, Swadeshi and self-reliance. Mr. Sachan made the remark while inaugurating the 10-day state-level ‘Uttar Pradesh Khadi Mahotsav-2026’ on Friday at the Central Sanskrit University campus in Lucknow’s Gomti Nagar. Organized by the Uttar Pradesh Khadi and Village Industries Board, the festival will run from 27 November to 06 December 2026. “The Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, had made Khadi the most important medium in the struggle for the country’s independence and self-reliance. The Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s calls for ‘Vocal for Local’ and ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ have given Khadi a new identity and fresh momentum since 2014, “ said the Minister. Minister Rakesh Sachan said that under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the State government is committed to creating employment in rural areas and making young people ‘not job seekers, but job creators’. He said that over the past 05 years, loans worth ₹2,544.35 crore have been disbursed under the ‘Chief Minister’s Village Industries Employment Scheme’ and the ‘Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme’. With this financial assistance, 24,799 village industries units have been established across the state, providing direct employment to more than 2,79,000 people. In addition, through 27,508 stalls at 115 exhibitions organized in all 18 divisions of the state, entrepreneurs have recorded sales of more than ₹161.54 crore, reflecting the growing public confidence in Khadi and Village Industries products. Mr. Sachan said that by adopting Khadi garments for weddings and other auspicious occasions, citizens are enriching traditional culture. “New Khadi sales centers are being opened in various cities for the convenience of customers. In addition, a special discount of 30% is being offered on the purchase of Khadi fabrics and garments from Gandhi Jayanti [02 October], so that more and more people can connect with Swadeshi products. Based on the theme ‘Culture in Threads, Progress through Khadi’, a total of 150 stalls have been set up at the festival by Khadi and Village Industries entrepreneurs and artisans from various districts of the State,” said the Minister. Mr. Sachan also visited all the stalls and encouraged the artisans. He said that today’s Khadi, with the assurance of 100 percent pure cotton, is increasingly becoming the first choice of young people in the form of modern and designer garments. Principal Secretary, Khadi and Village Industries Department, Anil Kumar Sagar, and Chief Executive Officer of the U.P. Khadi and Village Industries Board, Shishir, were present at the inaugural ceremony.

headline: Collegium favouring caste that is 5% of population: Ex-CJI Gavai writes to President
content: NEW DELHI: Ex-CJI B R Gavai on Friday scathingly criticised his successor CJI Surya Kant-led Supreme Court Collegium for ignoring SC, ST, OBC, minority and women candidates and favouring one particular caste -- with just about a 5% population share -- in the appointment of judges to SC & HCs, in complete disregard for the principles of merit and inclusivity, & sought President Droupadi Murmu’s intervention to set things right.Writing an unprecedented three-page letter urging President to hold the Collegium “accountable”, Justice Gavai said that when he headed the collegium, he had ensured that candidates from different sections of society were recommended for appointment as judges.Familiarity, networks factors in picking judges, says ex-CJIHowever, in the recent past, disturbing events have unfolded, showing complete disregard for principles of merit and inclusivity. Candidates belonging to one particular section of society are being favoured for recommendation/elevation, to the exclusion of everyone else, including marginalised communities like Scheduled Castes/Tribes, other backward classes, minorities, women and even persons from forward sections of society who are not from a particular community,” former CJI BR Gavai said, adding that the recent use of an unquantifiable metric like demeanour has only aggravated the problem of opacity and favouritism.He did not mention the caste in question, but the ire seemed to be targeted at Brahmins, the caste that CJI Surya Kant belongs to, with Justice Gavai referring to the large share the community has historically enjoyed among members of the higher judiciary.The ex-CJI said that in the first four decades of the Supreme Court, that is, till the 1990s, when the SC, through two judgements, took over selection of candidates for appointment as judges to the Supreme Court and high courts, a community (read Brahmins), then about 1/19th of the population, held over one-third of SC judgeships and lamented that even after 75 years, the pattern persists.The skew in the caste backgrounds of judges has been long debated and has been variously attributed to merit, historical lead of the upper castes, elite affinity and downright casteist bias. Social justice formations have cited this to demand reservation in the judiciary.The Narendra Modi govt also argued for the need to make the judiciary more socially representative while making a push for substituting the Collegium system with the National Judicial Appointments Commission as the recruitment agency for judges. However, it is rare for a former member of the collegium, that too one who served as the CJI, to put the issue so glaringly in the public domain.Lamenting the lack of objectivity and suitability in the process to select judges, the former CJI said it now operates through familiarity, networks and a weird theory of ‘who looks like Supreme Court material’.Ex-CJI Gavai stressed that he was not opposed to meritorious upper-caste candidates getting appointed as judges and only wanted that there must be proportional representation of marginalised communities in Constitutional courts to reflect the country’s social diversity.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Crime control, zero tolerance for drugs: Amritsar’s first woman SSP Dr Pragya Jain outlines priorities
content: Maintaining law and order and intensified action against drug trafficking will be the top priorities for Dr Pragya Jain, a 2017-batch IPS officer, who on Thursday assumed charge as the new Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Amritsar Rural.Jain, who succeeded the outgoing incumbent Kanwalpreet Singh Chahal, is perhaps the first woman police officer posted as the SSP of sensitive Amritsar rural police after a long time.Having extensive experience in policing and anti-drug operations, she earlier served as SSP Faridkot and Fazilka. She also served as Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in Amritsar city police commissionerate.Amritsar Rural belt has over 100 km International Border with Pakistan, posing a humongous challange of cross border smuggling of arms and drugs smuggling being airdropped by drones. She also paid obeisance at the Golden Temple and prayed for the welfare, peace and prosperity of all.During her postings, she led operations against criminal and terror modules and played a significant role in anti-drug campaigns. Under Mission Nishchay, a state-level anti-drug campaign, more than 350 drug smugglers were arrested in Fazilka and Faridkot.During her tenure in Fazilka, the police recovered 66 kg of opium from Jharkhand, described as the biggest seizure in the region in a decade. Properties worth more than Rs 10 crore belonging to drug smugglers were also frozen under the NDPS Act. In Barnala, she led action against pharmaceutical opioids, busting the Agra-Mathura gang and recovering more than three crore intoxicant tablets and capsules. During her posting in the Ludhiana Commissionerate, over 60 lakh intoxicant tablets and capsules were seized. As SP (D), Khanna, around 200 weapons were recovered during her tenure.For her performance as SSP, Faridkot, Jain became the first woman IPS officer from Punjab to receive the Union Home Minister’s Dakshata Padak. She has also received several DGP commendation discs and appreciation certificates.Speaking after paying obeisance at the Golden Temple, Jain said it was a matter of pride and privilege for her to serve the people of Amritsar, the holy city of the Gurus.

headline: Cultural values of language remain irreplaceable in AI era: Arabic meet
content: MALAPPURAM Artificial Intelligence (AI) may transform the way Arabic is learned and used, but human emotions and traditional values remain beyond the reach of technology, an international conference on the Arabic language held at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, observed on Thursday. The two-day conference, titled ‘Digital humanities: reimagining Arabic language and literature’, was organised by the Arabic department of the college in association with Calicut University’s Arabic department, Kerala State Higher Education Council, and Arab Union of Internet Writers. Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurated the conference on Wednesday. College Principal K. Mohammed Fawaz presided over the function. Arabic scholars Sumayya Ibrahim Abu Thailath from Palestine, Najeeb Ali Mulkhath from Yemen, Simi K. Salim, K. Ali Noufal, I.P. Abdul Salam, C.M. Sabir Navas, K.A. Nasser, P. Firoz, M.K. Ameer Swalahi, Shakir Babu Kuniyil, and K.P. Abdul Haleem Thangal spoke. E.T. Mohammed Basheer, MP, inaugurated the valedictory function on Thursday. He highlighted the growing global significance of the Arabic language in an increasingly interconnected world. Scholars Mujeeb Nellikkuth, Ali Jafar, Mohammed Aman K., P. Sulaiman and C. Abdul Wahab spoke.

headline: Amritsar: Top cop Harmanbir Singh Gill returns as DIG, Border Range
content: Nearly three months after taking over as the Commissioner of Police, Amritsar, Harmanbir Singh Gill has returned as the DIG, Border Range. He assumed the charge in his office today.Gill was earlier posted as the DIG, Border Range, in June this year. However, following the transfer of the then Police Commissioner, Gurpreet Singh Bhullar, he was given the additional charge of the Amritsar Police Commissioner on August 1. In a subsequent reshuffle on September 1, he was formally posted as the Police Commissioner, while Bhullar was shifted as the IG, Border Range.In the latest police reshuffle ahead of the Assembly poll, Bhullar has been posted as the Jalandhar Police Commissioner, while Gill has been brought back as the DIG, Border Range. DIG Kuldeep Singh Chahal has taken over as the new Police Commissioner, Amritsar.Known for carrying out night domination operations apart from successfully cracking the ASI Harjit Singh murder case who was gunned down by armed assailants in a targetted attacks on cops, Gill said strengthening security along the International Border, checking the smuggling of narcotics and weapons through drones and preventing youngsters from being lured into criminal activities would be among his key priorities. He said if any youth had been lured into crime by unscrupulous elements unknowingly, they would be helped into rehabilitation.The DIG said the police would also focus on preventing youngsters from falling prey to inducements offered by anti-national elements and criminal networks.Those found luring the youth into such activities would face legal action.After assuming charge, Gill said the functioning of the first and second lines of defence would also be reviewed, with emphasis on improving surveillance and accountability at all levels. He said the close coordination and cooperation with the various sister agencies would be ensured.The Village Defence Committees (VDCs), constituted in border villages, would be reactivated to strengthen the local intelligence network and ensure timely sharing of information about suspicious activities, he added.Gill said modern technology and a strengthened policing mechanism wouldbe used to improve security in the sensitive border belt.

headline: Not a single foot of blacktopping done on Amarnath route, PDP-BJP stoking Hindu-Muslim discord: Omar Abdullah
content: Srinagar J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Friday (November 27, 2026) said not a single foot of blacktopping was carried out on the Amarnath route, while referring to the Sheshnag controversy, and accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) of “deliberately pitting Hindus and Muslims against each other”. Also read | No tampering, violation found at Sheshnag lake: J&K Minister Altaf Kaloo https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/jammu-and-kashmir/no-tampering-violation-found-at-sheshnag-lake-jk-minister-altaf-kaloo/article71741828.ece “The BJP and those carrying the symbol of pen and inkpot [referring to the PDP] are again trying to foment Hindu-Muslim discord over the Amarnath route. They are alleging macadamisation. I challenge them to prove a single foot of blacktopping done on the route. I am ready to face an inquiry. There is a court [Supreme Court] direction to have a 12-feet stretch,” said Mr. Abdullah. Mr. Abdullah’s statement came days after local parties, religious leaders, environmentalists and civil society bodies reacted sharply to the presence of an earthmover close functioning to the Sheshnag lake situation at an altitude of 11,780 feet on the way to the Amarnath shrine, which is around 20 km away from the spot. Shocked to see use of heavy equipment at Sheshnag, no need for motorable roads to pilgrimages: Dr. Karan Singh Shocked to see use of heavy equipment at Sheshnag, no need for motorable roads to pilgrimages: Dr. Karan Singh ‘I was shocked to read that heavy earth moving equipment is being used to widen the route to Shri Amarnath ji, and that too at a spot overlooking Sheshnag, which is one of the most beautiful lakes in India,’ said Dr. Karan Singh Shocked to see use of heavy equipment at Sheshnag, no need for motorable roads to pilgrimages: Dr. Karan Singh storyline 1 A report prepared by the J&K Forest Department on the viral video, in which an earthmover was seen close to the lake, said, “The activity seen in the video is part of routine annual maintenance operations being undertaken by the Border Roads Organisation [BRO]. No new road construction or fresh alignment is being undertaken. It is further clarified that the Yatra track runs along the right-hand side of the lake and is situated at a considerable distance from the lake. “It said the lake remains protected and the maintenance activity in question “was not intended to alter its character or ecological integrity”. “The matter may, therefore, be viewed in its proper context, keeping in view the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the safety requirements of the annual pilgrimage and the longstanding nature of the track maintenance operations,” it added, while underlining that the maintenance and improvement of this track is a longstanding exercise undertaken regularly since 2012 and “not a new activity initiated in 2026”. Why viral video of an earthmover near Kashmir’s Sheshnag Lake has sparked protests | Explained Why viral video of an earthmover near Kashmir’s Sheshnag Lake has sparked protests | Explained Dismissing social media claims of fresh construction as “incorrect,” the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) clarified that the ongoing activity is strictly confined to widening and maintaining existing pilgrimage tracks Why viral video of an earthmover near Kashmir’s Sheshnag Lake has sparked protests | Explained storyline 1 However, Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti, who was denied permission to visit the spot with police citing security concerns, has asked the government to allow a team of politicians and experts to visit the Sheshnag lake. “If the Union Territory [UT] government is relying on satellite images to claim that no construction is taking place at Sheshnag, why not allow us to visit the site and see for ourselves? The JCBs wreaking havoc there are visible for all to see. To dispel all doubts, let the Chief Minister depute a team of political leaders and environmentalists to inspect the site and establish the truth. What is there to hide?” said Ms. Mufti. Meanwhile, referring to the allegations of irregularities in the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination conducted by the J&K Service Selection Board JKSSB), Mr. Abdullah said, “Political opponents were exploiting the concerns of unemployed youth and creating unnecessary mistrust about the recruitment process. I am always ready to admit if a mistake is committed. But when I dug deep into the matter, I found that instead of there being fraud in the examination, the fact is that the system worked properly. The paper did not leak. The paper was not stolen.” Terming the incident as a case of “attempted cheating but disallowed”, Mr. Abdullah said, “There were people who tried to cheat in the examination. I agree with this. They took out the question paper from the examination hall, used wireless devices and tried to get answers. But they were caught on the spot. They were arrested. The JKSSB should have been praised for it,” said Mr. Abdullah. Meanwhile, protests in J&K over the JKSSB recruitments continued with protesters demanding postponement of the upcoming examination for the posts of Sub-Inspector “till reformations are carried out”. The JKSSB had conducted the Finance Accounts Assistant examination on November 15, 2026, for around 600 posts and around 1,62 lakh candidates appear in it.

headline: Amritsar civic body is all talk, no action: Locals on stray dog crisis and control measures
content: The Municipal Corporation’s sterilisation drive appears inadequate to tackle the growing menace as only around 25 dogs are sterilised daily. The city’s canine population has been estimated at 60,000.The target is to sterilise 20,000 in the coming months.Dog bite cases in Amritsar have nearly tripled over the past five years, rising from around 12,000 in 2020 to around 58,000 in 2025.The city has also witnessed two deaths due to dog attacks this year. On November 23, an eight-year-old boy Ranjit Singh was attacked by stray dogs at Jalal Usma village in the Jandiala Guru area, highlighting the growing concern in both urban and rural areas.The rising number of incidents has exposed the limitations of the existing sterilisation programme and a lack of a comprehensive strategy to manage the stray dog population. Residents in several localities have complained about packs of dogs roaming streets, parks, neighbourhoods and public spaces, posing a threat to pedestrians, particularly children and elderly persons.The Municipal Corporation has set a target of sterilising 20,000 stray dogs in the coming months. However, at the current pace of about 25 sterilisation procedures daily, achieving the target will be difficult unless the programme is significantly scaled up.The Supreme Court has also issued directions regarding the management of stray dogs, including their removal from certain public spaces and institutional premises; and measures to prevent their return to the same locations. However, the the MC has so far failed to establish feeding points for stray dogs in compliance with court directions.Pawan Kumar, a resident said, “With dog bite incidents increasing and the sterilisation programme moving at a slow pace, how does the administration plan to contain the stray dog population and ensure public safety?”

headline: Experts at GNDU conclave call for balanced development of Amritsar
content: As Amritsar approaches the 450th anniversary of its foundation, heritage and architecture experts have called for a fresh approach to urban development that preserves not merely its historic monuments but also the traditional neighbourhoods, bustling bazaars, crafts and social fabric that have shaped the city’s identity over centuries.The issue came into focus during a special session on Architecture, Planning, History and Future of Amritsar, organised as part of the International Conclave on Amritsar 450 at Guru Nanak Dev University (GNDU). The discussion brought together heritage conservation and architectural experts, including Dr Balwinder Singh, Prof Sarbjot Singh Behl, Dr Radha Sharma, Dr Karamjit Singh Chahal and Punjab Chief Town Planner, Punjab, Pankaj Bawa.Revisiting the city’s historic urban landscape, Dr Radha highlighted how old Amritsar evolved as a vibrant commercial and artisanal centre under the patronage of Sikh rulers, who encouraged traders, weavers and craftsmen from different regions to settle here.“The city’s historic identity was reflected in its network of katras, kuchas, deoris and bazaars, many named after the communities and occupations associated with them. Neighbourhoods such as Katra Mian Singh, Katra Hakeema, Katra Baghian and Katra Khazana, along with Bazaar Kucha Bazian, Kucha Rababian and Kucha-i-Patrangan, represented a rich occupational and cultural landscape. The latter, associated with dyers, reflected the city’s textile traditions. The famous Batti Hatta, or cluster of 32 shops, remains a reminder of Amritsar’s early commercial foundations,” she shared.She stressed how preserving the cultural and heritage value of these katras and streets through nomenclature is necessary. “These katras and streets, historically, traces the city’s early trading settlements to merchants invited by Guru Ram Das. These merchants, artisans, craftsmen settled here and made Amritsar the way it is,” she said.Dr Balwinder Singh, who has an extensive experience as a spatial and conservation expert, also drew attention to the architectural and ecological heritage gradually disappearing from the walled city. Traditional craftsmanship, including gold and silver filigree, inlay work and wood carving, once contributed to its distinct character. He referred to historical records documenting around 1,400 wells in the city in 1892, most of them now either demolished or filled up for new, modern constructions.“Similarly, only a handful of traditional akharas survive today. The walled city’s inherent character has been lost to rampant construction and the loss of historic structures, including several deoris and market spaces, which has further weakened the continuity of its urban heritage,” he said.Prof SS Behl, former head of Guru Ramdas School of Architecture and Planning, GNDU, deliberated on the need to move beyond isolated monument conservation towards protecting the city’s organic urban form, human-scale streets, traditional markets and living communities.“The future of the city rests in striking a balance between infrastructure improvements and urban expansion that is planned in consultation with local stakeholders rather than imposed at the cost of the city’s architectural character. It needs political will, public participation and concerted efforts,” he said.As the city looks towards 2052, the question is no longer merely how to develop Amritsar, but how to ensure that it remains recognisably Amritsar.

headline: Mill workers protest over pending demands in Amritsar
content: With the support of BKU Ekta Ugrahan and Bharatiya Kisan Union Ekta Sangharsh, all the workers, including women employees of the OCM Mill took out a protest march from the mill to Khandwala Chowk, here on Friday. The protest was part of their stir which entered 21st day on Friday.Addressing the protesters, a leader of the protesters Shamsher Singh demanded that the unskilled workers who have been working for years should be regularised, the workers' committee be re-elected, other benefits including DA fund be given and about 70 workers who were dismissed from their jobs during the agitation be reinstated unconditionally. Apart from this, they demanded that weekly and festival holidays be given.Another leader Parminder Singh Pandori in his address said due to the government's pro-corporate policies, the condition of farmers, farm labourers and industrial workers, small traders, shopkeepers is continuously deteriorating. In the past, the four labour codes introduced by the Narendra Modi government opened the way for the loot of labourers. Inflation is continuously increasing, but salaries are very low and the burden of debt is increasing, he said. He demanded that the contract system be cancelled and a concrete solution be found after listening to the demands of the workers.

headline: Success requires consistent effort, discipline: Himachal minister Dharmani
content: Technical Education Minister Rajesh Dharmani urged students to make the most of every moment by learning new things and continuously upgrading their knowledge and skills. He was addressing the annual prize distribution function at Government Senior Secondary School, Dadhol, in the Ghumarwin Assembly constituency of Bilaspur district on Friday.He said that success in life could not be achieved through a single day’s hard work but required consistent effort, discipline and a commitment to continuous self-improvement.Dharmani observed that students who embrace good values, discipline and positive habits gradually progress towards success. He added that the purpose of education and personality development should not be limited to earning a livelihood but should also empower individuals to fulfil their responsibilities towards their families and society effectively.Appreciating the school staff, Dharmani said that despite limited resources and infrastructure, the school had consistently produced talented and promising students. He expressed hope that the institution would continue to set new benchmarks in education, sports and other co-curricular activities. Wishing the students a bright future, he encouraged them to move ahead with hard work, dedication and a positive mindset.The minister further said that development works worth Rs 2 crore had been completed in the Dadhol and Padyalgal gram panchayats through various departments, while several other projects were scheduled to commence shortly.Earlier, Dharmani honoured meritorious students from Government Senior Secondary School, Dadhol; Government Central Primary School, Dadhol; Government High School, Gahar; and Government High School, Chandoh, by presenting them with prizes.
