headline: Haryana Home Guards mock air raid drill tests emergency response
content: The Haryana Home Guards and Civil Defence Department conducted a mock air raid exercise at the Mini Secretariat complex in Sirsa on Friday to assess the preparedness of various departments to deal with emergency situations.The exercise aimed to ensure public safety during air attacks, provide prompt medical assistance to the injured and assess coordination among rescue and emergency response teams.A simulated airstrike scenario was created in which a building was shown as damaged, with 10 people reported injured. Of them, six were shifted to hospital by ambulance, while the remaining four received first aid at the spot.During the drill, the Civil Defence team practised rescuing people trapped on the first floor of the damaged building. Volunteers from the District Red Cross Society provided immediate first aid to the injured, while the Health Department demonstrated the procedure for shifting seriously injured people to hospital.The Fire Department also conducted a demonstration to control a possible fire following an airstrike and prevent further damage.Officials from different departments worked together to assess their emergency response, rescue arrangements and ability to use available resources effectively. The exercise also focused on implementing standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the safe evacuation of victims and the protection of life and property. The drill helped assess inter-departmental coordination and the readiness of various agencies to undertake rescue and relief operations during a disaster.DSP Subhash, Civil Defence Superintendent Sunil Kumar, District Red Cross Society Assistant Secretary Gurmeet Saini, Fire Officer Mohit, Fire In-charge Rishi Sihag, Sukhdev Singh Dhillon from the Scouts and Medical Officer Randhir Singh were among those present. Officials, staff members and volunteers from various departments also participated in the exercise.

headline: Kurukshetra to ban entry of heavy vehicles during International Gita Mahotsav
content: Ahead of the International Gita Mahotsav (IGM), the Kurukshetra police have decided to completely ban the entry of heavy vehicles into the city and divert them to alternative routes to avoid traffic congestion and ensure the smooth movement of vehicles.According to the Kurukshetra police, the restrictions will remain in force from December 3 to 25. The Mahotsav will be celebrated on the banks of Brahma Sarovar from December 5 to 25.Last year, the entry of heavy vehicles into the city was restricted from 8 am to 11 pm. This year, however, the police have decided to impose a complete ban during the stipulated period to prevent any untoward incident.Kurukshetra police spokesperson Naresh Kumar said a large number of tourists and devotees visit the city during the International Gita Mahotsav, resulting in a heavy flow of traffic. Keeping this in view, the police have decided to divert heavy vehicles through alternative routes. A traffic advisory has been issued to ensure smooth movement of vehicles and will remain in force till December 25.“A route diversion plan has been prepared and directions have been issued for its strict implementation to ensure smooth traffic movement during the Mahotsav. Checkpoints will be set up at all entry points to the city. Tourists and devotees arriving in their private vehicles will be advised not to park along roads and use only designated parking areas,” he said.As per the traffic advisory, heavy vehicles coming from Pehowa and Patiala and heading towards Saharanpur, Haridwar, Uttarakhand and Yamunanagar will have to take the Pehowa bypass, NH-152, NH-152D and Ismailabad bypass, and proceed through villages Thol, Kurdi, Nalvi and Shahabad to reach their destinations.Heavy vehicles coming from Kaithal district and heading towards Saharanpur, Haridwar, Uttar Pradesh, Indri, Ladwa and Yamunanagar will have to take the route via Pehowa, Dhand, Kaithal-Dhand, and villages Kaul, Nigdhu, Nilokheri and Indri, instead of passing through Kurukshetra.Vehicles coming from Patiala and other parts of Punjab towards Pehowa and heading for Karnal, Panipat, Sonepat and further towards Uttar Pradesh and Delhi via Kurukshetra can reach their destinations through Pehowa, Dhand and Kaul.Heavy vehicles travelling from the Yamunanagar side towards Pehowa and Punjab via Ladwa and Kurukshetra will be diverted through Ladwa, Babain, Shahabad, Nalvi, Thol and Ismailabad.Similarly, vehicles travelling from Yamunanagar district towards Kaithal and beyond will have to take the route via Ladwa, Indri, Bhadason and Nilokheri.

headline: JNV assault case: Six students suspended, principal served notice
content: The Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, Reckong Peo, has suspended six students accused of assaulting a Class IX student, following the circulation of a video of the incident.Kinnaur Deputy Commissioner Sonakshi Tomar said the administration had issued a show-cause notice to the school principal.Tomar said the victim was a Class IX student, while the six students accused of beating him were studying in Classes XI and XII. Following the emergence of the video, the administration sent teams from the Education Department and the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) to the school to conduct a preliminary inquiry. “A detailed investigation is underway. The victim and his parents are being counselled,” she said.Tomar said the role of the school management and the responsibility of teachers and wardens on duty at the time of the incident were also being examined. The inquiry would establish which teachers and wardens were present and the circumstances in which the assault took place.The administration is also investigating how students were allowed to carry mobile phones into the school premises. Some other irregularities have also come to light, including students leaving the school campus without permission. She said the police had also started investigations into the possible reasons behind the assault.The incident came to light when a video of the assault surfaced on social media yesterday. According to the officials, the incident took place around two months ago.

headline: Haryana government tightens norms for college teachers seeking PhD permission
content: The state government has tightened the procedure for granting permission to government college teachers to pursue PhD programmes, directing principals to thoroughly scrutinise applications and verify supporting documents before forwarding them to the directorate.The move follows observations that several cases seeking permission for higher studies by professors, associate professors and assistant professors were being forwarded to the directorate without proper scrutiny at the college level. The department has noted that incomplete documentation and failure to examine the applicable government instructions were resulting in unnecessary correspondence and delays in processing such applications.In a communication issued recently to principals of all government colleges across the state, the Department of Higher Education, Haryana, directed them to ensure that applications were examined in accordance with the Finance Department’s instructions issued on November 9 and 22, 2022, before being sent to the directorate.The department has also made it clear that incomplete cases or applications forwarded without proper scrutiny and requisite documents will not be entertained and may be returned to the colleges concerned for rectification.“To streamline the process, the directorate has also introduced a common proforma for government college teaching faculty seeking prior permission to take admission to a PhD programme or a no objection certificate (NOC) to pursue or continue research work by the college teaching faculty,” said sources.The sources further said the prescribed format required applicants to furnish comprehensive details about their employment and academic pursuits, including designation, employee ID, pay level, employment status, date of initial appointment in government service and present place of posting. They will also have to provide details of the university, its category, the mode of PhD programme, admission and registration dates, current research status and expected date of completion.“Significantly, the applicants will have to disclose whether their coursework, research activities or other academic requirements necessitate their presence during college working hours. They will also be required to specify attendance requirements, coursework schedules, leave requirements, if any, and the likely impact of their studies on teaching, examination and administrative responsibilities,” the sources added.The prescribed checklist also seeks details of any previous permission or NOC granted by an earlier employer or competent authority. The applicants will have to attach relevant documents, including joining reports, PhD admission and registration certificates, university regulations, coursework schedules, completion or exemption certificates and progress reports from their supervisers or universities, wherever applicable.The proforma provides for verification of the particulars by the principal against available service records before recommending the case to the competent authority.“The Finance Department’s November 2022 instructions provide different approval mechanisms depending on the employee’s group and the nature of higher studies. Under the November 22 instructions, permission for higher studies by Group A officers is considered and granted by the Finance Department on the recommendations of the concerned Administrative Department,” the sources pointed out.The Higher Education Department has directed all government college principals to ensure strict compliance with the revised procedure.“The directions aim to streamline the permission process, ensure uniformity and transparency in processing applications, and enforce compliance with Finance Department guidelines. The department also intends to ensure that the teachers’ academic pursuits do not adversely affect teaching, examination and administrative responsibilities while eliminating delays caused by incomplete documentation and procedural lapses.” said a college principal.

headline: Govt to launch hospital management info system
content: The Himachal Pradesh Government is set to implement the Hospital Management Information System (HMIS), which will provide access to patients’ complete medical reports at the click of a button.Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu emphasised the state government’s commitment to providing specialised healthcare services to the people and strengthening health institutions by ensuring adequate manpower, modern technology and improved infrastructure.Sukhu highlighted the introduction of HMIS and the strengthening of IT-related manpower in medical institutions as measures to enhance transparency, efficiency and accountability in the healthcare system. He assured that the government was continuously working to modernise health institutions, improve patient care and ensure that the benefits of technological advancements reached people throughout the state.The HMIS system aims to enhance efficiency, transparency and accountability in hospital administration and healthcare delivery. It will facilitate digitisation and effective management of patient records, hospital-related information, data entry, report generation and other essential institutional processes.To ensure the effective implementation of HMIS, the government has approved the engagement of 661 data entry operators/junior office assistants. The government has also decided to fill up 561 posts of junior office assistants (IT)/data entry operators in the Directorate of Medical Education and various government medical colleges.Additionally, 100 posts of data entry operator will be filled in other health institutions of the state.

headline: Holistic student assessment and hostel redesign: Education ministry committee lists suggestions for stude
content: Mumbai: Reducing the emphasis on Cumulative Performance Index (CPI), higher educational institutions should move towards more holistic assessment of students by giving recognition to co-curricular engagement through credits and evaluations. Hostel spaces should incorporate quiet ‘mind spaces’, green areas for informal conversations, open talking zones and ambient elements such as soft corridor music. Wardens should be expected to share meals and coffee with students, participate in games and cultural activities, and engage in ‘corridor conversations’ to understand their concerns.These are some of the recommendations made by a committee constituted by the Union ministry of education to strengthen student well-being and prevent suicides in HEIs. The committee, chaired by National Educational Technology Forum chairman Prof Anil Sahasrabudhe, has proposed a shift from a reactive approach to student suicides to a preventive model involving continuous monitoring, early identification of distress and stronger community support systems. Having dedicated 24x7 wellness professionals and training selected students as peer ambassadors to identify early signs of emotional distress among classmates are also some of its recommendations.Acknowledging the lack of personal connection as a key contributor to distress in hostel settings, the committee has emphasised humanising hostel life through micro-level community interventions, such as celebrating birthdays and personal milestones, recognising family events and achievements, and encouraging shared rituals and social interactions among students. “Regular informal interactions, such as icebreakers, cultural nights, themed evenings and floor-level gatherings, can help reduce anonymity and foster a sense of belonging…” mentioned the report. The committee also has released a self-assessment checklist for institutions.The committee has also recommended developing a secure, confidential, institute-wide early warning system to identify students at risk, incorporating hostel indicators, faculty observations and counselling data. Mental health screening should begin in the first year and continue across programmes as a routine practice for all students, like regular health check-ups, which would help in reducing stigma, enabling early detection and timely intervention, emphasised the report.Since the ministry issued its student well-being framework in July 2023, at least 54 student suicides or unnatural deaths have been reported across IITs, including 18 in the last 12 months alone, said Dheeraj Singh, Founder, Global IIT Alumni Support Group and IIT-Kanpur alumnus, who obtained the June 2026 report through RTI. “Institutions cannot claim to have prioritised student wellbeing simply because they have committees, counsellors and policies on paper. The real test is whether students feel safe, heard and supported when they encounter academic pressure, discrimination, isolation or institutional indifference. The Sahasrabudhe Committee has once again produced recommendations, but where is the honest accounting of why existing safeguards have failed? We cannot keep responding to student deaths with new frameworks while avoiding scrutiny of institutional practices. headline: Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri appointed as J&K’s Advocate General after two year gap
content: Srinagar Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri was on Friday (November 27, 2026) appointed as the Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir, eight months after the J&K government forwarded the proposal to Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha for his approval. The J&K government has been without an Advocate General for more than two years. “In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 79 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 (Act No. 34 of 2019) and in supersession of notification S.O. No. 07 of 2019 dated 01-11-2019, the Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir is pleased to appoint Mr. Syed Faisal Qadri, Senior Advocate, as Advocate General for the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir,” reads the official order. Mr. Qadri is a designated senior advocate with over 20 years of practice. With over 100 reported judgments, Mr. Faisal earned a name for himself by pleading cases of both private and government institutions in the J&K High Court and in the Supreme Court. The Omar Abdullah government in April this year had proposed the names for the post. The appointment, however, came after the J&K High Court heard a public interest litigation (PIL) petition on November 5 regarding the vacant post. Senior Additional Advocate General Monika Kohli had apprised the Division Bench, comprising Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajnesh Oswal, that the appointment would be made within a period of one month. Relief for Abdullah government It is a major relief for Chief Minister Omar Abdullah whose government was pursuing many pending policy matters before the J&K High Court in the past two years. Mr. Abdullah’s party National Conference (NC) had won the Assembly elections in 2024, but remained without an Advocate General since then. In 2019, senior advocate D.C. Raina was appointed as the Advocate General of J&K. He, later, tendered his resignation in October 2024.

headline: Cane price row: Farmers give Haryana Govt December 1 deadline
content: The sugarcane price agitation in Haryana intensified on Friday, with farmers demanding Rs 600 per quintal and giving the state government a December 1 deadline to accept their demand. They warned of a major confrontation, including a gherao of Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini's residence in Kurukshetra on December 2, if the government failed to announce a satisfactory decision.The ultimatum was issued at a mahapanchayat organised at Bhadson village under the banner of Haryana Sanjha Sangharsh Morcha, a newly formed platform of farmer unions. Leaders Gurnam Singh Charuni and Rattan Mann called upon farmers to reach the Chief Minister's residence in large numbers.Farmers have been protesting outside the Bhadson sugar mill for the past eight days. Similar demonstrations are underway outside sugar mills in Karnal, Kurukshetra, Ambala, Yamunanagar and other districts. The agitation has also started affecting crushing operations at several mills.The farmers have rejected the state government's decision to increase the State Advised Price (SAP) from Rs 415 per quintal in the 2025-26 crushing season to Rs 430 for the current season. They have also turned down the announced price of Rs 450 per quintal for 2027-28, insisting that nothing below Rs 600 would be acceptable.Addressing the gathering, Charuni said an increase of just Rs 15 per quintal was inadequate and accused the government of delaying a decision on farmers' demand. He asserted that the agitation would continue until the government announced a satisfactory price.Charuni also warned that farmer organisations would campaign against the BJP in Uttar Pradesh during the Assembly elections if their demand remained unaddressed.Mann accused the government of adopting an anti-farmer approach and said cultivators were being forced to take to the streets to secure remunerative prices for their produce. He urged farmers to demonstrate their strength in Kurukshetra on December 2.

headline: Art exhibition in Amritsar showcases state’s artistic diversity
content: Bringing together the traditional artistic vocabulary of Punjab and contemporary forms of creative expression, the KT Punjab State Art Exhibition 2026 has emerged as a vibrant showcase of the region’s diverse artistic talent. Featuring 130 selected artworks across paintings, drawings, sculptures, graphics, digital art and photography, the exhibition offers a glimpse into how artists are interpreting Punjab’s cultural heritage while exploring new artistic languages.Organised by KT Kala Museum, the exhibition was inaugurated by Dr Amardeep Gupta, Principal, DAV College, Amritsar. The artworks, contributed by artists from across Punjab, will remain on display at the museum until December 4.What makes the exhibition particularly significant is its effort to bring established professionals and emerging artists onto a common platform. Divided into two categories - Professional Artists (above 25 years) and Budding Artists (16-25 years) - the exhibition also features a special invitees’ section showcasing works by senior artists, allowing younger participants to engage with experienced practitioners and learn from their artistic journeys.According to the museum Director Brajesh Jolly, the response from the artistic community was overwhelming, with more than 600 entries received. An expert jury shortlisted 130 works for display. The organisers also announced 25 cash awards, including 10 awards of Rs 10,000 each for professional artists and 15 awards of Rs 5,000 each for emerging artists.Addressing the gathering, Dr Gupta appreciated KT Kala Museum’s sustained efforts to nurture artistic talent and provide a platform for creative expression. He noted that the diversity of works reflected the potential of Punjab’s artistic community.A catalogue featuring selected artworks was also released on the occasion. Secretary Rajesh Raina highlighted the exhibition’s growing contribution to the state’s art scene and commitment to supporting artists and encouraging creativity across generations.With participation from senior artists, students from various universities and art enthusiasts, the exhibition goes beyond displaying artworks. It creates a meeting ground for different generations and artistic traditions.

headline: Guhla schools adopt quiz culture to sharpen young minds in Haryana
content: Moving beyond conventional classroom teaching, government schools in Guhla block of Kaithal district have taken a step towards nurturing young talent by organising inter-school quiz competitions for students of classes IX and XII. At present, competitions are being held between students of classes IX and X and in coming days students of classes XI and XII will participate in it.The initiative, which has witnessed enthusiastic participation from all 18 senior secondary schools in the block, aims to provide students with a platform to showcase their knowledge, sharpen their intellectual abilities and develop a spirit of healthy competition. The first round of the quiz competitions, covering five subjects –English, math, social science, science and Hindi, has started and in the second round private schools will also participate.As per the authorities, the quiz competitions are providing students with an opportunity to assess their subject knowledge, respond to questions under competitive conditions and learn from experiences.“The purpose behind this step is to bring out the hidden potential of students and encourage them to participate confidently in academic activities. The students are motivated to explore subjects beyond their syllabus, develop curiosity and improve their general awareness,” said Manish Yadav, SDM Guhla, a brain behind this initiative.He said the students were showing enthusiasm towards the competitions. He emphasised the primary objective was not merely to identify winners but to provide every student with an opportunity to discover and demonstrate their abilities.Yadav further stressed that such activities could play an important role in building confidence among students and motivating them to perform better academically. “Healthy competition encourages children to prepare and think independently. It also helps them recognise their strengths and identify areas where they need improvement,” he added.Narender Dixit, Block Education Officer (BEO), Guhla, echoed the same sentiments, observing that such initiatives could bring a positive transformation in the functioning and learning environment of government schools. He said providing the students with opportunities to participate in activities beyond routine classroom teaching was essential for their overall development.He claimed that this step had also encouraged the teachers for these quiz competitions as they wanted their students to emerge victorious.Dixit also highlighted that quiz competitions helped the students improve their ability to think quickly, recall information, communicate effectively and work under pressure. Such experiences, he added, could contribute significantly to developing confidence and a positive attitude towards learning.He said after the successful completion of the first phase, private schools in the block would also be invited to participate in the second phase of the competitions. “This will bring government and private school students onto a common platform, giving them an opportunity to interact, compete and learn from one another,” he added.Sunil Dutt, Block Coordinator of Foundational Literacy & Numeracy (FLN) under the Nipun Haryana Mission, has also been associated with the initiative, helping facilitate its implementation at the ground level. “The interaction with the students and teachers during the competitions has encouraged them to participate in such academic activities,” he added.For the students, the competitions are also an opportunity to gain experience in facing questions before an audience, responding within a limited time and handling the excitement and pressure associated with competitive events. “We were limited to our classroom study and now this step has provided us an opportunity to think beyond our subject. Inter-school quiz competitions boost our confidence to express ourselves,” said a student of Class X of Guhla Government School.Teachers, meanwhile, see such activities as an effective way to identify the students’ interests, encourage classroom participation and make the teaching-learning process more dynamic.

headline: Haryana Govt makes one-month notice must for teachers’ foreign visits
content: Government college teachers in Haryana will now face stricter scrutiny while seeking permission for foreign visits, with the Department of Higher Education making it mandatory to submit a detailed set of documents, including an affidavit, passport copy, service particulars and leave details.In a communication issued on Friday, the Director General of Higher Education directed principals of government colleges to thoroughly examine applications and verify all relevant documents before forwarding them to the Directorate with their recommendations.The directions apply to professors, associate professors and assistant professors working in government colleges across the state. According to sources, the department has observed that several applications for personal and official foreign visits were being forwarded without proper scrutiny of the Finance Department's instructions and with incomplete documentation, leading to unnecessary correspondence and delays.The department has asked principals to ensure compliance with the Finance Department's guidelines issued on October 15, 2025. Teachers will now have to submit their applications at least one month before the proposed date of foreign travel, except in unavoidable circumstances.Under the prescribed checklist, applicants must provide details of their initial joining in government service and appointment to their present post. They must also declare whether any complaint or inquiry is pending against them.Other mandatory documents include an original affidavit in the prescribed format, a copy of the office identity card mentioning its number and date of issue, and an attested copy of the Indian passport. Applicants must clearly specify the proposed duration and period of their stay abroad.The guidelines also make it clear that government employees can leave the country only after obtaining prior permission for foreign travel and sanction of leave from the competent authority. No post-facto approval will be granted.Any violation of the prescribed procedure may invite disciplinary action under the Haryana Civil Services (Punishment and Appeal) Rules, 2016.The department has directed all principals to strictly follow the instructions and ensure that applications are forwarded to the Directorate only after proper verification and scrutiny.

headline: Rohtak PGIMS to train doctors in advanced respiratory care
content: The Department of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine (PCCM) at Pt BD Sharma Post Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS), Rohtak, will organise its 10th annual Continuing Medical Education (CME) programme on November 28 and 29, focusing on advances in respiratory and critical care medicine.The two-day academic event aims to improve the understanding and management of respiratory emergencies and critically ill patients. It will bring together senior faculty members and medical experts from across the country, along with healthcare professionals, for scientific lectures, interactive discussions, hands-on workshops and poster presentations, said Dr Dhruva Chaudhry, Head of the PCCM Department, on Friday.“A major highlight of the first day will be hands-on workshops on Non-Invasive Ventilation (NIV), High-Flow Nasal Oxygen Therapy (HFNO) and invasive mechanical ventilation. These workshops will provide practical exposure to modern respiratory support techniques used for patients with severe breathing difficulties and respiratory failure. They will help strengthen doctors’ skills in providing timely and appropriate critical care,” he said. Dr Chaudhry said the second day would feature expert lectures and scientific sessions on important advances, emerging challenges and evidence-based approaches in pulmonary and critical care medicine. The programme would also include poster presentations to encourage research, innovation and the exchange of clinical experiences among participants.“Respiratory illnesses remain a major cause of hospitalisation and critical illness. Advances in respiratory support and critical care techniques play an important role in improving patient outcomes.Through this CME, the department aims to promote academic excellence, enhance clinical preparedness and encourage collaboration among healthcare professionals,” he said. Dr Chaudhry said the event reflected PGIMS Rohtak’s continued commitment to medical education and improving care for patients with respiratory and critical illnesses.

headline: 4 child marriages stopped in Sirsa, girls aged between 11 & 15 rescued
content: In a major action against child marriage, four minor girls aged between 11 and 15 were saved from early marriages in Sirsa district of Haryana. The weddings were scheduled for Friday but were stopped following timely intervention by the Selfie With Daughter Foundation and the district administration.Among the girls, one was 15 years old and belonged to Santnagar, while the other three aged 14, 12 and 11, were from Faggu village.In the Santnagar case, the 15-year-old girl was taken by her aunt to Damdama village for marriage. Most of the wedding rituals had been completed, and preparations for the traditional wedding rounds were underway when the foundation received information about the marriage.Foundation founder Sunil Jaglan informed the administration. A team comprising officials from the Rania Block Development and Panchayat Office, the village panchayat and the police reached the spot and stopped the wedding.The girl, whose parents live separately, was taken into protective care. After spending a day at a protection home, she was handed over to her family.At Faggu village, the foundation’s team also intervened to stop the marriages of three minor girls. While the male family members reportedly left when the team arrived, the women were counselled about the legal consequences of child marriage. The administration subsequently helped stop the weddings.In both cases, the families and village panchayats submitted affidavits before the Child Welfare Committee, promising not to marry off the girls before they turned 18. The committee will monitor both cases.The Selfie With Daughter Foundation has been running a village-level campaign for the past three months to make Sirsa a child marriage-free district. Jaglan said the organisation was spreading awareness about the harmful effects and legal consequences of child marriage.He also pointed out that the post of Child Marriage Prohibition Officer in Sirsa had been vacant for the past year. The foundation has written to the state and Central governments seeking an appointment.Child Welfare Committee chairman Madan said action was taken as per the rules and the girls were handed over to their families after affidavits were submitted.

headline: District administration pledges to make Sirsa free from child marriage
content: The district administration will continue its campaign to make Sirsa free from child marriage, Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) Arpit Sangal said on Friday. Addressing an awareness programme at Chaudhary Devi Lal University (CDLU) on Child Marriage-Free India Day, Sangal said child marriage adversely affected girls’ physical and mental development and destroyed their dreams and future.He said the administration was working in coordination with anganwadi workers, ASHA workers, village sarpanches, school principals and gram secretaries to spread awareness in rural areas. He warned that strict legal action would be taken against those involved in child marriage. The ADC also appreciated Sunil Jaglan, founder of the Selfie With Daughter Foundation, for his efforts to make Sirsa free from the practice. He stressed that public participation was essential to eliminate this social evil.CDLU Vice-Chancellor Prof Vijay Kumar urged young people to raise their voices against child marriage and contribute towards bringing positive social change. BJP district president Yatindra Singh said every member of society must take responsibility for preventing child marriages and ensuring that girls were not deprived of their rights.Sunil Jaglan said laws alone could not eliminate the practice unless accompanied by a change in people’s mindset. He stressed that every girl deserved education, equal opportunities and the freedom to fulfil her dreams.The programme also featured a documentary, awareness tableaux and a street play highlighting the harmful effects of child marriage and its impact on society. In the tableau competition, Shah Satnam Ji Girls’ School secured the first position, followed by GD Goenka School in second place and DAV School, Ding, in third place.The District Legal Services Authority organised a legal awareness camp at Maharaja Agrasen Girls Senior Secondary School under the 100-day Child Marriage-Free India campaign. Students were educated about child marriage laws, legal marriage age, children’s rights and the importance of education. They were also informed about NALSA’s free legal aid helpline, 15100.

headline: Cabinet clears bills to raise 50% Lok Sabha seats across states, freeze delimitation till 2051
content: NEW DELHI: Amid growing support for the delimitation bills with support of DMK, the Sharad Pawar-led NCP faction and YSRCP, the Union Cabinet cleared the legislation to increase Lok Sabha’s maximum strength from 550 to 850 by proposing a uniform increase of 50% in constituencies in every state, while freezing any fresh delimitation to revise the numbers till 2051.Government circulated the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill for delimitation and operationalisation of women’s quota from 2029, and another bill for setting up a Delimitation Commission to MPs on Friday as numbers appeared to be falling in place for Parliament’s nod to the government’s centrepiece legislation, only months after a united opposition had voted down the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill with similar objectives.A third bill will seek to facilitate an increase in the number of seats in the UTs of Delhi, J&K and Puducherry which have assemblies.“The objective of the present bill (Constitution amendment) is to give immediate effect to one-third reservation for women, including women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, in Lok Sabha and legislative assemblies of states and Union Territories, through a delimitation exercise. Such delimitation shall provide for an increase of 50% in the number of seats in Lok Sabha and assemblies of states and Union Territories over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation,” the Constitution amendment bill said.The new bill is different from its previous version in making an explicit constitutional provision to assuage the concerns of parties like DMK and NCP (SP) of any diminishment of the existing share of states in LS, opening the path for them to junk their past opposition and join the BJP-led NDA in backing the Constitution amendment bill that needs support of two-thirds MPs for passage.For the simultaneous pursuit of the two objectives, the bills have been predicated on the numbers of two Census exercises. For determining the respective share of states in LS, the 1971 Census -- the one which was used for determining the current share of states in LS, is being retained. However, for redrawing the boundaries of LS constituencies in states, the 2011 Census numbers will be used: something which frees the government of the need to wait for the findings of the enumeration currently underway.In the proposed maximum strength of 850 in Lok Sabha, 815 will be for states and 35 for UTs with assemblies -- Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu and Kashmir. The real overall strength of Lok Sabha is likely to be around 816. LS currently has a strength of 543 against the maximum possible strength of 550.The government is set to table the bills, key for implementation of women’s quota, in Lok Sabha on Nov 30. The bills are more granular in their legal casing as well as political outreach, while keeping the same broad agenda of rolling out one-third reservation for women in LS and state assemblies from 2029, when the next national election is due.Signalling his likely change of stand, DMK chief M K Stalin said the share of Tamil Nadu, which has 39 LS seats, should not fall below its current 7.18%, and the existing proportion of parliamentary representation among states, as determined on the basis of the 1971 Census and frozen earlier, must remain unchanged for another 25 years. The government had offered to meet the condition in April itself and the new bill addresses both of Stalin’s points.NCP(SP) was more categorical, with its senior functionary Jitendra Awhad quoting party boss Sharad Pawar to say that the party, an INDIA bloc constituent, had decided to support delimitation.DMK’s 22 MPs in LS, NCP (SP)’s eight and four of YSR Congress, which is also expected to support, takes NDA’s strength in the House to 355. With 360 needed for the bills’ passage in the House, which has three vacancies, NDA appears all but certain to cross the threshold amid indications from the governing alliance that some more MPs may either abstain or even back it.Attention is also focused on whether the speaker will give his ruling on the legality of the split in TMC which has resulted in 20 MPs belonging to Mamata Banerjee’s party aligning themselves with NDA. A favourable ruling will free them from any legal encumbrance in taking an independent course.The Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, which will amend eight Articles of the Constitution, also proposes to raise the ceiling on the size of a state assembly from 500 to 650. It is being explicitly done for Uttar Pradesh as its assembly, the largest in the country, currently has 403 members.Passage of the bill will also provide the government an effective plank to showcase its pro-women credentials in the run-up to a crucial round of state elections, and government is likely to build political capital out of it by getting endorsement from assemblies of states where BJP and its allies are in office.With a new delimitation bill being tabled, government will withdraw the earlier legislation which is still pending in Lok Sabha.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Fuel shortage leaves fire station struggling during emergency
content: Imagine calling up a fire station during an emergency and being told that there’s no diesel in fire engines. That is precisely what happened a few days ago when a massive forest fire broke out in Nichar block of Kinnaur district.“I called up the fire station at Bhabanagar and asked them to send a fire engine to control the fire. To my shock, I was told there was no diesel in the fire engines,” said RP Negi, a resident of Chagaon gram panchayat, where the fire was particularly intense.Negi claimed that several others who called the fire station were given the same response. He said they later learnt that the fire station procured fuel from a nearby petrol station, which had stopped supplying it due to pending payments.Admitting that there had been a shortage of fuel for the fire engine, Nichar SDM Neha Negi said fuel was arranged for the vehicles on a priority basis through the disaster management mechanism. “There may have been some pending payments on the part of the Fire Department, due to which it was facing problems. The Deputy Commissioner, Kinnaur, however, sorted out the issue and arranged the fuel,” she said.The SDM added that the Deputy Commissioner would soon convene a meeting to review the preparedness of emergency services and ensure that they remained operational whenever required.Negi, however, questioned the purpose of maintaining fire stations and deploying staff if the vehicles could not be used during emergencies. “What if the fire had reached human habitations when we called for help? Who would have been responsible if there had been any loss of life or property?” he asked.

headline: Fire destroys over 200 hectares of forest cover in Kinnaur dist
content: A forest fire that has been raging in Nichar block of the Kinnaur district since November 23 has destroyed over 200 hectares of forest cover and caused extensive damage to wildlife.According to SDM Neha Negi, the fire has been brought under control near human habitations but continues to rage at higher altitudes, where difficult terrain and absence of road connectivity are hampering firefighting operations. Several firefighters have sustained injuries while trying to douse the blaze. A woman also died after a burning branch fell on the car she was travelling in, causing the driver to lose control.The fire broke out at two locations, Urni and Chagaon. While it has been brought under control in Urni, efforts are underway to douse the blaze at Chagaon. Such was the intensity of the fire that several agencies, including the Army and the ITBP, had to be pressed into service.Kinnaur DFO Arvind Kumar said the fire broke out at a high altitude, where the slopes were extremely steep, making it difficult for firefighting teams to reach the affected areas. “The fire broke out at a high altitude and the slopes are very steep. So, it is taking time to control it,” he said, adding that the teams were now close to bringing it under control.Forest officials suspect that human activity was behind the fire. An FIR has been registered against unidentified persons. “There is a practice of setting fire to grasslands to encourage the growth of fresh grass for cattle fodder. Someone set fire to a grassland, from where it spread uncontrollably,” the DFO said.He said strong winds at high altitude had further fanned the flames. “The slopes are extremely steep and there is no motorable road to transport water tankers to the affected areas. Also, rocks are falling from the heights. This made the operation very challenging. Several firefighters were also injured while trying to control the blaze,” he said. The fire has caused extensive damage to forest wealth and wildlife. The extent of the damage will be assessed once it is completely doused.Meanwhile, RP Negi, a local, attributed the vulnerability of the area to prolonged dry conditions caused by the lack of rainfall. “There’s also a possibility of fire being triggered by sparks from the high-tension power lines crossing the area. It’s very dry here and the electricity board should ensure proper maintenance of the area,” he said.

headline: Proving ability over disability, Amritsar shuttler Ranjit Singh dreams big, makes it big
content: For Amritsar’s para-badminton player Ranjit Singh, every medal represents a battle won beyond the badminton court.Adding another remarkable chapter to his sporting journey, the international para shuttler clinched three gold medals at the state-level Khedan Watan Punjab Diyan competitions held at Guru Nanak Stadium, Ludhiana.Ranjit demonstrated his versatility and competitive strength by finishing first in all three events — men’s singles, men’s doubles and mixed doubles — bringing laurels to Amritsar and reaffirming his place among Punjab’s promising para-badminton talents.His latest achievement is particularly significant, given the challenges he has overcome to reach the international sporting arena. Ranjit, who has lower-limb disability caused by polio, has been pursuing badminton since he was a teen. Supported by Pingalwara initially, he pursued his education while nurturing a passion for badminton while also training with professional badminton academy through his own efforts.His journey towards professional sport began with considerable limitations, including a lack of specialised equipment. In 2023, he participated in his first national para-badminton competition using a borrowed wheelchair.However, determination and support from well-wishers helped him progress to the international circuit.In October 2025, Ranjit made an impressive international debut at the Abia Para Badminton International Championship in Nigeria, winning three bronze medals in the WS-1 category across singles, doubles and mixed doubles’ events. His performance brought him recognition and opened doors to further international opportunities. The Mohali District Red Cross Society also extended financial assistance and provided specialised sports equipment to support his participation in international tournaments.Despite these milestones, access to advanced training facilities, specialised equipment and financial support remains a challenge for para athletes.Ranjit creditedhis latest success to his coaches, doubles partners and family, acknowledging their contribution to his sporting journey.

headline: Himachal: Experts converge at Shoolini varsity for summit on AI
content: Shoolini Business School, Shoolini University, is hosting the first International Summit on “The Age of Polycrisis, AI and Climate Anomalies in Alliance with Viksit Bharat 2047” from November 27 and 28, bringing together academicians, researchers and industry experts from India and abroad.Prof VV Gopal, president and Dean, Shoolini Business School, and Dr Nikhil Bhardwaj, Director, Doctoral Studies, are convening the summit.The two-day summit is being be held in a hybrid mode, with delegates participating both on campus and online.Prof VV Gopal said the summit would examine how two major forces shaping the contemporary world—artificial intelligence and increasingly erratic climate patterns—could be understood together rather than in isolation, and what their combined implications would be for India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.Delegates and keynote speakers are expected to participate from IIT-Jammu, Panjab University, the University of Delhi and other leading institutions in India and abroad.

headline: 2,000 Himachal Road Transport Corporation pensioners protest over dues
content: Around 2,000 Himachal Road Transport Corporation (HRTC) pensioners from across the state staged a protest outside the corporation’s headquarters here today, accusing the state government and the HRTC management of a discriminatory attitude and of delaying payment of their dues. They demanded that the government grant for pension payments be raised from Rs 20 crore to Rs 25 crore a month to ensure timely disbursement.The pensioners expressed resentment that they had been given only 3 per cent dearness allowance (DA), that too after a delay of nearly 18 months and without arrears. They said they were entitled to an 8 per cent DA hike and demanded the release of the remaining 5 per cent instalment, along with arrears of the 3 per cent DA.Their other demands include release of pensions to employees who retired after July 2025 and payment of gratuity and leave encashment to those who retired after September 2024. They also sought pension arrears at par with state government pensioners, monthly settlement of medical bills and revision of the pensions of those who retired before January 1, 2016, as per the pay matrix. They further demanded two increments for conductors after 20 years of service, with a corresponding revision of their pensions.The pensioners’ committee warned that if the government and the corporation management failed to take a positive and time-bound decision, the agitation would be intensified.

headline: Power cuts in Punjab expose AAP’s ‘zero-bill’ boasts: BJP’s Kewal Dhillon
content: Punjab is facing severe, unscheduled winter power cuts, affecting households, farmers, traders and industrial units, Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon has said. His remarks came a day after Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann conducted public surveys in Moga and highlighted the state government’s claim of zero electricity bills.Dhillon said the shutdown of six thermal power plant units across the state had reduced 2,260 MW of generation capacity. He claimed that against an average demand of 9,000 MW, total power generation was barely 3,500 MW.“Free electricity means nothing when there is no electricity in the wires. Even in peak winter, towns, villages and markets across Ludhiana, Amritsar and Sunam are facing three-to-four-hour outages every evening,” he said.Highlighting the impact on different sectors, Dhillon said steel and manufacturing units in Ludhiana were suffering production losses due to sudden voltage fluctuations and interruptions. Farmers, he added, were facing prolonged power cuts on agricultural feeders during the crucial wheat irrigation period.He also blamed poor maintenance planning for the shutdown of units at Ropar, Goindwal, Rajpura and Talwandi Sabo.Warning of a potential power crisis in the coming years, Dhillon said engineers had projected a deficit of 2,500 MW by the summer of 2027, citing the absence of capacity addition under the Mann government.He demanded immediate corrective measures instead of what he described as the government’s focus on advertisements.“The AAP government has pushed Punjab’s power sector into complete paralysis,” Dhillon said.

headline: Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation
content: New Delhi The amendments in the Constitution being proposed in a Bill approved by the Union Cabinet propose to continue the existing proportion of strength in the Lok Sabha of individual States for another 25 years, until 2051. The existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats was based on the population distribution recorded in the 1971 Census, and determined in the delimitation of 1973. That distribution continued for 50 years for the reason that a readjustment would adversely affect the proportion of States that stabilised population. Population stability was a stated objective of the Indian government. That link between population stability and Lok Sabha share has been removed in the proposed 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill. The freeze on proportion will continue for another 25 years, as a special measure to accommodate 33 per cent seats for women.

headline: Playground on paper, shops, police post in reality at Gohana govt school
content: The Haryana Human Rights Commission (HHRC) has taken serious note of the lack of adequate playground facilities for 862 students of Government Senior Secondary School (GSSS), Gohana, after an inquiry revealed that 28 shops, a police post and a government primary school were functioning on different portions of land recorded as a playground.Chairperson Justice Lalit Batra observed that 27 kanals and 10 marlas (around 3.44 acres) of land had been recorded in the revenue records as being in the possession of the Education Department since 1976-77. However, students have been unable to access adequate and uninterrupted sports facilities.The Commission has directed the Principal Secretary, School Education Department, to coordinate with the Deputy Commissioner and District Education Officer (DEO), Sonepat, and explain why the land has not been made fully available to students. A detailed report has been sought at least a week before the next hearing on February 10, 2027.During the hearing, DEO Naveen Gulia appeared through video conferencing and submitted an inquiry report dated November 2, along with photographs, a site map and relevant documents. The Deputy Commissioner's report was also placed before the Commission.The inquiry revealed that the school, which has been functioning since 1905, operates from two campuses separated by a public street passing through a market. The senior secondary wing (Classes IX to XII) has 581 students, while the middle wing (Classes VI to VIII) has 281 students.The inspection found 28 shops, a police post and Government Primary School, Mughalpura, on portions of the playground land. The primary school occupies around 430 square yards. Shopkeepers told the inspection team that rent collected from the shops was deposited with the SDM's office in Gohana.The playground's entrance key is reportedly with the Municipal Committee, while the SDM periodically grants permission for circuses, religious functions, jagrans and other events.The DEO suggested that students could use the ground after obtaining permission from the authorities concerned. Questioning this arrangement, the Commission observed that recording the Education Department's possession of the land in revenue documents was meaningless if students could not use it for educational and sporting activities.The Commission also directed that its order be placed on record in 133 connected complaints filed separately by children through individual postcards.

headline: Livestock contests draw crowds at National Dairy Mela in Karnal
content: Livestock of different breeds took centre stage on the second day of the three-day National Dairy Mela and Agri Expo at ICAR-NDRI on Friday, with beauty and milking competitions emerging as major attractions.The competitions brought together progressive livestock breeders and dairy farmers from across the region, showcasing superior animal breeds, their dairy potential and the efforts of farmers engaged in animal husbandry.Farmers from different states participated enthusiastically in the event. From well-built buffaloes and high-yielding milch cattle to prized goats, participants brought their best animals, hoping to earn recognition for their efforts in breeding, feeding and caring for them.For many farmers, the NDRI Dairy Mela has become an annual event. They said it provided an opportunity to meet fellow livestock owners, learn about different breeds, exchange experiences and gain information about the latest developments in dairy farming.While appreciating the arrangements and facilities provided by the NDRI administration, participating farmers raised concerns over the prize money. They said the first prize of Rs 21,000 should be increased, given the considerable expenditure involved in transporting animals and bringing supporting staff.“The prize money should be increased as it is a national-level mela. The input costs have increased manifold,” said Prem Singh, a farmer from Dadupur, who has been bringing his livestock to the event for several years.Raj Kumar of Sector 33, Karnal, who brought Sahiwal cattle for the competition, said higher prize money would encourage more livestock owners, particularly newcomers, to participate. Other participants, including Rishipal and Joginder Singh, also pointed out that private livestock fairs offered more attractive prizes and urged the NDRI administration to review the existing prize structure.On the occasion, ICAR-NDRI Director Dr Dheer Singh said a special session had been organised to promote women’s leadership, entrepreneurship and capacity building. The session focused on export readiness and capacity building under women’s leadership through integrated supply systems, value chains and stronger market linkages. Ruchita Bansal, Managing Director of Izhar Group, Gurugram, attended the session as the chief guest.Animals competed in various categories, highlighting the efforts of livestock owners in maintaining and managing their breeds. Vijender Singh of Jhajjar won the Murrah buffalo (two-toothed) category, while Hawa Singh of Pahuwala secured the first position in the Murrah heifer-calf (Katdi) category. Rajbir Singh of Dadupur won the HF crossbreed (two-toothed) category, and Vijay Pal of Rohtak topped the Tharparkar category.A paneer-making competition was also held, with participants demonstrating their traditional dairy-processing skills and expertise in value addition. Pinki of Manglora won the first prize, followed by Babita of the same village in second place and Rajbala of Ghogripur in third place.

headline: Himachal: Palampur varsity’s Dr Sood earns coveted vet fellowship
content: Chaudhary Sarwan Kumar Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya (CSKHPKV), Palampur, has achieved another significant academic distinction as Dr (Prof) Pankaj Sood, Dean, Dr GC Negi College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, has been conferred a prestigious fellowship by the Society for Veterinary Sciences and Biotechnology during its XIII Annual Convention and National Conference held recently at the Veterinary University, Patna.The distinction assumes special significance as the Society confers only two fellowships annually, making it a highly competitive and selective recognition. Adding to this achievement, Dr Sood's candidature was adjudged ‘Outstanding – Rank 1’ by the Society's screening committee.RD Nazeem, IAS, Vice-Chancellor, and Dr Avninder Sharma, Registrar of the university, congratulated Dr Sood on this remarkable accomplishment, which reflects the exceptional merit of his academic and professional contributions. They observed that such prestigious recognitions not only acknowledge an individual's dedication and contributions but also enhance the visibility, reputation and institutional standing of the university at the national and international levels.The fellowship recognises excellence and outstanding contributions to teaching, research and public outreach in the field of animal reproduction and biotechnology. With this recognition, Dr Sood has added another significant milestone to his academic career, taking the total number of fellowships conferred upon him to six.

headline: Govt reconstitutes Cabinet sub-panel to issue white paper on HP’s finances
content: The state government has reconstituted the Cabinet sub-committee headed by Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri to issue a white paper on the financial position of the state.The others in the all-important eight-member committee include Industries Minister Harshwardhan Chauhan, Revenue Minister Jagat Singh Negi, Education Minister Rohit Thakur, Rural Development Minister Anirudh Singh, Public Works Minister Vikramaditya Singh and Town and Country Planning (TCP) Minister Rajesh Dharmani. Secretary (Finance) will be the Member Secretary.The debate on the state’s finances and the BJP’s allegations of corruption saw the Congress and Opposition spar over the financial health of the state, with the two blaming each other for the present situation. As such, the move by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu to bring out a white paper is being viewed as an attempt to bring before the public the real picture and what he claims is the failure of the BJP to protect the state’s interest and to make efforts towards revenue generation.The notification for the reconstitution of the committee was issued by the Chief Secretary. The notification for the constitution of the earlier committee for the same task had been issued on May 12, 2023. Following this, Mukesh Agnihotri had presented the white paper on the financial position of the state in the Vidhan Sabha on September 21, 2023, less than a year after the Congress came to power in Himachal. The document reflected on the state’s finances during the five-year BJP regime headed by the then Chief Minister Jai Ram Thakur.Now, the state government has reconstituted the committee to present the picture three years after the previous document had been presented by the Deputy CM in the Vidhan Sabha. The move follows the BJP moving an adjournment motion in the recently concluded winter session of the Vidhan Sabha at Dharamsala to discuss the issue of corruption and what the Opposition termed as ‘Himachal on sale’.While presenting the earlier white paper in the Vidhan Sabha three years back, Agnihotri had hit out at the BJP for landing Himachal in a financial mess.Accusing the BJP regime of poor fiscal management, he had said the Congress inherited liabilities to the tune of Rs 92,774 crore when it assumed power in December 2022. This, he had remarked, had resulted in a debt of Rs 1.02 lakh on every newborn child.He had quoted that when the BJP came to power in 2017-18, the state’s debt was Rs 47,906 crore with an annual increase of 12 per cent (Rs 28,725 crore) which rose to Rs 76,631 crore in 2023-24.

headline: Himachal’s Dharamsala among 100 venues for Fit India’s cycling milestone
content: Dharamsala is among 100 locations across the country selected to host the 100th edition of the Fit India Movement’s ‘Sundays on Cycle’ initiative on November 29, celebrating Olympic values and promoting a culture of fitness.The event will be organised jointly by the Union Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, the Fit India Movement, the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA). Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya will lead the national-level celebrations at Pimpri-Chinchwad in Pune, while thousands of fitness enthusiasts, sportspersons and prominent personalities are expected to participate at 100 locations across the country.In Dharamsala, the programme will be held at the SAI’s National Centre of Excellence (NCOE), beginning at 8 am. Participants have been requested to report at the venue by 7 am.JP Shani, Assistant Director, SAI NCOE-Dharamsala, said the 100th edition marked a significant milestone for the initiative, which has evolved into a nationwide public movement since its launch in December 2024.He said the event would feature a cycle rally, fitness activities, cultural performances and interactive sessions with prominent sportspersons and fitness enthusiasts.Themed ‘Pedalling Towards India’s Olympic Dream’, the milestone edition will celebrate the Olympic values of excellence, respect and friendship. The initiative also seeks to strengthen India’s aspirations of hosting the Olympic Games in the future while encouraging citizens to adopt healthier lifestyles.Shani said the initiative aimed not only to promote physical fitness but also to spread awareness about environmental conservation and encourage greater community participation. He appealed to residents, cycling enthusiasts, youngsters and sportspersons to participate in the event in large numbers.The 100th edition will also feature activities across districts throughout the country, bringing citizens together to celebrate India’s sporting aspirations and the Olympic movement.

headline: Haryana Government issues retirement order for Sudhir Rajpal, extension uncertain
content: The Haryana Government has issued the retirement order for 1990-batch IAS officer Sudhir Rajpal, who is due to superannuate on November 30, fuelling speculation that the Centre may not approve the state's proposal for a three-month extension.The state government had sought the extension earlier this month, citing the ongoing preparation of the Budget and the possibility of disruption if the charge of the Finance Department was handed over to another officer. Rajpal currently holds the charge of Additional Chief Secretary (Finance) as well as Additional Chief Secretary (Home).Sources said the state had also cited relevant rules in its communication to the Centre to justify the proposed extension. However, no response has been received so far.The retirement order, signed by Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi, states that “the Governor is pleased to order that Rajpal shall retire from the IAS in the afternoon of November 30 on attaining the age of superannuation”.Rajpal is, therefore, likely to retire at the end of the month, although the Centre's decision could come even on his last working day.This is the second recent instance of the state issuing a retirement order shortly before an IAS officer's superannuation. A similar order was issued 48 hours before the retirement of 1992-batch officer Arun Kumar Gupta in September. Bureaucratic sources had then maintained that such orders were generally issued on the afternoon of an officer's last working day.Interestingly, no retirement order was issued for Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi on his last working day, even though approval for his extension came only in the evening.Sources said the Centre was of the view that an extension could be permitted only in the case of the Chief Secretary. However, the position will become clear by November 30, Rajpal's scheduled retirement date.Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini will be on an official tour of Europe to promote the upcoming Happening Haryana summit. Bureaucratic sources said the issuance of the retirement order made approval of the extension appear unlikely.

headline: Missing land records leave Una farmers in limbo
content: Farmers of Lalsingi village near Una city on Friday staged a protest under the banner of the ‘Kisan Yoddha-Sardar Rurka Singh Memorial Committee’ against the non-availability of village land records with the Revenue Department for decades, which has led to a number of revenue problems.Sardar Rurka Singh, born in 1899 in Panjawar village of Una district, was a prominent farmer leader and freedom activist known for organising small and marginal farmers to fight for land and revenue reforms. After Independence, he mobilised small, marginal and landless farmers across the district to press for revenue law reforms, playing a key role in the transfer of ownership to landless tenants. He died on March 15, 1962, while leading a farmers’ rally at Jhalera, where his statue stands at the road junction. The committee pursues his goals and has been fighting for the farmers.The farmer activists said that since the reorganisation of Punjab and the transfer of Una to Himachal Pradesh, the land records of some villages, including Lalsingi, have been missing. As a result, the settlement and consolidation of village land has not been done. They pointed to a communication dated May 13, 2008, from the Financial Commissioner-cum-Secretary (Revenue), which said that as the land record maps (‘lattha’ and ‘musavi’) for Lalsingi were not available, landowners would be given possession on the basis of their present occupation and the available Jamabandi records.The committee members said farmers had approached the Himachal Pradesh High Court against the orders and that the court had stayed further proceedings, with the stay continuing. In the present situation, they alleged, the land mafia was encroaching on private and public village land, as ownership was not defined. They said they had repeatedly asked the district administration to protect farmers from the mafia, but the administration and the police had refused to intervene.The activists warned that they would be forced to start a dharna if the stalemate continued and they were not given ownership of their land on the basis of the Jamabandi records at the earliest.

headline: Mewat Engineering College in Nuh, Haryana, gets a sports boost
content: Students of Mewat Engineering College in Nuh are set to get better sports facilities, with the Mewat Development Agency (MDA) repairing playgrounds and providing equipment on the campus.Deputy Commissioner and MDA Chief Executive Officer Akhil Pilani said cricket, basketball, badminton and volleyball grounds were being repaired. Most of the sports equipment had reached the college, while table tennis equipment was expected soon.Stressing the need to develop sports, Pilani said, “Sports facilities are very important across our education infrastructure.”He said the agency was working to provide modern facilities to students and strengthen the infrastructure of educational institutions in the region. The works at the college would help in the all-round development of students, nurture sporting talent and improve the academic environment.The facilities will also give students better opportunities to practise sports of their choice. MDA Deputy Chief Executive Officer Ashok Kumar and an Executive Engineer of Panchayati Raj recently inspected the works.The boost is not limited to sports. The agency has approved about Rs 20 lakh for books for the college library, for which the tender process is under way. Efforts are also on to install 50 solar streetlights through the Haryana Renewable Energy Development Agency (HAREDA). Work to convert the existing solar power plant into a hybrid system has begun.The attention comes in the wake of a protest lasting over 40 days at the Haryana Waqf Board-run college at Palla village, where the students and staff had raised concerns over basic infrastructure, faculty shortage and service matters. The dharna is now over.Set up in 2010, the college has over 700 students. Cracked walls and exposed iron rods at the hostel, home to around 150 students, had raised fears for their safety.The unrest built up around the beginning of October. The students put forward a 16-point charter seeking more faculty, better laboratories and library, safe drinking water, uninterrupted power, medical facilities, transport and building repairs. The staff took up delayed salaries, pending dearness allowance and stalled promotions.As the days passed, the students and staff marched about 2 km from the Nuh bus stand to the Mini-Secretariat and submitted a memorandum addressed to the Deputy Commissioner.The agitation later escalated into a hunger strike. A meeting with district and Waqf Board officials on November 4 ended without agreement. Talks with Cabinet Minister Rao Narbir Singh also failed to break the deadlock, while Nuh MLA Aftab Ahmed took up the matter with Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini.The students ended their 13-day hunger strike on November 11 after the Waqf Board gave a written assurance, accepting their demands in principle. The dharna, which continued thereafter, has since been called off.Waqf Board Administrator Zakir Hussain had earlier maintained that the buildings were safe and only the plaster was peeling. He had said Rs 8 lakh had been released for repairs, besides Rs 80 lakh to clear three months’ salaries. According to him, the board had spent about Rs 62 crore on the college.While the sports, library and power works promise some relief, the MDA’s latest announcement does not mention hostel repairs, drinking water, faculty appointments or staff dues. With the dharna over, the test now lies in delivering on these basics.

headline: Chaudhary Devi Lal University Sirsa professor gets Fulbright-Nehru fellowship
content: Professor Priyanka Siwach of the Department of Biotechnology at Chaudhary Devi Lal University (CDLU), Sirsa, has been selected for the prestigious Fulbright-Nehru Academic and Professional Excellence Fellowship for 2026-27.She will undertake a six-month research assignment at the University of Arizona, USA, from January to July 2027, in collaboration with Professor Judith K Brown, an expert in plant virology and insect-vector biology.Her research will focus on cotton leaf curl disease, which has been affecting cotton cultivation in Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan. The disease is transmitted by whiteflies, which are increasingly developing resistance to commonly used insecticides.The study will explore RNA interference (RNAi), a biotechnology-based approach that could help develop RNA-based alternatives to chemical pesticides and promote sustainable crop protection.“Cotton leaf curl disease continues to pose a serious challenge to cotton cultivation in north-western India. Our research aims to understand the interactions between viruses, whiteflies and plants and explore RNA-based approaches for better pest and disease management. The collaboration will also help us examine the potential of these technologies under Indian agricultural conditions,” Prof Siwach said.With more than 25 years of teaching and research experience, Prof Siwach has published over 85 research papers, authored or edited five books and guided nine PhD scholars. She has also served as Dean Research and Head of the Department of Biotechnology at CDLU.CDLU Vice-Chancellor Prof Vijay Kumar congratulated her, saying such achievements strengthened the university''s research culture. Registrar Dr Sunil Kumar and other faculty members also congratulated her.The fellowship would provide an opportunity to advance research and strengthen academic collaboration between India and the US, Dr Sunil said.

headline: Man injured in Fazilka encounter; 3 pistols seized
content: An accused wanted in a firing case was injured in an encounter with the police while allegedly attempting to evade arrest in the Jalalabad area on Friday evening. The police seized a Glock pistol, a .30-bore pistol and a country-made pistol from his possession.Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit Singh said the accused, Manpreet Singh, a resident of Chak Kathgarh village under the Amir Khas police station, had allegedly opened fire on his cousin on November 25, leaving him injured.A case was registered against him on Friday under Sections 109 and 3(5) of the BNS and Section 25 of the Arms Act at the Jalalabad (City) police station.A police party chased the accused to arrest him. He allegedly opened fire at the police personnel to escape arrest, with one of the bullets hitting the police vehicle this evening. The police retaliated, during which the accused sustained a bullet injury in the leg.Injured Manpreet Singh was subsequently shifted to the Civil Hospital, Jalalabad, for treatment.The SSP said the accused had three previous criminal cases registered against him. He said he was out on bail in a criminal case.

headline: Fake silver sheets bring a bitter shine to sweet treats
content: Hyderabad: Aluminium sheets and metal flakes are allegedly being passed off as edible silver foil to decorate sweets and paan, prompting health experts to warn consumers about the risks of repeated exposure to non-food-grade metals.Recent inspections by food safety teams found aluminium being used as a cheaper alternative to silver foil. Silver foil, commonly used for decoration, has no nutritional value and must meet FSSAI standards, which mandate a minimum purity of 99.9% for edible silver.Recently, four manufacturing units allegedly producing fake edible silver foil were busted in Charminar and Falaknuma, with their owners arrested. Officials seized 49 bundles of fake silver leaves and 10 kg of aluminium flakes allegedly supplied to sweet shops, bakeries and paan outlets across Telangana.“These units supplied fake silver coatings and flakes to sweet shops, bakeries, and paan outlets across Telangana. We also found 1 kg of fake, aluminium-coated sugar balls meant to be sold to bakeries as cake toppings,” an official said.Shopkeepers are required to ensure that foil is food-grade and sourced from authorised manufacturers. However, cheaper alternatives, including aluminium foil and metal-coated sheets, are allegedly being used to cut costs.Dr Naresh Gundapuneni, internal medicine specialist at Renova Hospitals, said counterfeit silver foil could be made from industrial aluminium or scrap metal, potentially containing lead, cadmium and nickel.“Prolonged exposure to these contaminants could damage the brain, nervous system, kidneys and liver, while excess aluminium may affect bone health. Nickel contamination can trigger allergic reactions, and coarse metallic flakes could irritate the stomach, causing nausea, cramps and constipation,” he said.Studies have linked aluminium accumulation in patients with kidney failure to dialysis-related bone disease and brain damage. The European Union has not authorised silver (E174) as a food additive since 2016, citing insufficient safety data, although its use is permitted in India under FSSAI norms.Experts also flagged concerns about repeated exposure potentially disturbing gut microbes. Such effects may develop gradually, making it difficult to identify their source.Even genuine silver offers no health benefits. Dr Venkat Kumar Nani, an internal medicine consultant, said edible silver foil was generally safe when genuine, hygienically manufactured and compliant with the 99.9% purity standard. However, he advised avoiding unnecessary coatings.Experts recommend choosing sweets without metallic decoration, opting for natural garnishes such as saffron and pistachios, and using glass containers to heat or store food, particularly acidic items.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news.
