headline: Mandi’s surveillance hit as 212 of 276 CCTV cameras go defunct
content: The city’s surveillance network has suffered a major setback with 212 of the 276 CCTV cameras installed across Mandi remaining non-functional for a prolonged period.With only 64 cameras currently operational, surveillance across several public places like Khaliyar, Paddal, Sanyard, Jail Road, Mangvain and main Mandi town has weakened, raising concerns over public safety and the city’s ability to monitor suspicious activities.The CCTV network was installed to deter criminal activities, keep watch over sensitive locations and assist police in investigations. However, the widespread breakdown of cameras has significantly compromised the monitoring system, leaving several areas without effective surveillance coverage.According to police officials, the cameras have become dysfunctional due to multiple reasons, including technical faults, damaged cables, monkey menace, interference by residents and damage caused by heavy vehicles to hanging wires.Additional Superintendent of Police, Mandi, Abhimanyu Verma, said monkey-related damage to wiring was among the major reasons behind the malfunctioning of cameras. Cables passing through residential properties are also sometimes damaged by local residents, while wires hanging along roads get caught in heavy vehicles and are broken. Damage to poles and infrastructure during disasters has further affected the surveillance network.He suggested that installing CCTV cameras based on Wi-Fi connectivity could help reduce dependence on vulnerable cable networks and minimise recurring damage. He also stressed the need for the Municipal Corporation to conduct a joint survey with the police to identify key locations for installing new cameras, with surveillance control preferably placed under the Police Department.Mandi SP Vinod Kumar also confirmed that more than 200 CCTV cameras were dysfunctional. He said the authorities concerned had been informed and asked to take necessary steps towards restoring the surveillance network.Meanwhile, the Mandi Municipal Corporation has initiated efforts to repair and reactivate the defunct cameras, an exercise estimated to cost around Rs 45 lakh.Mayor Suman Thakur said the issue had been discussed with the Superintendent of Police, during which the extent of the damage and technical problems affecting the network came to light. She said around Rs 45 lakh would be required to restore approximately 212 cameras.The Municipal Corporation is working to arrange the required funds and plans to submit a proposal to the state government seeking financial assistance. A detailed project proposal will also be forwarded to the Central Government to explore additional funding for strengthening the city’s surveillance infrastructure.The corporation aims to restore CCTV coverage across the city to improve security at public places and strengthen monitoring of drug-related activities, antisocial elements and criminal incidents.The prolonged failure of a large part of the surveillance network has also affected the availability of CCTV footage, which often proves crucial in identifying suspects, tracing incidents and gathering evidence in cases of theft, assault and other crimes.Residents are now awaiting the restoration of the cameras, as a functional citywide surveillance system remains an important component of public safety and effective policing.

headline: Haryana Panchayats Dept loses Rs 100 cr in cyber fraud
content: In a major cyber fraud involving Haryana's Development and Panchayats Department, Rs 100.86 crore has allegedly been siphoned off through 1,827 unauthorised transactions involving 523 bank accounts, prompting the state government to order a comprehensive cyber security assessment of all schemes involving financial disbursements.This is the second major banking fraud involving the department this year. In February, it lost nearly Rs 90 crore in the Rs 657-crore IDFC First Bank-AU Small Finance Bank scam.According to the department's communication to the Haryana Police, separate zero-balance accounts have been opened with Punjab National Bank (PNB) for gram panchayats, panchayat samitis and zila parishads. The actual funds are maintained in a Central nodal account, while individual institutions are assigned spending limits after government approval.The payment system is operated digitally through software managed by Panchkula-based Austere System Pvt Ltd. Payments are authorised through joint digital signatures of the sarpanch and gram sachiv, or designated officers in the case of other panchayati raj institutions. Instructions are transmitted directly to PNB through a server-to-server arrangement without physical visits to bank branches.Initially, seven suspicious transactions worth Rs 74.70 lakh, carried out on November 14 and 15, came under the scanner. The department told the police that no authorised government officer or public representative had approved these payments.An FIR was registered on November 19 for forgery, cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal conspiracy. Investigators traced the money from these transactions to an account of The Soft Safari Toys Pvt Ltd. Two suspects, Mukesh Kumar and Utpal Kant, were apprehended from Bihar.Bank records and an Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) report subsequently revealed that Rs 1.98 crore had been credited to an RBL Bank account of Neelkanth Traders as the first layer of transactions. Account holders Sanjay Kumar and Abhishek were arrested from Yamunanagar, Tarun Kumar from Panipat, bank manager-level official Gurjinder Singh from Karnal and Gagandeep Arora from Lucknow. Investigators found that some accused had allegedly accepted commissions for allowing their accounts to be used.Meanwhile, Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi on Friday ordered a comprehensive cyber security assessment of government schemes to identify vulnerabilities and prevent unauthorised transactions. The IT, Electronics and Communications Department, National Informatics Centre and other departments will prepare a list of schemes involving financial disbursements.Multidisciplinary committees comprising technology experts, NIC representatives, finance officials and senior administrative officers will examine security gaps. Rastogi also directed daily reconciliation of financial transactions.Finance Secretary Sudhir Rajpal said the state's financial operations exceeded Rs 2 lakh crore, making strong technological safeguards and continuous vigilance essential.

headline: Haryana Govt clears Rs 455-cr elevated corridor to ease Gurugram traffic
content: In a major push to ease traffic congestion in Gurugram, the Haryana Government has approved a Rs 455.22-crore six-lane elevated corridor between Hero Honda Chowk and Umang Bhardwaj Chowk.The 2.24-km corridor will be constructed along National Highway-352W and is expected to improve connectivity towards Jhajjar and the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal (KMP) Expressway.The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) will execute the long-pending project as a deposit work of the Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority (GMDA).The approval follows the submission of a revised proposal by GMDA. Its Chief Executive Officer, Dushmant Kumar Behera, reviewed the project after assuming charge and took up the matter on priority.Earlier, on October 1, it was reported that the state government had entrusted the project to GMDA, which was asked to prepare a fresh detailed project report. Following consultations with its engineering officials, the authority recommended that NHAI execute the elevated corridor.The project aims to segregate local and through traffic, increase road capacity and ensure smoother movement along the busy stretch. It is expected to benefit daily commuters and vehicles travelling towards Jhajjar and the KMP Expressway.The road is an important link in Gurugram's transport network, connecting a key junction on the Delhi-Jaipur highway with the route towards Jhajjar.GMDA has already incurred an expenditure of around Rs 116.55 crore on land acquisition and shifting of utilities for the project.Behera said the government's approval was a significant step towards implementing the infrastructure project. He added that the corridor would strengthen Gurugram's road network and improve commuting convenience.However, the official statement did not specify when tenders would be floated, construction would begin or the project would be completed.

headline: Potato rates nearly halve, Haryana Farmers seek relief
content: Potato prices have nearly halved at the Pipli grain market, leaving farmers disappointed, with traders attributing the decline to ample stocks and stable demand.Farmers have urged the Haryana Government to raise the secured price under the Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana (BBY) from Rs 600 to Rs 900 a quintal to protect them from losses.The Pipli grain market is one of the major markets for potato produce. Earlier, the crop fetched Rs 1,200 to Rs 1,500 a quintal, but on Friday, prices ranged from Rs 650 to Rs 1,050 a quintal.Gaurav Kumar, a potato farmer, said, “The crop has not been fetching remunerative prices for the past three years, due to which I have reduced the cultivation area from over 35 acres to 26 acres this year.“Even this year, the prices have been disappointing. Since old stocks are easily available at cheaper rates, traders are not offering better prices for the new stock, forcing farmers to sell at lower prices,” he added.“After seeing some good levels, potato prices have been declining gradually. Farmers are unlikely to reap any profit this year. The government should increase the secured price under the Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana as well,” he said.The secured price of potato under the scheme is Rs 600 a quintal. The government compensates farmers if their produce is sold below the secured price declared by it. The compensation covers the difference between the secured price and the average sale price.Rakesh Bains, a potato farmer and spokesperson for the Bhartiya Kisan Union (Charuni), said, “Farmers have been demanding that the government increase the secured price under the scheme from Rs 600 to at least Rs 900 a quintal to protect them from losses.“The arrivals have started at the grain markets, but crop verification is pending. To avoid any disputes later, the government should get the verification done through patwaris at the earliest,” he added.Dharmpal Mathana, a potato trader at the Pipli grain market, said, “On Friday, red-skinned potatoes fetched Rs 650-850 a quintal, while white-skinned potatoes fetched Rs 700-1,050 a quintal. There are adequate old stocks in Haryana, UP and Punjab, due to which the early variety is not fetching higher prices. Arrivals are expected to increase in the coming days. However, a major fall in prices is unlikely at this point.”Meanwhile, Kurukshetra District Horticulture Officer Shivendu Pratap Singh Solanki said arrivals at grain markets had started and no major disease in the crop had been reported so far.“Farmers have been advised to register their crop on the MFMB portal and submit the required application to the horticulture office for physical verification to avail themselves of benefits under the BBY. GPS coordinates and photographs of the crop are mandatory for verification,” he added.

headline: Major fire engulfs textile factory in Panipat
content: A major fire broke out at a shoddy yarn manufacturing unit on Kabri Road in Panipat around midnight, causing extensive damage to the factory and its machinery. The intensity of the blaze was such that additional fire engines had to be summoned from National Fertilisers Limited (NFL) and Sonepat to bring it under control.The fire broke out at Kapoor Wooltex factory and spread rapidly, engulfing the premises within a short span. Thick clouds of black smoke rose into the sky, drawing a large number of people to the spot. They alerted the Fire Department, following which fire engines were rushed to the factory.However, by the time the fire brigade reached the site, the flames had assumed alarming proportions due to the presence of highly inflammable material inside the unit.The fire engulfed the entire factory, damaging raw material, rag-cutting machines, waste polyester, the building, electric panels, solar panels and other equipment.Amit Kumar, leading fireman with the Fire Department, said fire engines from Panipat were pressed into service immediately after receiving information about the incident. However, given the intensity of the blaze, additional fire engines were called from Sonepat and NFL to assist in the firefighting operation.He said the presence of highly inflammable material had contributed to the rapid spread of the fire, resulting in extensive damage to the factory.The exact cause of the fire was yet to be ascertained. The extent of the financial loss was also being assessed.No loss of life was reported in the incident, Kumar added.

headline: Punjab scraps GMADA’s Rs 15K-crore fundraising tender
content: The Punjab Government has initiated the process of cancelling the controversial Rs 15,000-crore fundraising tender issued by the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) to raise funds through bonds, bank loans and other debt instruments.GMADA had awarded the tender to a Gujarat-based firm to arrange the funds for a fee of Rs 191.16 crore. However, the selected company insisted on an accrual-based accounting system, while GMADA follows a double-entry accounting system. Converting the existing system would take at least six months, prompting the department to decide to cancel the tender, an official said.A senior government functionary confirmed that the decision to cancel the tender was conveyed during the hearing of a public interest litigation (PIL) before a Bench headed by Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra of the Punjab and Haryana High Court today. The official said the tender could not be processed due to technical differences over the accounting system to be adopted for the proposed fundraising exercise.Meanwhile, the ED is also probing GMADA’s Rs 15,000-crore fundraising project, and several officials have already been questioned in connection with the matter.In the PIL, Jaskirat and other petitioners, represented by senior counsel Baltej Singh Sidhu along with advocates Shehbaz Thind, Himmat Singh Sidhu and Reema, objected to GMADA’s proposal to raise nearly Rs 15,000 crore through bonds, debentures, bank loans and other debt instruments.The petitioners alleged that the funds were intended to finance the state government’s populist schemes. They pointed out that the Accountant-General (Audit) had questioned the transfer and accounting of approximately Rs 6,400 crore remitted by GMADA to the state treasury. The audit report had also noted that the premature transfer of approximately Rs 927.90 crore had put pressure on GMADA’s liquidity, forcing it to rely on commercial overdrafts.The petitioners further submitted: “It was also reported that the state government sought approximately Rs 1,000 crore more from development authorities, including around Rs 300 crore from GMADA, while the PSPCL was proposing to raise nearly Rs 10,000 crore through a merchant banker. The petitioners, therefore, seek the production and examination of the complete financial and decision-making record before substantial public funds are committed and third-party rights are created.”

headline: Modi invokes Lord Murugan; BJP says Tamil Nadu govt. acted against Hindus
content: NEW DELHI Hours after the Supreme Court directed that the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam be lit on the deepathoon (stone pillar) on the Thirupparankundram hill on November 28, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday posted a message on X invoking Lord Murugan. “Vetrivel Muruganukku Arogara [Victory to Lord Murugan, bearer of the sacred spear!],” said Mr. Modi. The same message was posted in Tamil and Hindi too. Supreme Court orders Karthigai Deepam to be lit at ‘deepathoon’ on November 28; issues contempt notice Supreme Court orders Karthigai Deepam to be lit at ‘deepathoon’ on November 28; issues contempt notice Bench directs Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, DGP, Madurai District Collector, temple authorities to be present for next hearing on Dec. 15; court sees ‘pre-meditated conspiracy' between State and temple trustees Supreme Court orders Karthigai Deepam to be lit at ‘deepathoon’ on November 28; issues contempt notice storyline 1 Earlier, the BJP welcomed the Supreme Court’s directive, describing it as a major victory for devotees of Lord Murugan and accusing the Tamil Nadu Government of acting against the Hindu community. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/bharatiya-janata-party/ While hearing contempt petitions over the failure to light the Karthigai Deepam at the deepathoon, the Supreme Court observed that the chain of events indicate that the Executive authorities had acted “according to the dictates of their political bosses”. Despite a Supreme Court directive, the ceremonial lamp was lit at the traditional location on November 24, and not on the deepathoon, located near a dargah. Through a post on X, BJP president Nitin Nabin said the top court’s order was a historic victory for every devotee of Lord Murugan. “By ordering the ceremonial lamp to be lit at the Thiruparankundram deepathoon tomorrow [November 28] and pulling up Tamil Nadu authorities for acting at the dictates of their political bosses, the Hon’ble Supreme Court has thoroughly exposed the INDI Alliance government’s anti-Sanatan mindset,” he said. The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), led by Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, is a part of the INDIA bloc. “No political conspiracy can stop the sacred traditions of Bharat. May the divine blessings of Lord Murugan protect all devotees and guide them on the path of courage and righteousness. Vetri Vel! Veera Vel!,” Mr. Nabin said. At a press conference, BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia accused the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister of hating “Sanatan traditions and the Hindu community”. “This hatred is so deep that a Chief Minister who has taken oath under the Constitution of India to protect and preserve the ethos of the Constitution wilfully decided to violate it,” he alleged. Alleging that the INDIA alliance and Mr. Vijay were “hell-bent on violating the orders of the Supreme Court and hurting the sentiments of the Hindu community”, Mr. Bhatia said the “tolerant” Hindu community took the legal route and approached the top court. “It is a rap on their knuckles by the Hon’ble Supreme Court...When I say that the Constitution of India is the life and soul of our democracy, questions will be asked of leaders like Rahul Gandhi and C. Joseph Vijay. When you take an oath under this Constitution, how is it that you can even dare to violate the spirit and the provisions of this Constitution with impunity?” he said. headline: Complete development projects within stipulated time frame: Dy CM to officials
content: Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri today inspected several ongoing development works in the New Haroli area of Haroli Assembly segment, estimated at Rs 100 crore. Accompanied by officials, he toured the entire complex to assess the progress of construction work and issued instructions to complete all projects within the stipulated time frame while maintaining high quality.Agnihotri said around 40 percent of the work on the synthetic track had been completed and a target had been set to reach 60 per cent completion by December, which would include the preparation of the necessary structural base for the track. Once weather conditions become favourable, the laying of the synthetic surface would commence during the summer so that the track gets fully functional by the end of April 2027.He said the heliport, currently under construction in New Haroli would be completed by April. The entire New Haroli complex between the Swan river bridge in Rora village to the Jal Shakti Department rest house in Haroli is being developed into a modern hub equipped with modern facilities including an indoor stadium, a ground to organise fairs and festivals, a Sainik Bhawan for ex-servicemen, an Udyog Bhawan to serve as office of the Industries department, circle office of the Jal Shakti Department, he said, adding that an automated testing station for vehicles has already been completed.Agnihotri directed officials to ensure an effective and permanent drainage system throughout the complex to prevent water logging since New Haroli is situated close to the Swan. He pointed out that a ring road is also proposed to interconnect all the projects and ensure smooth movement within the complex. Additionally, a roundabout will be constructed near the Rampur bridge, leading towards Haroli, which will help improve the overall traffic management system.The Deputy Chief Minister mentioned that all projects in New Haroli were being developed in an integrated manner, ensuring that sports, social, administrative and other modern amenities are available to the public within a single complex.

headline: Experts guide school heads on AI, inclusive teaching skills in Haryana
content: Artificial Intelligence (AI), student psychology and inclusive education were key topics discussed on the second day of a five-day capacity building programme for school heads at the District Institute of Education and Training (DIET), Ding.The programme is being organised under the directions of SCERT Haryana, Gurugram, and under the guidance of Sirsa’s District Education Officer, DIET Principal Subhash Phutela and DIET in-charge Surender Singh Nunia. The second day’s sessions began with DIET subject expert Satpal Singh, who briefed the participants about the day’s training schedule and collected feedback on the activities conducted on the first day.Rajesh Kumar, Assistant Professor in the Department of Computer Applications at Lala Hansraj Phutela Law College, Sirsa, delivered a session on ‘Artificial Intelligence in Education: A New Revolution for Teachers and Administrators’.He explained how AI can improve teaching and learning, help create educational content, simplify administrative work and save time. He also introduced various AI-based tools and encouraged the school heads to use them responsibly and creatively.Daljit Singh Kalra, a retired professor and psychologist from the Haryana Higher Education Department, conducted an interactive session on ‘Understanding Human Behaviour: The Psychology behind Students’ Behaviour’.He highlighted the importance of emotional understanding, self-awareness and sensitivity in dealing with students. He said understanding students’ behaviour and psychological needs can help schools create a positive learning environment.DIET expert Dr Dalip Singh Godara spoke on inclusive education, stressing equal opportunities, respect for diversity and proper support for children with special needs. He said every child should have access to quality education without discrimination and that school heads have an important role in achieving this goal.Dr Vinod Bhattu, coordinator of the District Centre for School Leadership (DCSL), DIET, said principals, headmasters and head teachers from different schools across the district participated in the programme. The experts also answered participants’questions and emphasised the practical implementation of the concepts discussed during the sessions.The programme is being supervised by IFIC wing in-charge Naresh Narula, training programme coordinator Dr Vinod Bhattu and co-coordinator Dr Rajesh Khurana.

headline: Himachal: Pragpur NCC Officer bags prestigious commendation
content: Vivekanand Sharma, Associate NCC Officer at Government Senior Secondary School, Pragpur, Kangra, has been honoured with the prestigious Chief of the Army Staff (COAS) Commendation Card in recognition of his distinguished service and contribution to the National Cadet Corps (NCC).The commendation was announced by Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi on the eve of Army Day, January 15, 2026. It was formally presented to Sharma by Lt Col Ravinder Singh, Commanding Officer of 6 HP (I) Company NCC, Una, at a ceremony held in Una.According to the NCC unit, Sharma is the only Associate NCC Officer in the country to have received this distinction.

headline: Constitution Gaurav Rath visits 11 Ambala government schools
content: A mobile exhibition, ‘Constitution Gaurav Rath’, visited 11 government schools in Ambala as part of a special awareness campaign organised on Constitution Day on Thursday.According to the Education Department, the mobile exhibition spreads the message of the Constitution and Dr BR Ambedkar’s contribution towards its making to students, parents and rural communities across the district. The 11 schools covered were GPS Rupamajra, GMS Sarangpur, GMS Dhurkara, GSSS Balana, GPS Ladana, GSSS Jalbera, GPS Metheri Jattan, GSSS Saunda, GMSSS Police Lines, GSSS Baldev Nagar and GSSS Sultanpur.The mobile exhibition was flagged off from the District Shiksha Sadan, Ambala, by BJP district president Mandeep Rana. The Rath carried a specially designed exhibition showcasing Dr Ambedkar’s life, educational journey, struggles, ideology and contribution to the framing of the Indian Constitution. Display panels highlighted the constitutional ideals of equality, liberty, fraternity and social justice, along with important milestones in his life.A special section highlighted five significant places associated with Dr Ambedkar: his birthplace; Columbia University and London, where he pursued his education; Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur; his Mahaparinirvan site in Delhi; and Chaitya Bhoomi in Mumbai. The exhibition also covered various constitutional issues, including Article 370, and highlighted Ambedkar’s views on social equality, fraternity and the uplift of all sections of society.Before flagging off the Rath, Mandeep Rana, accompanied by other guests, visited the exhibition and appreciated the initiative. He said such campaigns provided an effective platform to take the ideals of great personalities and the message of the Constitution beyond classrooms and into the wider community.District Education Officer (DEO) Sudhir Kalra, on whose directions the exhibition was organised, said school heads had been instructed to invite village representatives, parents and members of school management committees to ensure that the campaign reached as many people as possible. A specially prepared seven-minute audio presentation on Dr Ambedkar’s life and his contribution to the making of the Constitution was also played at every stop.

headline: Two-wheeler, SUV numbers used for paddy procurement in Kaithal
content: Motorcycles, scooters and SUVs have figured in records of vehicles used to transport paddy to grain markets in Kaithal district, raising serious questions over the verification mechanism under the state government’s procurement system.A committee constituted by Deputy Commissioner Aparajita has flagged bogus vehicle registration numbers and duplicate land entries in its interim report, prompting the administration to widen the investigation.The inquiry has also revealed that paddy was reportedly brought to the Pehowa grain market in vehicles bearing two-wheeler registration numbers. Pehowa is located outside Kaithal district. The estimated financial loss to the government exchequer is yet to be assessed, though sources suspect it could run into crores.The administration has now ordered verification of vehicle registration numbers mentioned in grain market gate-pass records against CCTV footage from all mandis and procurement centres in the district.The inquiry was initiated on November 18, 2026, following directions from the Deputy Commissioner. The committee is headed by SDM Guhla and includes officials from the Agriculture, Revenue, Food and Civil Supplies departments and the Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board.35 farmers under lensIn another significant finding, the Revenue Department has submitted a list of around 35 farmers who reportedly do not own land in the villages against which they are registered on the Meri Fasal Mera Byora (MFMB) portal. Their mobile numbers were either switched off or unreachable, raising further concerns over the verification process.“We have submitted our interim report to the Deputy Commissioner. Fake vehicle registration numbers and duplicate land entries have been found. We have now started verifying gate-pass records of every grain market in the district,” said Manish Yadav, SDM Guhla, who is heading the committee.Deputy Commissioner Aparajita said the report has not yet been finalised. Action will be taken based on the facts and findings that emerge once the investigation is complete. The detailed examination of MFMB portal data and gate-pass records is expected to help establish the extent of irregularities.

headline: Tell us about your past, tell us how many youths got jobs, asks U.P. CM Yogi to Samajwadi Party
content: Lucknow Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday (November 277, 2026) hit out at the Samajwadi Party (SP) over its released manifesto and asked them to tell about the record of their alleged past misdeeds and track record. He added the BJP government has made more than twice as many appointments as were made during the seven terms of SP and the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) governments combined. Mr. Adityanath’s statement is in light of the SP manifesto released on November 26, promising over 25 lakh government jobs within five years, if elected to power in upcoming assembly polls.. Samajwadi Party releases manifesto with focus on youth, jobs and farmers storyline 1 Also read | SP, Congress alliance failed even before polls, says Yogi Adityanath https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/uttar-pradesh/sp-congress-alliance-failed-even-before-polls-says-yogi-adityanath/article71743598.ece “The pace at which appointment letters are being distributed in the state is such that Saifai Syndicate will not be able to count them. All it knows is how to count currency notes. I challenge SP president Akhilesh Yadav: if you know how to count, then count them. We would have issued nearly 9.75 lakh appointment letters by now. But you have not told us where you will get 30 lakh appointment letters from, or how many appointment letters the SP distributed during its four terms in government. Tell us about that too. Tell us what you did when you yourself were the Chief Minister. Tell us about your past, because every person in Uttar Pradesh knows it. When your past is not good, your future cannot be good either,” said Mr. Adityanath in a function where he distributed appointment letters to 1,594 candidates selected by Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC) for the Directorate of Internal Audit and Accounts. These include 201 Accountants and 1,393 Assistant Accountants. SP-Congress seat-sharing: the uneasy arithmetic of U.P.’s Opposition alliance SP-Congress seat-sharing: the uneasy arithmetic of U.P.’s Opposition alliance As the Samajwadi Party unilaterally declares five candidates after floating a 26-seat formula for Congress, old wounds, local turf wars, competing memories, and a tug-of-war over Muslim votes test the alliance in UP Analysis SP-Congress seat-sharing: the uneasy arithmetic of U.P.’s Opposition alliance storyline 1 The U.P. CM said fairness and transparency have become the defining features of the recruitment process in Uttar Pradesh, under the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government. “The proof is that during the selection process, no candidate was asked for money, no one attempted to intimidate them and no irregularity was found at any level of the process. This is the identity of new Uttar Pradesh. Today, an appointment letter is not merely a document granting a government job; it is recognition of the years of hard work, struggle and talent of young people,” he said. The U.P. CM said in the last 9.5 years the state’s youth got a new identity, confidence and faith in their future, and added process of appointments is not going to stop. “Preparations are underway to issue appointment letters to around 50,000 more youths next week, including approximately 8,000 Lekhpals and 42,000 Home Guards,” he said. Comparing the tenure of previous governments, Mr. Adityanath claimed even if we add together all the appointments made during the four terms of Samajwadi Party and three terms of the BSP, he (U.P. CM Yogi Adityanath) distributed more than twice that number of appointment letters to the youth of Uttar Pradesh. “Over the past nine and a half years, nearly 9.75 lakh youths in the state have been provided government jobs,” he said. U.P. CM accused previous SP government of corruption and extortion in recruitment process accusing SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and SP leader Shivpal Singh Yadav of collecting money for jobs. “Before 2017, the moment a job advertisement was released, ‘chacha-bhatija’ duo would set out to collect money. During that period, hardworking and deserving candidates were denied their rightful opportunities. Youth who appeared for the examination would be left behind, while someone else would receive the appointment letter. The film ‘Munna Bhai MBBS’ was a living example of the recruitment system in Uttar Pradesh at that time. In 2015-16, the topper of the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission had secured third division in High School, Intermediate, and graduation, yet topped the PCS examination and was selected for the post of SDM. He did not top the examination; he was made to top it. In such a system, the talent and future of hardworking youths were both subjected to injustice,” the U.P. CM alleged. Mr. Adityanath, further alleged, “Recently, I read a statement by a leader of Munna Bhai gang in Lucknow. It reminded me of the recruitment system during SP government’s tenure. At that time, one person would apply for an examination, another would appear for it and someone else would get the appointment. Our government has put an end to this system and provided deserving candidates opportunities based on their talent,”. The U.P. CM described the state as a center of opportunities, investment, employment and robust governance. “U.P. is no longer an ‘Upadrav Pradesh’, but has become a center of opportunities, investment, employment and governance. This new identity is giving young people new wings, while their success is giving the state a new identity,” he said. Hitting out at the Samajwadi Party over the Old Pension Scheme. “Today, the Opposition talks about providing OPS to government employees, but it should also tell us who introduced the New Pension Scheme. When we assumed office in 2017 and reviewed the accounts of employees covered under NPS and the status of the government’s contribution, we found that from 2005 to 2017, neither had the employees’ accounts been opened nor had the government deposited its contribution. A committee was constituted to rectify this situation. The government increased its contribution from 10% to 14% and made approximately ₹10,000 crore available from the budget, transferring the amount to employees’ accounts. The objective was to enable employees to use the money deposited in their accounts for their needs, their children’s education, their daughters’ marriages, housing and other requirements,” he said.

headline: Flying festival begins at Shimla’s Junga
content: The fourth edition of the Shimla Flying Festival, organised by Glide Inn, was inaugurated at Junga on Thursday by Naresh Chauhan, Principal Adviser (Media) to the Chief Minister. The three-day festival aims to promote adventure tourism in Junga and adjoining rural areas and showcase the region’s tourism potential. About 25 ‘Children of the State’ took part on the opening day and some of them also tried paragliding.Chauhan said the state government was making concerted efforts to wean youth away from drugs and promote sports. Adventure activities such as these, he said, gave youth a positive direction. The government was also working to take tourism beyond the cities to rural areas. “Paragliding at Junga has given tourists a new activity in Shimla, which would boost tourism, develop rural areas and generate direct and indirect employment for local youth,” he said.The festival is supported by the Tourism Department and the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) and seeks to promote rural and adventure tourism and the activities and products of self-help groups. Paragliding is being offered to tourists at a nominal Rs 500 during the festival. On the first day, about 12 to 15 tourists used the facility.A Hospitality Expo will also be held at the historic Ridge in Shimla from November 30 to December 3 to give wider exposure to tourism and hospitality activities. Students of Keonthal Convent School, Junga, presented a cultural programme at the inaugural function, and the Himachal Pradesh Homestay Association also took part.District Tourism Development Officer, Shimla, Jagdish Sharma spoke about the Tourism Department’s schemes and the government’s initiatives to expand tourism. Arun Rawat, Managing Director of Glide Inn and organiser of the festival, thanked the chief guest, dignitaries, participating children, tourists and all supporting departments and institutions.

headline: Dharamkot MLA skips ED summons citing civic body polls
content: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) legislator from Dharamkot Devinderjeet Singh Laddi Dhos skipped the Enforcement Directorate (ED) summons on Friday citing his political engagements in connection with the Dharamkot municipal elections scheduled for November 28.Dhos was summoned to the ED’s zonal office in Chandigarh on Friday in connection with an ongoing money laundering case linked to the alleged fraudulent acquisition and transfer of government and other properties.Dhos said he had submitted an application with the inquiry officer, seeking another date from the agency to record his statement in the case. “I have sought exemption due to my busy schedule in Dharamkot municipal council elections,” he said.The investigation, stemming from a Dharamkot police station FIR, centres on the alleged fraudulent acquisition and transfer of government, municipal corporation, market committee, and church trust properties, as well as the siphoning of more than ₹1 crore in compensation funds meant for local residents whose land in Adhraman village was acquired by the government for highway construction.

headline: Civil defence holds air raid blackout drill in Amritsar
content: A civil defence air raid blackout mock drill was conducted at Sri Guru Ramdas Urban Estate, Airport Road, at 8 pm. The exercise is being organised to assess the preparedness and operational capabilities of the civil defence system.It was conducted in accordance with the directions issued by the Punjab Government’s Department of Home Affairs (Civil Defence Branch), Chandigarh, and the instructions of the Special DGP, Punjab Home Guards, and Director, Civil Defence Department.Sharing this information, Additional Deputy Commissioner (General) Pallavi Mishra said the mock exercise was aimed to familiarise people with the air raid warning signal. During the exercise, the siren sounded in a rising and falling tone for two minutes, indicating an air raid warning.The blackout was implemented only in the area specifically designated by the Deputy Commissioner-cum-Controller, Civil Defence, Amritsar, and the District Commander, Punjab Home Guards-cum-Additional Controller, Civil Defence, Amritsar.

headline: Dera’s bid to illegally occupy municipal land thwarted
content: Acting against illegal encroachments on public property, the Estate Department of the Municipal Corporation, Amritsar (MCA), today foiled a fresh attempt by a religious dera to grab prime municipal land situated opposite Guru Ram Dass Hospital on Shaheedan Sahib Road and successfully reclaimed the site.The Estate Department carried out the action immediately on the directions of Municipal Commissioner Bikramjit Singh Shergill and Additional Commissioner Dr Jai Inder Singh.The enforcement operation was conducted under the direct supervision of MCA Secretary Sushant Bhatia and Estate Officer Dharminderjit Singh, with field execution by Inspectors Preeti Chauhan and Aman Kumar, assisted by the local police force. MC officials claimed that it was a repeat offence by the said institution. In June 2025, the dera had similarly attempted to encroach upon the same municipal plot by trying to install a tubewell, a bid that the Estate Department promptly thwarted. Taking serious note of today’s repeated violation, the officials cleared the site and issued a strict warning of immediate criminal and legal action if another encroachment attempt is made.Municipal Commissioner Bikramjit Singh Shergill: “Municipal land is public property meant for civic welfare and urban development, and any attempt to illegally occupy it will be met with zero tolerance. I have directed the Estate Department to maintain strict vigilance on this site and initiate immediate FIRs and stringent legal proceedings against anyone attempting to repeat such violations.” Additional Commissioner Dr Jai Inder Singh: “This is the second time an attempt has been made to encroach upon this specific municipal property since June 2025. Repeat offenders will not be shown any leniency, and strict statutory action will be enforced to safeguard public assets.” MCA Secretary Sushant Bhatia: “Our field teams are on high alert across all zones to protect corporation properties. We warn all encroachers to refrain from illegal activities as no individual or institution will be spared if found violating municipal laws.”

headline: Minister Aman Arora calls on investors to support Punjab’s entrepreneurs
content: Punjab has received investment proposals worth nearly Rs 2 lakh crore, with an estimated employment potential of over 6.63 lakh jobs, since March 2022, Industries and Commerce Minister Aman Arora said on Friday.Addressing the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) at Bharat Mandapam, Arora said the state had received 10,673 investment proposals between March 16, 2022, and November 10, 2026. He said the government had introduced a deemed approval provision under which applications would be treated as approved if the concerned department failed to take a decision within 45 working days.The provision is part of the FastTrack Punjab digital single window system, which brings more than 300 services from over 20 departments under one platform. The minister said the government had also constituted 24 sectoral committees to formulate the Industrial and Business Development Policy (IBDP) 2026 and sector specific policies in consultation with industry representatives.Highlighting Punjab’s industrial strength, Arora said the state had 18.12 lakh registered MSMEs, with traditional manufacturing centres such as Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Mandi Gobindgarh and Batala contributing to its industrial base.He said companies such as Tata Steel, Nestle, PepsiCo, Unilever, Cargill, Danone, Linde, Yanmar, Freudenberg, Sunjin, Toppan and Sanathan Textiles had established operations in Punjab. “The state is also looking to expand its presence in emerging sectors, including electric vehicles, automobile components, defence and aerospace, electronics, textiles, food processing, information technology, global capability centres and sports goods,” the minister said.Arora informed that Aerospace and Defence Advisory Forum was helping connect MSMEs with large buyers, while the HUNAR Punjab Portal linked industries with around 1,750 educational and training institutions for employment, internships and industrial training.Inviting investors to visit the Punjab Pavilion, he said, “I invite every investor visiting this Fair to visit the Punjab Pavilion and meet the Invest Punjab team. The Government of Punjab stands with every entrepreneur, from the smallest MSME to the largest investor.”Meanwhile, the Punjab Pavilion won the Gold Medal in the Thematic Presentation category at IITF 2026. It showcased the state’s cultural heritage alongside its industrial capabilities and technological advancements under the theme ‘Vikas aur Virasat’.Punjab Pavilion administrator Arshdeep Singh and Deputy Administrators Gurpreet Singh and Amanpreet Singh received the award at the felicitation ceremony.

headline: CM expresses happiness over coin in honour of Sobha Singh
content: Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu has expressed happiness over the decision to issue a commemorative coin of Rs 125 denomination to honour legendary artist Sobha Singh on his 125th birth anniversary.The Chief Minister said Sobha Singh was one of the most distinguished painters of the country, whose extraordinary artistic talent and remarkable contribution to Indian art had earned him a special place in the cultural history of the nation. His paintings, particularly his iconic portraits and depictions of Sikh Gurus, reflect India’s rich spiritual, cultural and artistic heritage, he added. Sukhu said Singh brought international recognition to the state through his exceptional artistic accomplishments. “His association with Andretta in Kangra district had made the place an important centre of art and culture, attracting artists, art lovers and visitors from across the country and abroad,” he said.

headline: Residents protest over rising monkey menace at Kakroi village in Sonepat
content: Enraged over the rising monkey menace, residents of Kakroi village led by Zila Parishad member Sanjay Badwasania, staged a protest at the main gate of Government School in the village on Friday.The protesting villagers demanded immediate intervention by the government and local administration and demanded that it launch a massive drive to capture these monkeys. According to the villagers, over 500 monkeys have overrun the village, disrupting daily life and posing a severe threat to public safety. The villagers alleged that a troupe of monkeys could be seen easily jumping from onr roof to another at the village. The children in the school were not safe as the monkeys jumped on the rooftops of classrooms or trees in the school.Monkeys atop the roof of Government School at Kakroi village.The villagers further said the monkeys entered the houses and damaged goods in search of food items and tore clothes and made the villagers’ life miserable.Sanjay Badwasania highlighted that the surging monkey population had led to frequent attacks, leaving several villagers injured. Expressing anger over the district administration’s inaction, Badwasnia said the villagers had complained to the officials concerned several times, yet no action had been taken on the ground.Badwasania also alleged malpractices being adopted by the private monkey-catching contractors. He alleged that these contractors caught monkeys from Sonepat city and secretly released them into nearby villages such as Badwasani, Mahlana, and Kakroi etc. Later, they caught monkeys from these villages and dumped them back into the city. He claimed this cycle was continuing intentionally so that the contractors ran brisk business and continued to make money from the government.To find a permanent solution, the Zila Parishad member urged the district administration to establish dedicated shelters for monkeys—similar to gaushalas or relocate them to distant forest areas so they couldn’t return to the residential areas.Badwasania warned that if the administration failed to start a capture drive by Monday, the protesting villagers would catch the monkeys themselves and present them as ‘gifts’ to the officials concerned. A large number of villagers participated in the demonstration, echoing the demand for swift action.

headline: No water meters, yet Nurpur consumers face steep hike
content: The Jal Shakti Department (JSD) has landed in another controversy over domestic water billing in Nurpur town after charging consumers under the faulty-water-meter category for six months, from April to September 2026, despite household connections not being equipped with water meters. The department has issued bills at the rate of Rs 444.07 per month per connection, replacing the earlier fixed monthly charge of Rs 243. The nearly 83 per cent hike has triggered resentment among urban consumers, who have questioned the rationale behind imposing a tariff prescribed for faulty meters when the town does not have a household water-metering system.Social activist Pavnesh Gupta and affected residents Harsh Kumar, Udit Gandhi, Shani Kumar, Praveen, Vivek, Hanumati and Shashikant have sought an explanation from the authorities on the applicability of the revised tariff to unmetered domestic connections.They pointed out that a Himachal Pradesh Government notification dated September 21, 2024, prescribed a monthly charge of Rs 444.07 for connections with faulty water meters. The notification introduced consumption-based charges for urban domestic consumers according to their monthly water usage. However, residents said the department had yet to install meters at household connections in Nurpur, questioning the basis for placing unmetered consumers in the faulty-meter category.The controversy has revived a long-standing dispute over urban water pricing and irregular billing. The JSD had been increasing domestic water charges by 10 per cent annually since 2005, when the monthly tariff stood at Rs 40. It had reached Rs 243 by March 2025. Under the earlier revision mechanism, the monthly charge was to increase to Rs 267.23 from April 2025 and Rs 294 from April 2026.Significantly, the department discontinued its regular billing cycle after April 2025, leaving domestic and commercial consumers without bills for several months. The Tribune had highlighted the issue in September 2026, when residents apprehended that accumulated dues could impose an additional financial burden on households. Subsequently, the department deferred outstanding bills for the 11-month period from May 2025 to March 2026 and resumed billing from April 2026, applying the faulty-meter tariff of Rs 444.07 per month.The issue has assumed significance as residents have repeatedly complained about irregular and inadequate water supply. Several households reportedly receive piped water for barely 20 to 30 minutes once a day. Consumers have questioned the justification for successive tariff increases without any corresponding improvement in the quality, regularity and reliability of supply.Promodh Mahajan, president of the Nurpur Sudhar Sabha, who has been raising the issue for more than six months, has demanded the immediate withdrawal of the faulty-meter charges until water meters are installed across the town. He has also sought restoration of the earlier billing mechanism. The sabha has demanded that the department install meters at its own expense, on the pattern followed by the State Electricity Board.Chief Engineer, JSD, Dharamshala, Deepak Garg, said the department’s September 2024 notification prescribed a monthly tariff of Rs 444.07 for connections with faulty water meters. Since no separate flat-rate tariff had been notified for unmetered connections, consumers without installed water meters were also being charged at the faulty-meter rate, he clarified.He said local JSD authorities had been directed to ensure the installation of water meters within a month so that consumers could be billed at the metered rate of Rs 14 per kilolitre of water consumed.

headline: Digvijay Chautala backs Sirsa MLA Gokul Setia in face-off with CM Saini
content: The political face-off between Sirsa MLA Gokul Setia and Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini has taken a fresh turn, with JJP leader Digvijay Chautala backing the legislator.Meanwhile, Setia has made public details of development grants received under his MLA quota in response to the CM’s questions and taken a swipe at the Municipal Council chairman.The controversy escalated on November 22 when Saini visited Sirsa for a grievance redressal meeting.Ahead of the visit, Setia wrote a letter in blood highlighting the city’s poor roads, sewerage and drinking water problems and sought to hand it over to the Chief Minister.The police detained him and took him to the Civil Lines police station. He was released only after Saini left Sirsa.During the meeting, Saini criticised Setia, saying he should not indulge in “drama”. He also pointed out that grants had been released under the MLA’s quota over the past two and a half years.In response, Setia shared details of the grants received under his MLA quota over the past two years, listing the works undertaken with the funds.He said the money was not given to him as “alms” but was part of the MLA quota available to all legislators. He also alleged that the government was still withholding payments for works sanctioned under his quota.Digvijay Chautala backed Setia, saying the government should listen to the elected representative instead of trying to suppress his voice.“Gokul Setia is an educated and capable MLA of our city. If he is raising his voice over Sirsa’s condition, the government should listen to him,” he said.Digvijay’s statement comes after Hisar MP Jai Prakash also extended support to Setia.Meanwhile, Setia took a swipe at Municipal Council Chairman Veer Shanti Swaroop.In a social media post, he wrote, “My blood was shed, but someone else is feeling the pain.” He said the chairman should have performed his duties earlier and warned him to ensure that the work was completed or be prepared for another round of criticism.The post came after the chairman began inspecting civic works following action against municipal officials and a contractor over alleged irregularities.On Friday, he inspected the damaged road from Suratgarhia Chowk to Subhash Chowk and directed the contractor to expedite repairs.

headline: Punjab youth alleges forced recruitment in Russian army, seeks rescue
content: A youth from Jalandhar, who travelled to Russia in search of a job as a driver to secure a better future for his family, has allegedly been forcibly recruited into the Russian army. He is currently stranded in Ukraine after escaping from an area under the control of the Russian military.The family of Gurpreet Singh Randhawa has alleged that he was beaten after reaching Russia and subsequently forced to join the Russian army.In an attempt to save his life, he reportedly wandered through forests for three to four days without any food or water before managing to escape and reach Ukraine.His family recently met Rajya Sabha MP Balbir Singh Seechewal and sought his intervention to ensure Gurpreet’s return to India. Seechewal said he had written to External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, urging him to intervene and take necessary steps to bring the youth back safely.Gurpreet’s sister Jaswinder Kaur said he travelled to Russia in August 2026. “Days after reaching Russia, his old passport and other documents were allegedly taken away and he was issued a new Russian passport. His mobile phone was also confiscated, completely cutting off his communication with his family,” she said.Stranded in Ukraine after escaping from army areaThe family remained worried for several weeks as they had no information about him. On October 11, Gurpreet managed to contact them and informed them that he had been brutally beaten and forcibly recruited into the Russian army before informing them about his escape to Ukraine. He also expressed fears for his life and described the difficult conditions he was facing.According to the family, Gurpreet later escaped from an area under the Russian army’s control and reached Ukraine. However, contact with him was lost again.The family subsequently came across a social media video in which he narrated his ordeal during a podcast with a YouTuber.Gurpreet’s family comprises his wife, two children and four sisters, who are anxiously awaiting his safe return.Expressing concern, Seechewal said it was unfortunate that Punjabi youth travelling abroad in search of employment and a better future were being pushed into the horrors of war. He urged youngsters not to fall prey to fraudulent agents or companies and advised them to thoroughly verify overseas employment offers and recruitment agencies before accepting jobs.

headline: Punjab Congress likely to do away with ‘one family, one ticket’ policy
content: Eyeing a return to power in the 2027 Assembly elections, the Congress is likely to do away with its “one family, one ticket” rule.As the party’s state election committee has initiated discussions on potential candidates, leaders have started questioning the viability of such a formula. They maintain that candidates’ winnability should take precedence over their family background.A senior member of the committee, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said there were situations wherein a member of a political family was already an MP while another was seeking an Assembly ticket. “The candidate’s potential to win the constituency should be the decisive factor,” the leader said.Party insiders said there were at least 10 cases involving concerns of “dynastic” politics. Several senior leaders, including Rana Gurjeet Singh, Amrinder Raja Warring, Tript Rajinder Bajwa, Sukhjinder Randhawa, Charanjit Singh Channi and Madan Lal Jalalpur, among others, are keen on fielding their family members.Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh, meanwhile, has maintained over the past few days that there was no general yardstick and that each case would be assessed individually.The statement indicates that the party could field more than one member of the same political family in the upcoming polls, provided they meet the twin criteria of winnability and public acceptability. However, the final decision rests with the party high command.There is speculation that Rana Inder Partap, an Independent MLA from Sultanpur Lodhi and son of Congress MLA Rana Gurjeet Singh, may join the party. His father said the decision rested with the leadership. Channi, too, wants to field his elder son, Navjit Singh, in the polls. He had earlier said there was no harm in giving tickets to two people from the same family.Following the announcement of the alliance between the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Congress high command has also initiated a fresh survey to assess the winnability of candidates in the changed political scenario. Special attention is being given to Assembly constituencies where there is more than one claimant.Earlier, the survey was being conducted on two fronts: the party’s position vis-a-vis its political opponents — the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), the SAD, and the BJP — and the winnability and strength of candidates in the race.The party plans to announce its first list of nearly 40 candidates in the coming weeks.“Many candidates who are expected to figure in the first list are keen that the names be put out in December or the first week of January at the latest,” a senior party leader said.

headline: Amritsar: Land demarcation in Thandi Khui deferred
content: The demarcation of a multi-crore municipal land parcel at Thandi Khui on Mall Road was postponed after teams from four departments reached the site, but could not proceed without police personnel and a duty magistrate.The exercise was initiated on the directions of Municipal Commissioner Bikramjit Singh Shergill to establish the boundaries of the civic body’s land. Teams from the Municipal Corporation, Punjab Waqf Board, Revenue Department and the Electricity Board reached the site around noon.However, officials decided against proceeding with the demarcation, citing the possibility of a dispute or confrontation in the absence of police security. The revenue official present at the site said a written request was required for deploying a duty magistrate and police personnel.During the visit, a person approached the civic officials and claimed ownership of a portion of the land. He said he had visited the office several times earlier, but could not meet the MC team and came to present his claim after seeing a notice pasted at the site.The civic officials asked him to submit documents supporting his ownership claim. They said if his claim was established through the records, action would not be taken against his portion, while proceedings against the remaining land would continue as per rules.A written communication was prepared in the presence of MC Secretary-cum-Estate Officer Sushant Bhatia, recording that officials from the four departments had reached the site on November 26 to demarcate land falling under Urban Circle-110, Mall Road, Thandi Khui, comprising khasra numbers 1193 to 1199.The letter also sought police assistance and the appointment of a duty magistrate for the next exercise, citing the possibility of a dispute at the site. The communication was handed over to the revenue official, and the demarcation will proceed once security arrangements and the magistrate’s deployment are ensured.

headline: AAP failed to keep its word given to NHM workers: BJP
content: The ongoing agitation by contractual employees under the National Health Mission (NHM) has opened another political front for the Bhagwant Mann government, with the BJP accusing the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) of reneging on its pre-election promises of regularising the contractual staff.Senior BJP leader and former Punjab BJP president Shwait Malik on Friday targeted the state government over the alleged discrimination against more than 14,000 NHM employees, turning their long-pending service demands into a larger question of political accountability.Malik said the AAP had secured public support by promising job security and regularisation to contractual employees, but had failed to deliver after coming to power. Recalling Arvind Kejriwal and Bhagwant Mann’s November 27, 2021, appearance alongside protesting employees in Mohali, he questioned the gap between the AAP’s political assurances and its subsequent administrative decisions.He also cited Mann’s March 22, 2022, announcement promising regularisation of 35,000 temporary employees.The BJP leader alleged that while the government publicised regularisation in other departments, the NHM workers continue to be excluded. He highlighted the disparity between regular nurses, who reportedly earned Rs 60,000-70,000 monthly, and contractual NHM nurses, who received just Rs 15,000-Rs 20,000 despite performing similar duties.Employees serving for 15-18 years, he said, remained deprived of regular status, gratuity, pension and health insurance.The controversy has also brought the Centre-State funding arrangement under scrutiny, with Malik accusing the Mann government of using NHM’s 60:40 funding structure to evade responsibility for regularising its workforce. Linking the employees’ agitation to public service delivery, Malik said all 236 Ayushman Arogya Kendras in Ludhiana district had remained shut for 21 days, disrupting primary healthcare, TB testing and child screenings.Politically, the issue gives the BJP an opportunity to challenge the AAP’s employment narrative while putting the state government’s handling of contractual workers under the spotlight.

headline: SAD picks Pehlwan as halqa incharge; seniority bypassed, say workers
content: Akali workers and residents of Amritsar South were in for a surprise when the SAD announced its Amritsar Urban president Surjit Singh Pehlwan as its halqa incharge, bypassing seniority.The development comes days after Pehlwan was named president SAD (Urban).It is learnt that nor the residents, neither the party workers are familiar with the face.“He is not even a resident of the constituency,” said a party worker Jaspal Singh.Amritsar South is considered the stronghold of the Akalis, with Inderbir Singh Bolaria winning the seat in a row from 2007 to 2017.After parting ways with the SAD Badal, Bolaria had contested as a Congress candidate, while the SAD fielded Talbir Singh Gill in the last elections. Gill had then defected to the AAP.On November 20, Sukhbir Singh Badal through a social media post announced that he was pleased to announce the appointment of Surjit Singh Pehlwan as the halqa incharge for the Amritsar South Assembly segment.“Pehlwan, a senior leader of the Shiromani Akali Dal, is already serving as the district president, Amritsar (Urban). I am confident that he will discharge the new responsibility with commitment and contribute effectively to enable the government to come to power,” said Badal.As the news broke, the residents and Akali workers of the Amritsar South constituency said the party had overlooked senior leaders like Avtar Singh Truckanwala and Inderjit Singh Pandori, both sitting councillors.Associated with the SAD for the past nearly four decades, Truckanwala Singh had a stint as a senior deputy mayor of the holy city, besides being the chairman of the MC’s House Tax Committee. He is serving his fourth term as a councillor of ward number 30.Earlier, he was elected the councillor from ward numbers 15, 29, and 36. Ward number 36 is still in the South constituency, while the rest of the wards now fall in the East segment.

headline: Govt to set up centre of excellence for apple cultivation with expertise from NZ
content: Horticulture Minister Jagat Singh Negi today said the state government would establish a modern centre of excellence for apple cultivation in Himachal and experts from New Zealand would provide technical support.Negi today chaired a high-level meeting here with a technical delegation of New Zealand to discuss the establishment of the centre. The minister said that the state government was committed to strengthening the horticulture sector by introducing modern technologies and increasing the income of orchardists.He said that collaboration with New Zealand would bring advanced horticultural technologies to Himachal Pradesh and help strengthen the state’s apple economy. The initiative would benefit orchardists by improving productivity, ensuring availability of quality planting material and promoting sustainable horticulture practices.“The proposed centre would provide high-quality and disease-free apple planting material developed on rootstocks. It would also facilitate the introduction of improved apple varieties, modern horticultural techniques and high-density plantation systems suited to changing climatic conditions,” he said. The centre would also serve as a dedicated training facility to help orchardists from Himachal Pradesh and other states adopt modern horticultural practices, he added.Negi said that the project was being implemented under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) scheme of the Government of India, which would provide one-time financial assistance of Rs 15 crore. Experts from New Zealand would provide technical support for the establishment, technology transfer and management of the centre, while the Himachal Pradesh Horticulture Department would provide land, infrastructure, resources and staff.The minister directed the department to expedite the establishment of the centre so that the production and distribution of high-quality apple planting material could begin from the coming year.The meeting was attended by Secretary Horticulture Sudesh Kumar Mokhta, Director Horticulture Dr Satish Sharma and other senior officials.The New Zealand delegation was led by Ishan Jayawardhana, Lead Adviser, Ministry for Primary Industries, New Zealand High Commission. Priyam Arora, Agriculture Partnership Manager, technical experts Jack Hughes, David Manketlow, Mike Nelson and Lachlan Mackay were also present at the meeting.

headline: Himachal: Palampur university equips defence personnel for life beyond uniform
content: Chaudhary Sarwan Kumar Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya (CSKHPKV), Palampur, successfully concluded a certificate course on “Protected Cultivation and Value Addition of Vegetable and Horticultural Crops” for Junior Commissioned Officers (JCOs) and equivalent ranks at the Directorate of Extension Education.Organised from August 10 to November 27, the training programme aimed to equip defence personnel with technical knowledge and practical skills in agriculture and allied activities, enabling them to explore self-employment and entrepreneurial opportunities as part of their second innings after retirement.Maj Ravi Kumar Singh from Holta Military Station graced the concluding ceremony as the chief guest, while Dr Sonia Sood, Associate Director of Extension Education, was the guest of honour. The chief guest appreciated the university’s initiative to provide skill-oriented training to defence personnel and highlighted the potential of protected cultivation and value addition in creating sustainable livelihood opportunities after retirement.Dr Sonia Sood emphasised the importance of such capacity-building programmes in equipping retiring defence personnel with practical agricultural skills and encouraging them to establish agriculture-based enterprises. She also highlighted the university’s role in facilitating their transition towards productive and self-reliant second careers. Dr Janardan Singh, Director of Extension Education, in his message, congratulated all the participants on successfully completing the training programme and wished them success in their future endeavours.Dr Lav Bhushan, training coordinator, briefed the gathering on the training programme and its objectives. He informed that a total of 40 defence personnel, comprising 28 from the Army, four from the Navy and eight from the Indian Air Force, successfully completed the course.Dr Bhushan further informed that this was the eighth training programme sponsored by the Directorate General of Resettlement (DGR), New Delhi. So far, 223 JCOs and equivalent-rank officers of the Indian Armed Forces have been trained by the university in various agricultural and allied fields, including protected cultivation, dairy farming, goat rearing, poultry farming, beekeeping, agroforestry, mushroom cultivation and value addition of vegetable and horticultural crops.The participating trainees also shared their feedback and expressed appreciation for the training programme. They highlighted its usefulness in enhancing their technical knowledge and practical skills, as well as providing them with opportunities to explore agricultural entrepreneurship and self-employment after retirement.

headline: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
content: DHAKA Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from ‌Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising ​costs eroded the country’s competitive edge, three factory owners said. Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth ⁠of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh’s economy and could extend beyond the current unrest. Hasina has become a ‘thorn’ in Bangladesh-India ties: Minister Humaiun Kobir Hasina has become a ‘thorn’ in Bangladesh-India ties: Minister Humaiun Kobir State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir says New Delhi is beginning to realise the strain the former Prime Minister’s presence in India is causing to bilateral relations Hasina has become a ‘thorn’ in Bangladesh-India ties: Minister Humaiun Kobir storyline 1 Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped ‌make Bangladesh the world’s second apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing. The protests have caused more than $400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more ‌than 80% of Bangladesh’s export earnings and nearly 40% of its manufacturing jobs. Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia also benefit India has emerged ‌as ⁠the biggest beneficiary, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery ⁠reliability, industry leaders said. Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, the smallest rise in four decades. The increase fell well short of workers’ demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, ​said the wage increase was “satisfactory” and that he hoped all ‌workers would resume work from Saturday. Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh’s labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global industry standards. Babul Akhter, a union leader and workers’ representative on the government-appointed wage board, said brands should not use the unrest to justify shifting orders out of Bangladesh. Bangladesh tightens border security ahead of Hasina's planned return; deploys 108 BGB platoons Bangladesh tightens border security ahead of Hasina's planned return; deploys 108 BGB platoons The heightened security comes amid fears that Ms. Hasina's supporters could intensify violence and sabotage in the coming days. Awami League, whose activities have been banned, is promoting a lockdown programme for November 29 and 30 through online platforms, adding to concerns over a possible escalation of tensions Bangladesh tightens border security ahead of Hasina's planned return; deploys 108 BGB platoons storyline 1 He said retailers already factor political instability and labour ‌unrest into sourcing decisions, making such moves “hard to justify” and raising “serious doubts” whether the unrest was more than an excuse. Factory ​owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of ⁠the business. Zara owner Inditex declined to comment on Reuters’ questions, while M&S, H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment. Indian textile shares rallied after the Reuters report, with Gokaldas Exports jumping as much as 11% and Trident gaining about 5%. Other potential beneficiaries, including Welspun Living, ‌KPR Mill and Vardhman Textiles rose around 2% each. M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA, said higher wages, utility and raw-material costs were adding to pressure on manufacturers “at a time when buyers are demanding lower prices and competition from rival sourcing countries is intensifying”. More business at risk Factory owners said the bigger concern was that diversions of business could become permanent. Persistent energy shortages, exacerbated by the Middle East crisis, have added to production disruptions and forced some factories to rely on more expensive alternative power sources. But Chowdhury said that price became secondary when brands were under pressure to meet strict delivery deadlines. India can offer buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and ‌Cambodia can cut lead times by as much as 15 days, Chowdhury said. Rival sourcing hubs can typically complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, ​compared with about 120 days in Bangladesh, he added. The disruptions have also created production backlogs, with manufacturers around Dhaka losing an estimated 20 to 25 production days. Some are considering overtime and costly air freight to meet delivery commitments. Khan ⁠Monirul Alam, managing director of Alps Apparels Group, which mainly supplies European brands, said the unrest was already hitting new business. Analysis | Sheikh Hasina’s return gambit tests Bangladesh’s political fault lines https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/sheikh-hasinas-return-gambit-tests-bangladeshs-political-fault-lines/article71745537.ece “Since November 1, most ⁠of my buyers have stopped placing orders because of the unrest,” Alam said. “They are telling us our orders have been shifted, postponed or cancelled and that they have already found alternative solutions.” Political tensions surrounding former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s possible return ‌to Dhaka from India have added to concerns about further disruption. Industry leaders said restoring stability and uninterrupted production would be critical to retaining international buyers. Chowdhury warned that orders shifted elsewhere during periods of instability might not return even after conditions improved. “The challenge is ​restoring buyers’ confidence before temporary shifts become long-term sourcing decisions,” he said. “Brands have options. They will not wait for us if instability persists.”

headline: Kumari Sachu honoured withcultural excellence award
content: CHENNAI Veteran actress, comedian and dancer Kumari Sachu was honoured with the Dr. Mrs. YGP Award of Cultural Excellence at a ceremony hosted by Bharat Kalachar at Rama Rao Kala Mantap, Karnataka Sangha School in T. Nagar in the city on Friday. Instituted in the name of the late Smt. Kalyani Venkataraman to mark the 101st birth anniversary celebrations of Dr. Mrs. YGP, the award was presented by Rtn. Ravi Venkataraman. The event was graced by veteran actor Sivakumar as the chief guest and Rtn. Shriram Duvvuri, District Governor, Rotary International District 3233, as the guest of honour. Mr. Sivakumar and Kalaimamani Bombay Gnanam, renowned theatre and film writer, director, and producer, felicitated the awardee during the ceremony.

headline: Civil rights group claim that involvement of police in SIR exercise illegal
content: Kolkata Civil rights groups in West Bengal on Friday (November 27, 2026) claimed that police involvement in the State's deleted voter verification process is illegal. They sent letters to the poll body and the Chief Minister, urging them to address the matter immediately and withdraw police presence. Mr. Bose appealed for the use of police to be stopped immediately, as it leads to an intimidating experience for citizens. “The police refused to show any documents or official orders that asked them to conduct this exercise,” Mr. Bose, the chairperson of the W.B. Congress SIR committee said. This concern has been echoed by many, including Opposition leaders and civic groups. There are viral posts on social media where local BJP leaders have asked voters in the tribunals to appear before the police within the next few days. “Those whose names on the voter list are currently under consideration by the tribunal are being advised to contact their respective police stations,” one such poster posted on the social media handle of Naihati BJP MLA Sumitra Chatterjee read. Arindam Niyogi told The Hindu that they have no involvement in the matter. All major Opposition parties, including Mamata-Trinamool, Congress, CPI(M), and other Left parties, have also raised objections to this exercise and questioned its validity. The Association for Protection of Civil Rights has also raised an alarm over the issue.
