headline: Saurav Das tells Piers Morgan show that he was born in Delhi and is Indian
content: TOI Correspondent from London: Cockroach Janta Party co-convener Saurav Das told “Piers Morgan Uncensored” on Thursday that he was born in Delhi and he is not Nepalese.He claimed he did not have a birth certificate as a lot of people from his generation didn’t, but said, “I can prove I was born in Delhi.”He said he and his family have spent their whole lives in India. “My mother’s side of the family might have lineage from Nepal, but so do crores of people in India who have come from different nations because in the past we were one,” Das said.BJP national spokesperson Shazia Ilmi alleged on the YouTube show there were three reported discrepancies in Das’s documents — his father’s name, date of birth and place of birth. Later she said: “I am sure he is Indian.”Das denied that his father “had multiple names” and said his date of birth was Jan 15, 1999. He said the show-cause notice issued to him “only mentions place of birth as discrepancy” and he wants to know “where they got the inputs from”. “Is anyone free in India to raise issues against any person on the basis of which passports can be suspended?” he asked.“As far as I am concerned, all my records are the same.”He said he had flown on his current passport twice to Norway last year, and this year to Thailand, and he was facing these “frivolous allegations” now as the government wanted to stop him from spreading the message of the CJP movement outside India.Ilmi said Saurav had a “delusion of grandeur” that he was a great enemy of the Indian government and that “formidable adversaries of the Modi government routinely travel abroad and criticise him”. “Political activism cannot confer immunity from legitimate document verification,” she said.Das also admitted that he failed his law exam but said he only failed it once, not four times as Ilmi alleged.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Mirwaiz under house arrest after Sheshnag, Vande Mataram criticism; barred from leading Friday prayers
content: SRINAGAR: The J&K administration on Friday placed Hurriyat Conference chairman and Kashmir’s chief cleric, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, under house arrest and barred him from leading Friday prayers at the historic Jamia Masjid in Srinagar.Mirwaiz attributed his latest house arrest to his criticism of alleged construction work near the ecologically fragile Sheshnag Lake and the opposition expressed by the Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama (MMU), an organisation led by him, to the rendition of Vande Mataram at the waqf board function on Monday.“In keeping with the tradition of putting me under house arrest on Fridays, ahead of visiting Jamia Masjid for sermon and prayers, I have again been put under house arrest today. I had anticipated this, as I had raised people’s grave concerns over the disaster waiting to happen in the eco-fragile region of Sheshnag after the viral visuals, and later the recitation of Vande Mataram at the religious function of the waqf board, I would be punished this Friday by being put under house arrest,” Mirwaiz said.“It would do the ruling regime much better if instead of applying pressure on me, it understood the sensitivity and impact these issues have on the people of Jammu & Kashmir, whose welfare it claims to hold dear, and desists from imposing things that cause people hurt and concern,” he said.On Wednesday, several Muslim clerics who attended a J&K Waqf Board function where Vande Mataram was played in full expressed regret and said they had prayed for repentance, as the national song triggered a religious controversy in Kashmir.Monday’s waqf board function was attended by Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju, waqf board chairperson and BJP member Dr Darakhshan Andrabi, Lok Sabha MP Mian Altaf Ahmad and others.All six stanzas of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay’s 1875 poem Vande Mataram were played at the event in accordance with a Union home ministry protocol directive issued earlier this year that mandated the full version at state functions, official events and legislative sessions.On Thursday, MMU, an amalgam of religious organisations and institutions, said there was no legal obligation to play the song at an official function, and criticised the waqf board for playing it at an event organised by an institution entrusted with safeguarding Muslim religious endowments. “Any expression or practice that attributes divinity to the motherland is contrary to the fundamental Islamic belief of Tawheed and is, therefore, un-Islamic and impermissible for Muslims,” MMU had said.PDP president Mehbooba Mufti said she strongly condemns the continued house arrest of Mirwaiz, particularly on Fridays when he is prevented from offering prayers and delivering his sermon at Jamia Masjid.Police have not issued any statement on the issue.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Karnataka government serves show-cause notice to IOCL terminal in Bengaluru over ethanol measurement discrepancies
content: Bengaluru The Karnataka government on Friday served a show-cause notice on Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) over discrepancies in the measurement of ethanol and motor gasoline at its terminal in Devanagonthi, Bengaluru, and directed the oil marketing company (OMC) to submit an explanation within seven days. The action follows inspections initiated by the Department of Legal Metrology, Karnataka, at the terminals of oil marketing companies. Tests of samples from petrol stations in Karnataka by the State government had revealed ethanol blending to be as high as 32% in some cases, Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology Minister Rizwan Arshad claimed earlier this month. This was denied by OMCs and Union Ministers. Mr. Arshad had also written to the Union government seeking display of accurate ethanol blending in petrol at every station. Show-cause notice According to the show-cause notice, officials detected discrepancies in the quantities of ethanol and motor gasoline dispensed through mass flow meters during an inspection at the IOCL terminal on Wednesday (November 25). According to the Minister, the inspection was conducted using the “master proving” test method. At Bay No. 9, officials found that the meter was dispensing 14 litres of ethanol in excess for every 3,000 litres. At the same bay, the quantity of motor gasoline supplied was found to be 4 to 6 litres short for every 3,000 litres. Another mass flow meter at Bay No. 4 was also found to be dispensing an additional three litres of ethanol for every 3,000 litres, the notice stated. Mr. Arshad said that the discrepancies exceeded the permissible limits prescribed under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009, and the rules framed under it. “The inaccuracies in measurement could adversely affect the interests of consumers, distributors and other stakeholders dealing with petroleum products,” he said. The show-cause notice, issued to the Deputy General Manager in charge of the Devanagonthi terminal, has sought a written explanation within seven days of its receipt, warning that failure to submit a satisfactory explanation within the stipulated period could lead to further legal and departmental action against the terminal and the officials responsible. The department has asked IOCL to explain the reasons behind the discrepancies and provide details of the measures taken to ensure the accuracy of the mass flow meters and associated batch control units. It has also sought records of their latest calibration and maintenance, along with details of corrective measures proposed to address the discrepancies. Further, the department has directed IOCL not to use the affected measurement systems for commercial transactions until their accuracy and compliance with prescribed legal standards are verified.

headline: Why Michael Phelps' struggles with mental health became one of the most important parts of his life after
content: Michael Phelps is the most decorated Olympian of all time. Yet the part of his story he talks about most now has nothing to do with a pool. For more than a decade, the swimming great has spoken openly about depression, anxiety and the dark stretch that followed his second DUI arrest in 2014, when he checked himself into an inpatient treatment center. Retired since 2016, Phelps has turned that low point into a mission. Through his partnership with online therapy platform Talkspace, he is pushing men in particular to stop hiding what they feel.Why did Michael Phelps' mental health struggles become so important after his Olympic glory?The trouble began long before 2014. Phelps first dealt with depression after the Athens Games, where he won six gold medals as a teenager. A few months later, at 19, he was arrested for drunk driving for the first time.What made him almost unbeatable in the water also hurt him away from it. Phelps was brilliant at boxing up his feelings, believing that sharing them would hand rivals an edge. Looking back in an Instagram post, he admitted that "a lot of times I wasn't my authentic self."He told TODAY.com, "I was almost ashamed of the things that I was going through and feeling." That shame peaked after his second DUI arrest in 2014. Phelps has described sinking into depression deep enough that he thought about ending his life. He spent time in a treatment facility, and therapy, he says, saved him.That is why this chapter matters so much. Gold medals made Phelps famous. Talking honestly about his worst days made him relatable to millions who will never swim a lap in competition.How is Michael Phelps helping others with mental health today?Phelps retired after the 2016 Rio Olympics, and the drive that carried him to 28 medals now goes into advocacy. His partnership with Talkspace, which links people with therapists online, aims to cut through the stigma that keeps many from asking for help.Men are his main focus, and the numbers explain why. Fortune, citing the National Institute of Mental Health, reported that just 40% of American men with a mental illness received care in the past year. For women, the figure was 52%.Phelps does not pretend he has it all solved. He still has rough days, and he has been clear that the work never really ends. "My depression and anxiety aren't going to just disappear," he told Healthline. Hearing that from the most decorated Olympian ever carries weight. It tells people that struggling is not the same as failing.Now living in Arizona with his wife Nicole and their four children, Phelps leans on them, his friends and his therapist in ways he once would have called weakness. His priorities have shifted. "My number one goal is to try and save a life," he told Fortune.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Nagenthran, Annamalai welcome SC order on Thirupparankundram issue
content: CHENNAI BJP state president Nainar Nagenthran on Friday said Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay should resign, in the light of the observations made by the Supreme Court in the Thirupparankundram issue. In a social media post, Mr. Nagenthran said the apex court suspending the temple’s Board of Trustees and issuing show-cause notices on contempt against the Chief Secretary, DGP, authorities of the HR&CE Department, among others, was proof of the administrative failure of the government headed by Mr. Vijay. The Supreme Court appointing High Court former judges as receivers to administer the temple, was a “befitting reply to the anti-Hindu attitude of the TVK government,” Mr. Nagenthran said. He welcomed the apex court directing the deployment of the CRPF personnel in this issue. “After the strong observations of the Supreme Court, Mr. Joseph Vijay is not fit to continue as the Chief Minister,” he said. We The Leaders founder K. Annamalai said he sincerely hoped the TVK government would desist from any further attempts to defy the court’s orders and stopped “playing with the faith and devotion of countless devotees of Lord Muruga across Tamil Nadu.” In a social media post, Mr. Annamalai said: “We reiterate that the rule of law cannot be subject to the whims of those in power, whether you like it or not. At this juncture, I appeal to all political parties and religious organisations to step back and allow devotees of Lord Muruga, without any political or organisational affiliations, to light the lamp at the deepathoon.”

headline: Civil society groups urge Karnataka Chief Minister to scrutinise SIR deletions ahead of local polls
content: Bengaluru Members of various civil society groups under the banner of the “Anti-SIR alliance” on Friday submitted a memorandum to Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, demanding that the State government reject the final electoral roll published after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and take a clear stand against the exercise, with local body elections approaching. The alliance said the final electoral roll was riddled with errors and demanded that the 2025 electoral roll be restored, subjected to public scrutiny and revised in a voter-friendly manner before being used for local body elections. The alliance also cited the Election Commission’s recent instructions to States conducting SIR to “revisit deleted and left-out voters”, publish booth-wise deletion lists and make efforts to restore those wrongly excluded. It said these directions pointed to serious shortcomings in the SIR. The groups, in their letter, also criticised statements by some Congress Ministers that Karnataka had not lost anything through SIR and could use the revised rolls for local body elections. The alliance said the government should not assess the exercise through the narrow lens of electoral gains or losses. It also pressed for a social audit to establish the legitimacy of deletions made during SIR.

headline: KPSC released a list of 4,697 candidates, who have qualified for the main examination Gazetted Probationary posts
content: Bengaluru The Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) released a shortlist of 4,697 candidates, who have qualified for the main examination for the recruitment of 319 Gazetted Probationary posts (2026-27 batch). These candidates were selected based on the preliminary examination results, following a 1:15 ratio. For the 297 posts under the Residual Parent Cadre (RPC), 4,367 candidates have qualified, while 330 candidates have qualified for the 22 posts under the ‘Kalyana Karnataka Cadre.’ The KPSC has also published the category-wise cut-off marks for the qualified candidates. For the RPC, the cut-off mark for the General Merit (GM) category is 206.5, whereas for the Kalyana Karnataka Cadre, it is 210. Notably, 41 candidates secured the exact same cut-off score of 206.5. A total of 1,47,067 candidates had applied for these positions. Of these, 88,450 candidates appeared for Paper-1, and 87,817 candidates appeared for Paper-2. In the preliminary examination, which consisted of Paper-1 and Paper-2 with a total of 400 marks, the highest score achieved by a candidate was 264.5. The registration numbers, names, marks obtained in Paper-1 and Paper-2, and total marks of all candidates who appeared for both examinations have been published. Based on a 1:15 ratio, a total of 4,785 candidates were expected to qualify for the Main Examination. However, in three specific categories, General (Transgender), Blindness, and Low Vision, the required number of candidates (falling short by 88) could not be found to meet this ratio.

headline: Vijay reviews rainfall situation in T.N., directs steps to ensure drinking water, fodder supply
content: CHENNAI Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Friday held a review meeting with Ministers and senior officials at the Secretariat in Chennai on the impact of rainfall deficit in the State and the preparedness measures to ensure adequate drinking water and fodder for livestock in the ensuing summer. An official release said the Chief Minister held a detailed review of the rainfall situation in the State, water storage in dams and lakes, groundwater levels, and the area under cultivation of agricultural and horticultural crops. Though the State had received 20% less rainfall than normal between June 2026 and November 25, 2026, only 22 districts had recorded deficient rainfall. While the water storage in dams stood at 32.9% of their total capacity, 73% of the lakes under the Water Resources Department had storage levels of 50% or less, the release said. Compared with the corresponding period last year, the area under cultivation of agricultural crops had declined by 18.4% this year. Further, standing crops in several districts had been affected due to deficit rainfall, it said. In view of the prevailing situation, Mr. Vijay has ordered an immediate survey of crop damage in areas where it exceeds 33%. Steps will be taken to provide compensation to eligible farmers in accordance with the relevant rules, the release said. The State government will also conduct special camps and awareness campaigns to ensure that all eligible farmers benefit from the crop insurance scheme. The Chief Minister has directed District Collectors and Agriculture Department officials to ensure that no eligible farmer is left out of the crop insurance scheme. Teams comprising Ministers and senior government officials have been asked to visit districts with deficit rainfall and assess the situation on the ground, including crop damage, farmers’ requirements and essential needs, and to submit detailed reports so that appropriate measures could be taken. Monitoring officers assigned to districts have also been instructed to visit the districts assigned to them, assess the situation in detail, and submit reports to the government, along with recommendations on the measures to be taken, the release said. Mr. Vijay has directed the Municipal Administration and Water Supply, Water Resources, and Rural Development departments to assess drinking water requirements and prepare a comprehensive action plan for uninterrupted drinking water supply in summer. An allocation of ₹13.26 crore has been made from the State Disaster Relief Fund towards fodder production and subsidies. The Animal Husbandry Department, Aavin, and related departments were asked to ensure adequate fodder availability, particularly in districts likely to face fodder shortages, during the period from February 2027 to June 2027.

headline: VCK, MMK flag concerns over SC ruling in Thirupparankundram issue
content: Chennai Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi founder Thol. Thirumavalavan, on Friday sought to know why the Supreme Court did not consider the Tamil Nadu Government’s review petition, but instead, chose to prioritise the “contempt of court” case in the deepathoon issue at Thirupparakundram hill. In a statement, Mr. Thirumavalavan questioned “the urgency and anger”, and asked whether the Supreme Court saw this as a matter of ego. “Is the Supreme Court’s ego more important than social harmony? So many rulings have been left unimplemented, haven’t they? In particular, why is the Supreme Court, which did not get angry about the non-implementation of its ruling on women’s entry into Sabarimala, taking this issue so seriously? The tradition is to light lamps on Karthigai Deepam. Isn’t ordering that a lamp be lit on another day, overriding even that tradition, an assertion of the Supreme Court’s power and ego?” he asked. He further said, “Is the ruling delivered today justice for the people? Or is it an assertion of dominance meant to demonstrate the court’s ultimate authority? Is not handing over Thirupparankundram hill to paramilitary forces an assertion of dominance that crushes the State government’s rights? This is deeply shocking and frightening!” Manithaneya Makkal Katchi president M.H. Jawahirullah urged the Chief Justice of India to intervene and protect the religious rights of all communities and traditional worship practices. He also appealed to the CJI to “take steps to ensure that social harmony and peace continue to prevail in Tamil Nadu”. In a statement, Prof. Jawahirullah said the SC, after directing that the lamp be lit on Saturday at what he described as the “survey pillar”, has also ordered the suspension of the temple’s Board of Trustees, the appointment of retired judges to take charge of its administration, and the handing over of security arrangements on the hill to the Central Reserve Police Force. “This order constitutes a grave encroachment upon the administrative jurisdiction of the State government, the statutory administrative responsibilities of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department, and the State’s authority to maintain law and order,” he said. He further said, “It is distressing that the Supreme Court has lent support to the actions of ‘communal forces’ seeking to exploit this issue for political objectives. The freedom of religion guaranteed by the Constitution is not a right exclusive to one community. It is a fundamental right that must be equally protected for people of all religions.”

headline: J&K gets advocate general after 2 years
content: SRINAGAR: Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri was appointed the advocate general of J&K on Friday, filling a key constitutional post that had remained vacant for two years.Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha approved the appointment of Qadri, who practices at the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh high court.The position had been vacant since CM Omar Abdullah took the oath in Oct 2024 after then-advocate general D C Raina submitted his resignation when the elected govt assumed office.Though Omar wanted Raina to continue in the post, differences emerged with the LG administration over the issue, and an additional advocate general had been running the office for the past two years.A high court lawyer had filed a PIL before the HC over the delay in appointing an advocate general, arguing the prolonged vacancy was detrimental to legal governance in the Union Territory. It also impacted the functioning of the Jammu & Kashmir Advocates Welfare Fund Trustee Committee, of which the advocate general is the ex officio chairperson, the petitioner claimed.On November 5, the J&K administration assured the HC that the appointment process was underway and the post would be filled within a month.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: CRPF arrives in Madurai to secure Thirupparankundram area
content: MADURAI Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel arrived at Thirupparakundram here on Friday night to take security control of the hill and Sri Subramania Swamy Temple, hours after the Supreme Court ordered Central forces to secure the area for lighting the Karthigai deepam at deepathoon on Saturday (November 28, 2026). Contingents of the paramilitary force began moving around the foothill and along the pathways leading to the disputed dheepathoon. The deployment followed a hearing earlier in the day before a Supreme Court Bench, comprising Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi. The court suspended the temple’s Board of Trustees and appointed former Madras High Court Judges S. Vaidyanathan and V. Parthiban as receivers to oversee the temple’s affairs and ensure the ritual is conducted on Saturday without obstruction. The lamp is to be lit at the deepathoon using the flame from the Uchipillaiyar Mandapam, where the customary lighting had taken place earlier in the week. The Central forces have been tasked with guaranteeing the safety of both the temple and the dargah, ensuring that Muslim worshippers retain unobstructed access to the shrine while devotees are permitted to participate in the lamp-lighting ceremony under regulated security. According to officials, the CRPF personel are establishing perimeter checkpoints and securing key vantage points across Thirupparakundram.

headline: Loop in Punjab, Haryana on  ₹1,454-cr funding for HC expansion plan: Centre tells UT
content: Taking up the ₹1,454-crore proposal for expansion of the Punjab and Haryana high court complex, the Centre has directed the Chandigarh administration to share the project details and proposed funding mechanism with the stakeholder governments of Punjab and Haryana to work out cost-sharing.The decision was taken at a meeting between the Union home secretary and the chief secretaries of Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh in New Delhi on November 20.The Chandigarh administration had earlier forwarded the proposal to the Centre, seeking clearance for adding at least 35 courtrooms to the common high court of the two states and Chandigarh to address the acute shortage of courtrooms and mounting space constraints.For nearly three years, various proposals—such as shifting the entire court to Sarangpur or the IT Park area, both on the outskirts of Chandigarh—were deliberated upon, but failed to find consensus, especially with the Bar. Later, a consultant was hired and the current blueprint was drawn up.In the meeting, it was also resolved that the Chandigarh administration may also obtain the high court’s views afresh, and a meeting would be held again with various stakeholders to finalise the future road map.Meanwhile, the ministry of culture and the UT administration will follow up expeditiously with World Heritage Centre, UNESCO, for necessary consultation and approval requirements, it was decided.“The chief secretary, Chandigarh administration, shall share the project proposal with the governments of Punjab and Haryana, inter alia, covering the detailed scope of work, infrastructure requirements, preliminary cost estimates duly vetted by the CPWD and the proposed mechanism for sharing the project expenditure among the concerned stakeholders and seek their views,” the decision taken in the November 20 meeting reads.It is immediately not clear what the views were regarding the expansion proposal and funding pattern between the different stakeholders at the meeting.Why is expansion needed?The need for expansion arises amid a serious infrastructure crunch, acute space shortage and severe parking bottlenecks.Over 10,000 cars and thousands of two-wheelers come to the HC daily as there are 10,000 lawyers and over 3,300 court employees, besides the litigants. Additionally, against a sanctioned strength of 85 judges, the high court currently has courtrooms for only 69.Planned to cater to the court’s infrastructure needs for the next 50-60 years, the expansion project envisages four new blocks spread over 11.42 lakh square feet behind the existing high court building.The structure is part of the Le Corbusier-designed Capitol Complex, which was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2016. The expansion plan also includes additional parking capacity on 11.17 lakh square feet at the Capitol Complex.The advocate general (AG) offices of Punjab and Haryana, judicial record room and old lawyers chambers, among others, built on a 2.07 lakh square feet area, are to be demolished and merged into the extension blocks.The parking will have three floors below the new complex. Only three floors, including the ground floor, can be constructed as the skyline of the heritage building has to be protected. With this, the total parking capacity would go up to 22 lakh square feet, according to the plan prepared by the high court administration and UT.Even if cleared by the Centre, the project will need clearance from UNESCO due to Capitol Complex’s heritage status. The UNESCO arm is likely to take up UT proposal later this month.‘No need to obtain views again’: HC presses for immediate solution On Friday, when the outcome of the meeting was presented before the high court, apprehending further delays, the bench of chief justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra observed that the court’s functioning had been impacted due to lack of space and told the Centre and other stakeholders to take immediate steps so that requisite infrastructure is provided “at the earliest”.“Though this court has a sanctioned strength of 85 judges, the court halls available as of now is much less. Space for Bar offices and parking facilities are all proving to be inadequate. The high court is thus in urgent need of additional infrastructure,” the court lamented during hearing of a public interest litigation (PIL) highlighting infrastructural shortcomings on the court premises.The court also observed that once a proposal had come from the court and the UT administration, there was no need to obtain the views again, an apparent reference to resolution of November 20 meeting.“We are faced with a peculiar situation where the functioning of the court is severely curtailed on account of lack of requisite infrastructure required for the efficient and smooth running of the court,” it said, adding that it expected central government officials dealing with it to examine the issue with the “requisite sensitivity”.Deferring the hearing for December 11, the court at the end requested additional solicitor general of India Satya Pal Jain to personally meet the Union home secretary on the issue.

headline: GITAM opens admissions to 111 programmes for 2027-28
content: VISAKHAPATNAM GITAM Deemed to be University has opened admissions to 111 undergraduate and postgraduate programmes across its three campuses for the 2027-28 academic year, university officials said at a press conference in Visakhapatnam on Friday. Pro Vice-Chancellor Gouthama Rao Yejju said admissions would be based on the GITAM Admission Test (GAT-2027), to be held online in selected cities on March 27, 2027. The last date for applications is March 24. GIMSR Pro Vice-Chancellor Gitanjali Batmanabane, Registrar D. Gunasekaran, Admissions Director M. Jagadeesh, and deans, directors and principals of the university were present. According to the university, candidates with high scores in national and state-level entrance examinations such as JEE, CUET, CLAT, LSAT and the entrance tests of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka are exempt from GAT-2027 and may apply directly. For MBA admissions, the university conducts the GITAM Business Aptitude Test, from which candidates with a valid CAT score are exempt. The university said the four-year Integrated Teacher Education Programme offered by the GITAM School of Education requires candidates to qualify the National Common Entrance Test conducted by the National Testing Agency. The university said merit scholarships, covering up to 100 per cent of tuition fees, would be awarded on the basis of GAT-2027 performance or ranks in recognised national entrance examinations. It also offers need-based aid, sports scholarships and fee waivers for personnel and families of the Indian Armed Forces and CRPF. The “Pathway” scholarship examination will be held in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana to identify academically gifted students from government-run Social Welfare institutions, officials said. EOM

headline: Power Outages, Flood Risks Linger as Storm Leaves East Coast
content: (Bloomberg) -- More than 400,000 homes and businesses along the East Coast are without power after an explosive storm uprooted trees in Queens and Manhattan and inundated commuter rail lines in New Jersey on Thanksgiving Day.The nor’easter system that pummeled New York City and surrounding areas also carried heavy rains as far south as North Carolina. Though the storm is losing power Friday, beaches from Virginia to Maine are still at risk of coastal flooding during high tide, according to the US National Weather Service. “It was not a typical nor’easter,” said Brian Hurley, a meteorologist with the service’s Weather Prediction Center in Maryland. “It’s been a while since we saw one that had such a footprint in terms of power outages, that wasn’t tied to a tropical system.” Strong wind gusts scoured the eastern seaboard, toppling trees and knocking down power lines. Electricity is still out for more than 117,000 customers throughout Pennsylvania, according to PowerOutage.com, with over 85,000 outages in New Jersey and about 42,000 throughout New York State. The remaining outages stretch across Delaware, Maryland and Virginia. Gusty winds and lingering rain discouraged some Black Friday shoppers from waiting in line across the region. But conditions had eased considerably from the peak of the storm. Weather gauges captured gusts of up to 66 miles (106 kilometers) per hour at LaGuardia Airport in New York City Thursday evening. In Manhattan’s Central Park, top winds measured 54 miles per hour. Construction scaffolding collapsed on Central Park West and in the Bronx, according to the city’s emergency management department, while wind-blasted trees crashed through parked cars and at least one home throughout the five boroughs. Storm gusts were too strong to safely fly gigantic balloons in the iconic Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. For the first time in its history, organizers postponed the parade until Saturday morning.(Updates with new power outage numbers, damage reports starting in paragraph 1.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: BJP spreading misinformation over my Rafale remarks: Negi
content: Amid Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) holding protests seeking resignation over his remarks in the Himachal Pradesh assembly concerning the Rafale fighter aircraft, revenue, horticulture and tribal development minister, Jagat Singh Negi, categorically denied having made any statement against the Indian Army and challenged the BJP to point out any such remark in his speech.“Show me where I have spoken against the army. In my statement, there is not a single word against the army. Is mentioning Rafale an insult to the army?,” he asked while speaking to the media in Shimla on Friday.Negi alleged that the BJP had deliberately linked his remarks on the Rafale aircraft with the army to divert attention from the issues he had raised during the assembly proceedings.He said his statement was specifically about the cost of the Rafale aircraft and allegations concerning its pricing, claiming that aircraft which he said were earlier valued at around ₹700 crore were subsequently purchased at approximately ₹2,300 crore.Clarifying his remarks about the aircraft and Pakistan, Negi said he had referred to the Rafale in the context of the controversy over its performance and claims made during political discussions.He said the controversy was deliberately created after his speech, alleging that BJP leaders had attempted to turn his statement into an issue of alleged disrespect towards the armed forces.Negi said that the Leader of the Opposition had intervened in the assembly shortly after his statement on November 18 but had not accused him of insulting the army at that time.He alleged that the controversy was subsequently manufactured as a political strategy after his remarks on the RSS ideology, the BJP’s 12-year tenure and other issues during the assembly debate had put the opposition on the defensive.“The entire controversy was a well-planned conspiracy. They had nothing to counter what I had raised, so the next day they deliberately dragged me into another controversy which was completely far from the truth,” he said.‘BJP delaying implementation of women’s reservation’Negi accused the BJP-led central government of delaying the implementation of women’s reservation and using the proposed delimitation exercise for political gains.Negi questioned the Centre’s decision to convene a special session of Parliament when the monsoon session had not been formally concluded and the winter session was yet to be convened.He questioned the urgency behind holding a special session and said the government should explain why it was not following the regular parliamentary procedure.

headline: Health minister Khader orders private hospitals to display treatment costs at a prominently visible place
content: Shivamogga: Private hospitals must mandatorily display treatment cost at a prominently visible place in the hospital, said health minister UT Khader Friday.The health department will inspect hospitals that have already put up rate charts and use them as a model to enforce the rule across all remaining private hospitals, he added.The minister told reporters in Shivamogga that the govt has already issued clear directives regarding the display of treatment charges.Responding to questions on medicine shortages in govt hospitals, Khader explained that delays in the tender process caused the bottleneck. Since drug manufacturing, quality testing and supply take time after tenders are finalised, distribution is affected.To ensure patients do not suffer, officials have been instructed to procure and supply essential medicines under the Ayushman Bharat Arogya Karnataka scheme, he said, assuring that the department will review the situation to prevent future shortages.Regarding non-availability of anti-snake venom in certain hospitals, the minister clarified that existing rules mandate a minimum stock of 10 vials at primary health centres (PHC), 30 vials at taluk-level hospitals and adequate reserves at district drug warehouses. If any PHC faces a shortage, arrangements must be made to source it immediately from the warehouse.He noted that this was the first time the shortage in Shivamogga had been brought to his attention and promised an immediate inquiry.The state govt is planning to construct a dedicated district hospital. Discussions are currently under way on whether to build it in the taluk housing the medical college or at a central location accessible to residents across the entire district.Drawing attention to the rise of fake doctors in Shivamogga district, Khader said the health department was preparing to crack down on the offenders. Clear instructions have been issued to district health officers, district AYUSH Officers, and taluk health officers to identify and report unqualified practitioners.“Those practising medicine without qualifications must leave the state, or they will face strict legal action,” he warned. He also clarified that Ayurvedic doctors should not be equated with quacks. headline: Karnataka’s class 6 vocational education plan sparks concerns over academic foundations, equity and futur
content: Dharwad: Karnataka’s decision to introduce vocational education in govt schools from class 6 has sparked debate over whether early job-oriented training could come at the expense of academic development, particularly for students from economically weaker backgrounds.The initiative covers electrical work, plumbing, beauty and wellness, agriculture and horticulture. The govt says nearly 40% of students drop out at the SSLC and pre-university levels and struggle to find jobs for lack of vocational skills.Equipping students with employable skills is a legitimate goal, but job-specific training from class 6 raises concerns about their academic foundations. Students need grounding in mathematics, science, languages and social sciences to develop analytical skills and prepare for higher education. Early specialisation could narrow their aspirations before they explore their interests and abilities.The move also raises questions about educational equity. Children from affluent families are likely to receive a broad academic education in private schools and prepare for higher studies, while govt-school students risk being channelled into vocational streams early, limiting their choices.Several organisations, including the AIDSO Dharwad district committee, oppose the initiative. AIDSO says it could divert poor students from mainstream education and create cheap labour for companies under the banner of skill development.Educationist BS Patil says vocational education should begin at the plus-two stage, after SSLC, when students can choose academic or vocational pathways based on their interests and career aspirations.Karnataka has tried a similar approach before. The state offered a two-year, central govt-sponsored job oriented course (JOC) at select pre-university colleges to teach practical skills and promote self-employment. Recognised as equivalent to PUC, it also allowed graduates to pursue arts and commerce degrees.The Congress govt later discontinued the programme after the Centre withdrew funding. It said the course had failed to meet its goal because most students pursued higher studies rather than self-employment.The initiative has also raised questions about conditions attached to the Rs 2,000-crore results-based loan from the Asian Development Bank for the Karnataka Public Schools scheme.Skill development is essential, but tackling dropouts and unemployment requires stronger govt schools, better access to higher education and meaningful vocational pathways after SSLC.Academic education and skill development should complement each other. headline: RBI restores 90% daily CRR requirement for banks as liquidity tightens
content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to restore the minimum 90 per cent daily maintenance of the cash reserve ratio (CRR) by banks, effective December 1, 2026, amid tight financial conditions as system liquidity turned into a deficit and led to the hardening of short-term rates. The daily requirement was increased to 99 per cent with effect from October 16. The reduction will release ₹50,000 crore in the banking system, treasury officials said. “On the basis of an assessment of the current and evolving macroeconomic situation and liquidity conditions, it has been decided to reduce the minimum daily maintenance of the CRR from 99 per cent of the requirement to 90 per cent effective from the fortnight beginning December 1, 2026,” the central bank said. The liquidity deficit in the banking system—as measured by the amount banks borrowed from the RBI’s liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) window—was ₹47,641 crore on Thursday. The weighted average call rate (WACR) is hovering near the upper band of the rate corridor, that is, the marginal standing facility (MSF) rate of 5.75 per cent. The MSF rate is 25 basis points (bps) above the repo rate and the standing facility rate; the lower band of the corridor is at 5.25 per cent, with repo rate at 5.5 per cent. Ideally, the WACR should align with the policy repo rate. At the weekly government bond auction, the RBI accepted less than half the notified amount in one of the four government securities, as investors sought higher yields. The central bank accepted bids worth ₹3,677.495 crore in the 6.20 per cent GS 2029 against the notified ₹9,000 crore, setting the cutoff yield at 6.9960 per cent. There was no devolvement on primary dealers in any of the four securities. Yields on the 10-year government bond hardened 3 bps to settle at 7.27 per cent, tracking rise in crude oil prices. The rupee fell for the second day to settle at 92.99 per dollar against its previous close of 92.44 per dollar. In November so far, the rupee has appreciated over 2 per cent against the dollar. Foreign investors have bought about $16 billion of Indian equities in November, reversing a large part of the outflows seen in the first 10 months of the year. The inflows have helped the rupee outperform most Asian peers even with the dollar index near a two-year high. A revival in demand for artificial intelligence (AI)-heavy markets could now divert some of that money. Oil added to the pressure. Brent crude rose above $96.50 a barrel in Asian trade on supply concerns, bringing back worries about India's import bill. "The rupee's sharp appreciation has brought the rupee into an important support zone," said Amit Pabari, managing director, CR Forex Advisors. He sees the 92.00-92.30 range as strong support, but expects some consolidation and a recovery towards 93.00-93.50 in the coming days. Attention now turns to the RBI’s policy decision next week. The central bank is widely expected to raise rates by 25 bps, though some economists see room for a larger hike, which could support the rupee.

headline: India, EU condemn terrorism, underscore need for lasting peace in Ukraine in key meeting
content: New Delhi, India and the European Union on Friday held a key consultation on foreign policy and security, underscoring the need for "comprehensive, just and lasting peace" in Ukraine in accordance with international law and the principles of the UN Charter.At the 12th round of India-EU Foreign Policy and Security Consultations held in Delhi, both sides also exchanged views on the need to restore freedom of navigation in the Black Sea to "minimise the negative impact" on global food security, the Ministry of External Affairs said.The two sides "unequivocally and strongly condemned terrorism and violent extremism" in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, it said.The meeting was co-chaired by Sibi George, Secretary in the MEA, and Olof Skoog, Deputy Secretary General for Political Affairs at the European External Action Service.Both sides also exchanged views and perspectives on the security and defence cooperation under the India-EU security and defence partnership, including maritime security, defence industry and technology, cyber and hybrid threats, space and counterterrorism, the MEA said in a statement.The two sides appreciated the hosting of the inaugural Security and Defence Dialogue in March in New Delhi, and noted the progress and importance of concluding the India-EU Security of Information Agreement.They agreed to conduct the second edition of the Security and Defence Dialogue next year.The consultations provided an opportunity for both sides to review the "strong momentum" and current state of play in India-EU relations and to discuss ways to further deepen the strategic partnership, in line with the 'Towards 2030: A Joint India-European Union Comprehensive Strategic Agenda' endorsed at the 16th India-EU Summit in January, the MEA said."In the current geopolitical context with multilateralism and international law being challenged, both sides underlined their firm commitment to upholding the UN Charter and the rules and principles it enshrines, in particular those of sovereignty and territorial integrity," it said.Both sides emphasised the importance of an effective multilateral system, with the United Nations at its core. They also exchanged views on important regional and global developments, including in the Indo-Pacific.The two sides underscored the need for "comprehensive, just and lasting peace" in Ukraine in accordance with international law and the principles of the UN Charter.The consultations reaffirmed India and the EU's shared commitment to deepening strategic partnership, strengthening cooperation in addressing common security challenges and promoting regional stability, the ministry said.Both sides emphasised the importance of closer coordination in support of a free, open, peaceful and prosperous Indo-Pacific built on international law and mutual respect for sovereignty, territorial integrity and peaceful resolution of disputes, the statement said."As trusted, predictable and like-minded partners, they reaffirmed their commitment to deepen the India-EU strategic partnership, including through regular high-level exchanges and existing institutional dialogue mechanisms, and to deliver mutually beneficial, concrete and transformative outcomes," it added.The meeting also provided an opportunity to review the preparations for future meetings at leaders' level.It was agreed to hold the next FPSC in Brussels at a mutually convenient date next year.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Horticulture Development Centre to Come Up at Ladowal, Ludhiana, at a Cost of Rs. 7 Crore: Mohinder Bhagat
content: LUDHIANA: Punjab Horticulture, Freedom Fighters and Defence Services Welfare Minister Mr. Mohinder Bhagat today laid the foundation stone of Administrative Block of the Horticulture Development Centre at Ladowal, Ludhiana, to be established at a cost of Rs. 7 crore under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY). He also inaugurated the High-Tech Polyhouse Unit. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Mohinder Bhagat highlighted the importance of horticulture in promoting agricultural diversification, enhancing farmers’ income and generating new employment opportunities in rural areas. He said that the Punjab Government is committed to strengthening horticulture infrastructure and encouraging farmers to adopt modern technologies and cultivate high-value crops. The project includes an administrative complex, a Plant Health Clinic, four high-tech polyhouses, modern machinery and equipment, and a seed storage shed. Of the four high-tech polyhouses, two will be dedicated to raising vegetable seedlings, with an annual production capacity of approximately 40 lakh seedlings. The remaining two will be used for guava nursery production, with an annual capacity of approximately 50,000 plants. The Minister said that these facilities would ensure the availability of quality planting material to farmers, promote scientific cultivation practices and help enhance horticultural productivity as well as farmers’ income. The Plant Health Clinic would also facilitate the scientific identification and effective management of plant diseases, pest attacks and other crop-related problems. On the occasion, Mr.Latif Ahmed, Additional Secretary HorticultHorticulture Department, said that the establishment of the Horticulture Development Centre is a significant step towards strengthening the Department’s institutional and technical infrastructure. He said that the facilities being developed at Ladowal would be effectively utilised to provide farmers with quality planting material, technical guidance and modern horticultural services. Horticulture Director Mr. Manish Kumar apprised the gathering of the initiatives being undertaken by the Department to promote crop diversification, protected cultivation, quality nursery production and modern agricultural technologies. He urged farmers to make maximum use of the facilities being developed by the Department and the expertise of its technical specialists. Mr. Harmel Singh and Mr. Gursharan Singh, Joint Directors of Horticulture; Mr. Dalbir Singh, Deputy Director of Horticulture, Ludhiana; Mr. Vijay Pratap, Assistant Director of Horticulture; Horticulture Development Officers, Project Officer Nikhil Ambish Mehta and departmental staff were also present. More than 150 farmers participated in the programme. A technical session on various horticultural crops was also organised. Subject matter experts from the Department apprised farmers of improved cultivation techniques, crop management, plant protection and modern horticultural practices. The session also provided farmers an opportunity to interact directly with technical experts and receive practical guidance.

headline: Chandigarhs Kalagram comes alive with cultural fervour
content: Punjab Governor and UT Administrator Gulab Chand Kataria today inaugurated the 16th Chandigarh National Crafts Mela at Kalagram by beating the traditional “nagara” (drum).Organised jointly by the UT Department of Cultural Affairs and the North Zone Cultural Centre (NZCC), the 10-day mela will continue till December 6. It brings together 225 artisans and more than 250 folk artistes from 25 states and Union Territories to showcase India’s traditional crafts, folk art, music and dance.This year’s theme, “Chandigarh: Sanskritiyon Ka Sangam”, celebrates the city’s diverse cultural identity and its role as a meeting point of different traditions. Traditional cuisines from various states are also a major attraction.Addressing the gathering, the Administrator described artisans as custodians of India’s cultural heritage, preserving centuries-old traditions and craftsmanship. He said the Government of India had established Zonal Cultural Centres in the 1980s to preserve and promote the country’s rich cultural heritage. The inaugural evening featured choreographed folk dance performances from different parts of the country. The mela will also host Sufi, Punjabi, Haryanvi, Uttarakhandi, Kashmiri and Himachali musical evenings featuring renowned artistes, including Lakhwinder Wadali, R. Nait, Somvir Kathurwal, Aabha Hanjura, Gagan Kokri and Prabh Gill, among others.

headline: Holy Family Hospital opens 150-bed super speciality block in Delhi
content: NEW DELHI Holy Family Hospital in south Delhi on Friday inaugurated a 150-bed super speciality block, expanding its capacity to provide advanced cancer care, organ transplantation and specialised neurological and cardiac services. Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the facility at the hospital premises on Okhla Road. The new block will introduce services in surgical, radiation and medical oncology, haematology-oncology and bone marrow transplantation, nuclear medicine, advanced cardiothoracic and vascular surgery, neurology and neurosurgery, and organ transplantation. The expansion takes the hospital’s total bed capacity from 345 to 495, strengthening its ability to treat patients requiring complex and critical medical interventions. Addressing the gathering, Mr. Radhakrishnan called for cancer institutions across the country, including Holy Family Hospital, to establish a common forum to share expertise, discuss challenges in oncology and work towards making quality cancer treatment more accessible and affordable. The inauguration carried historical significance for the institution. Archbishop Anil J.T. Couto, president of the New Delhi Holy Family Hospital Society, recalled that the foundation stone of the original hospital building was laid in 1953 by the then Vice-President, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. Seventy-three years later, another Vice-President bearing the same surname inaugurated its new super speciality facility. A message from Pope Leo XIV congratulating the hospital was read out by Andrea Francia, Chargé d’Affaires at the Apostolic Nunciature in India. The Pope described the new facility as a manifestation of the Church’s continuing commitment to the healing mission of Jesus Christ. Established in 1953 by the Medical Mission Sisters, Holy Family Hospital is a charitable, non-profit institution managed by the Delhi Catholic Archdiocese. The NABH- and NABL-accredited hospital says the new block will combine advanced medical technology and specialist expertise with its commitment to providing affordable healthcare across socio-economic groups.(EOM)

headline: Beyond the smog: When Delhi’s lingering cough masks a silent killer
content: New Delhi: A persistent cough that refuses to go away, unexplained weight loss or breathlessness that is dismissed as the effect of pollution could sometimes be signs of something far more serious. Lung cancer, often detected at an advanced stage because its early symptoms can be subtle, is emerging as a growing public health concern, particularly in cities like Delhi, where prolonged exposure to polluted air adds to the risk.Over 6,500 lung cancer cases have reportedly been recorded in Delhi’s govt hospitals over the past few years, according to figures obtained through an RTI. While the numbers do not capture the complete burden of the disease or establish how many of these cases are directly linked to pollution, they underline the need for greater awareness and timely diagnosis.Smoking remains the biggest established risk factor, but doctors warn that non-smokers are increasingly part of the concern. Passive smoking, prolonged exposure to PM2.5, occupational pollutants like asbestos and diesel exhaust, indoor pollution and genetic susceptibility can also contribute to the risk.“Pollution is also associated with an increased risk of lung cancer, but this is linked to prolonged exposure rather than exposure over a few days,” said Dr Manoj Kumar Goel, principal director and unit head of pulmonology and sleep medicine at Fortis Memorial Research Institute, Gurgaon.He pointed out that street vendors and people working in poorly ventilated industrial environments, regularly exposed to smoke, dust and toxic gases, are particularly vulnerable.Dr Abhijeet Singh, associate director and unit head, pulmonology, ShardaCare-Healthcity, also flagged air pollution as an emerging risk factor, particularly among women and non-smokers. He said the hospital has observed an increase in respiratory illnesses and highlighted that pollution exposure is not limited to outdoor environments.Dr Ankit Jain, senior consultant, medical oncology, Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals, cautioned against attributing every case to pollution. “Air pollution is a recognised risk factor for lung cancer and is an important public health concern in Delhi-NCR. However, it would be inaccurate to attribute all lung cancer cases in the region to pollution alone. Smoking, occupational exposure, family history and other individual factors must also be considered,” he said.One of the biggest challenges is recognising the symptoms. Dr Parveen Jain, senior consultant and head of oncology at Aakash Healthcare, said lung cancer symptoms are often mistaken for seasonal allergies, pollution or routine respiratory infections.A cough lasting more than three weeks, blood in sputum, unexplained weight loss, persistent chest pain, increasing breathlessness, repeated chest infections, hoarseness and unexplained fatigue are warning signs that warrant medical evaluation. “Coughing up blood is a sign that you need to see a doctor immediately,” Dr Parveen Jain said.Doctors also underscore the problem of late diagnosis. “Unfortunately, the vast majority of patients reach us at a very late stage. In Stages 1 and 2, the disease stays largely silent, often causing nothing more than a mild, intermittent cough that people easily ignore,” said Dr Mandeep Singh Malhotra, chief mentor at Art of Healing Cancer, Gurgaon.He added that some patients lose valuable time receiving symptomatic treatment or being treated for tuberculosis before consulting an oncologist.Dr Amit Upadhyay, senior consultant, medical oncology, PSRI Hospital, said over 70% of lung cancer patients walk in at Stage IV. “In Stages 1 and 2, symptoms are often absent or limited to a mild cough. By the time persistent coughing and other severe symptoms emerge, patients may have self-medicated or been misdiagnosed with conditions like tuberculosis, delaying specialist consultation and diagnosis,” he said.Doctors say low-dose CT (LDCT) screening can help detect lung cancer early in high-risk individuals, particularly those with a significant smoking history. However, Dr Parveen Jain stressed that the screening should be guided by a doctor and should not become a routine test for everyone.The treatment depends on the type and stage of cancer and may include surgery, radiation, chemotherapy, targeted therapy and immunotherapy.Dr Ankit Jain highlighted the importance of biomarker testing, which helps identify genetic changes, such as EGFR mutations and guide treatment choices.Research is also exploring how pollution may trigger cancer development. Arun Asaithambi, PhD, founder and CEO of Katamaran Industries, cited a 2023 ‘Nature’ study showing how PM2.5-induced inflammation can promote tumour development in lung cells carrying cancer-associated mutations.With pollution exposure difficult to eliminate entirely, doctors recommend avoiding tobacco, monitoring air quality, reducing exposure to indoor pollutants and seeking medical attention for persistent respiratory symptoms. headline: Delhi-Bihar bus services on 18 routes after inter-state pact
content: New Delhi: Delhi and Bihar signed a transport agreement Friday to launch regular buses across 18 routes. Chief minister Rekha Gupta noted that this year-round service will ease hometown travel for nearly 20 lakh residents from Bihar and Purvanchal living in the capital.Under the agreement, Delhi’s transport department has issued 216 permits to Bihar for operating buses on the identified routes. The chief minister flagged off the interstate bus service from Maharana Pratap ISBT at Kashmere Gate. Bihar transport minister Damodar Rawat and Delhi transport minister Pankaj Kumar Singh were also present.The services will connect Delhi to 13 cities and regions in Bihar — including Patna, Gaya, Darbhanga, Madhubani, Bhagalpur, Muzaffarpur, Buxar and Purnia — while also covering major hubs in Uttar Pradesh. Key cities like Patna, Gaya and Muzaffarpur will be served by multiple routes.Gupta said the initiative reflected the growing cooperation between the two states. She said the improved connectivity would also benefit students and workers who frequently travel between the two states.Transport minister Pankaj Kumar Singh said the facility would provide relief to passengers who face difficulties getting tickets during festivals such as Chhath, Diwali and Dussehra. The number of buses would be increased according to passenger demand, he added.The deal builds on successful festive special bus operations, which saw 210 corporation and PPP buses run in 2025, followed by 155 buses connecting Bihar with Delhi and other states during Diwali and Chhath this year.To expand services, Bihar State Road Transport Corporation has procured 75 non-AC and 74 AC buses. It also plans to deploy 150 buses through the PPP model. The agreement allocates 12 permits each to Delhi and Bihar on every route, paving the way for organised and regular interstate services.Passing through major Uttar Pradesh transit hubs — including Gorakhpur, Lucknow, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Kanpur, Agra and Noida —the routes will link Delhi to 13 Bihar destinations: Araria, Bihar Sharif, Bhagalpur, Buxar, Darbhanga, East Champaran, Gaya, Kishanganj, Madhubani, Muzaffarpur, Nawada, Patna and Purnia.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. headline: Delhi shuts 23 liquor stores for ‘people’s benefit’, 52 more to close
content: New Delhi: Delhi govt has shut down 23 retail liquor shops across the city over public nuisance, proximity to schools and religious places, and clustering of outlets, and identified another 52 for closure over similar concerns, taking the total number of affected stores to 75.Under Delhi Excise Rules, 2010, liquor vends cannot be opened within 100 metres of a school, college or any recognised institution of higher education, a religious place or a hospital with 50 beds or more. However, the restriction does not apply if the school, religious place or hospital comes up after the liquor vend has been set up.“We have received several complaints from people over the past few months against several liquor stores over public nuisance. Our approach is to balance the availability of quality liquor through authorised outlets while also ensuring that residents do not face any inconvenience,” said an official. “Wherever a vend is found causing nuisance or affecting the neighbourhood, appropriate action is taken.” The closure will not affect the availability of liquor, he claimed.According to a departmental report seen by TOI, another key reason is clustering — multiple vends located in close proximity, ranging from around 200 metres to 700 metres.Five outlets have been flagged over public nuisance and complaints from residents, while four have been identified because of their proximity to schools or temples. Around 10 have been shut for clustering.Delhi has around 700 functional retail outlets, operated by four govt corporations — Delhi Consumer’s Cooperative Wholesale Store (DCCWS), Delhi State Civil Supplies Corporation (DSCSC), Delhi State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (DSIIDC) and Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation (DTTDC).DTTDC has the highest number of affected outlets at 23, including 12 already closed and 11 identified for closure. DSCSC accounts for 19 vends — eight closed and 11 identified, while DSIIDC has 17 identified outlets. DCCWS has 16 affected vends, of which three have been shut and 13 are proposed to be closed.Delhi has nearly 1,600 registered liquor brands. The number has increased from 1,470 in 2023-24 to 1,579 in 2024-25, giving consumers a wider choice across Indian-made foreign liquor, imported spirits, wine and beer.The liquor sale has seen fluctuations in recent years. It stood at 2.3 crore cases, including beer, in 2021-22 and increased to 2.7 crore in 2022-23.
